**Updated by:** Builder — **the identity ruling implemented (Chris, 2026-08-05): FieldScout stores no name for a person**, branch `fix/identity-username-only-v2`. Not a milestone task — a whole-app ruling that lands across the league surface, so it is recorded here. Chris, verbatim: *"we don't need either a display name or a full name. we just need the email, password and unique username."* `handle_new_user` seeded `profiles.display_name` from the OAuth `full_name` claim, so a Google sign-in wrote a REAL NAME into a row that the `profiles` policy "Profiles are viewable by everyone" USING (true) exposes to **anon** — and every identity surface rendered `display_name ?? @username` (Chris saw his own name across the app). **Migration 075** does two things and no more: `handle_new_user`'s profile INSERT becomes `(id, username, avatar_url)` — no name written, the OAuth claim ignored — and `UPDATE profiles SET display_name = NULL` clears the names already stored. **No schema change**: the column is NULLABLE with no default, so once nothing writes it it sits inert, and the migration and the app deploy are order-independent against the live site (this is what sank the earlier PR #96, which renamed the column to `full_name` and called it private — the world-readable policy made that untrue, and neither merge order was safe). The migration body is production's LIVE `handle_new_user` (`pg_get_functiondef`, 2026-08-05) minus the name write — it deliberately does NOT import the 049/050/051 username-contract guards, which were never applied to production and which 073 reverted locally too; restoring them is a real but SEPARATE bug, flagged not smuggled (see D115(3)). The five other functions that read the column (`notify_list_followers`, `create_league`, `seat_league_member_internal`, `get_join_preview`, `draft_actor_name`) are deliberately NOT replaced: each reads through a `COALESCE` onto `username`, so with the column permanently NULL they already resolve to the handle — zero churn, and three of them do not exist in production at all. `ai_personas.display_name` is untouched (PUBLIC parody brand copy carrying the "(AI)" transparency marker — no human behind it, nothing to leak; PR #96's `persona_name` rename is dropped). Spec **v2.9** folds the ruling into §7.2's identity table + render rule, §7.2.1's retained-history line, §12.23's claim-preview comment and §16.4's growth-loop rule. Account settings loses its name field entirely: email, password, avatar and a read-only permanent handle. New vitest `src/lib/identity-render.test.ts` (10): source-level sweep of every surface (the `launch-scope-gates` precedent) — no code reads or writes a name on a profile, no PostgREST select pulls one out of `profiles`, settings offers no name field, no seed/dev script plants one, and 075 makes no `ALTER TABLE`/`RENAME`/`DROP COLUMN` at all. pgTAP 005's R31 slot now asserts the trigger writes **no** name (the strongest form of that guard). **Search narrowed to handle-only matching** — there is nothing else left to match on. D115. ### MP task checklist *(breakdown authored 2026-08-21 and **rewritten the same day to Chris's second ruling** — **awaiting his approval of breakdown PR (this one)**; `MP.*` is takeable only after it merges, and only once ACTIVE-BUILD carries the lane clause — **F102**)*

*(**Why this lane exists — TWO premises were wrong, and the second is the bigger one.** **(1)** §8.8 said since v2.3 that a mock is a rehearsal of one specific league (*"v1 scope: league-attached only"*). Chris: *"a user may run a mock draft without even being 'in a league'."* **Practice is the purpose; a league is optional context.** The failure that told on it was `create_mock_draft`'s seat gate (`092:1233–1241`) refusing his own practice — *"it says i need 11 more people"* — **working exactly as designed and answering the wrong question.** **(2)** This document's first cut then answered the corrected premise by designing a hidden per-user "practice container" — a `leagues` row nobody sees — so a league-less mock could satisfy league-shaped RLS, league-shaped FKs and §8.8 isolation. Chris: *"i didn't think mock drafts were going to add so much complexity … I doubt they are doing any of this inivisible league blah blah blah security container stuff."* **He is right and the reason generalises: mocks were built INSIDE the leagues system and inherited its whole threat model — RLS by membership, isolation, commissioner authority, audit immutability — all of which exists because a real draft has twelve humans with money at stake. A MOCK HAS ONE HUMAN AND ELEVEN BOTS: no adversary, nothing to protect.** The complexity was **inherited, not required**. **The new shape: a mock is STANDALONE, settings from the six base scoring templates plus the spec's own defaults, which the launcher changes at launch.** **D228 (the container) is WITHDRAWN and kept in the record as withdrawn**, with its figures corrected — it priced the alternative at *"50 in-body `is_league_member` sites across 18 files"*; measured against the deployed schema it is **13 calls across 9 live functions, 11 sites across 8 on a mock's path** — roughly 4× too high. **League-attached mocks are DEFERRED, not cancelled** (Chris rates the feature highly), and §6.1 of the breakdown protects them. Spec **v2.16** is the fold.)*

**Sequencing:** MP is a **peer of `AP.*`, `MS.*`, `DR2.*` and `SE.*` and blocks none of them.** **`MP.1` is an investigation and nothing skips it — it decides the storage shape every server task is built on.** `MP.5` may start immediately and in parallel. **TWO hard ordering constraints. (1) `MP.2` before `MP.3` — RULED 2026-08-24 by D234(8), a hard prerequisite and not a preference:** under D234's chosen shape a NULL `league_id` makes `draft_mock_cpu_need`'s `JOIN public.leagues` match nothing and every bot's need term collapse, and no storage decision can defend against it. **(2) THE `MP.6` CHAIN, SPLIT IN THREE 2026-08-24 (D243, answering Q25) AND ORDERED `MP.6` → `MP.6b` → `MP.6c` — route, then write path, then spine.** The order is a rule: **MP.6c's acceptance is a browser drive** (bots acting, pause/resume, the chat posts rendering) and **none of it can run until MP.6b's verbs work league-free**; built the other way it would claim its states from intent (§4 rule 9). **`MP.7`'s leagues-off pin needs `MP.6c`, not `MP.6`** — MP.6 gives the room a URL, MP.7(4) asserts the room LOADS (**R470** / D231(3a)). **`MP.8` is takeable now but SEQUENCED AFTER the 6-chain** (D243(6)): a standalone mock cannot COMPLETE until the room works, and a report verified only against league-attached mocks is the half the lane exists to escape. **`MP.9` has no such dependency.** `MP.10` after the surfaces exist; `MP.11` last. **One cross-lane seam: `MP.4` and `MS.8` both touch the launch form AND the launch RPC — neither forks; whichever lands second composes.** **Recommendation recorded for Chris (not applied — F102):** the **mock track runs AHEAD of the league lanes**, since it is what users are invited to during the 2026 launch while league work waits for demand.

**Release gate:** its **own** flag — `NEXT_PUBLIC_FLAG_MOCK_DRAFTS` / `featureFlags.mockDrafts`, **never `featureFlags.leagues`**. **A RELEASE statement, not code isolation:** the shared draft engine stays shared (and is what makes the standalone mock affordable — 58 live functions / 6,252 lines that name their tables literally). **Independence is a claim about ROUTES as well as components** — `(room)/leagues/layout.tsx:18` redirects every `/app/leagues` URL when the leagues flag is off, mock room included (**R470**). **Launch-facing:** Chris intends to invite users to it, so states and polish are in scope (**§4 rule 14**).

### MS task checklist *(breakdown authored 2026-08-20 — **awaiting Chris's approval of breakdown PR (this one)**; `MS.*` is takeable only after it merges, and only once ACTIVE-BUILD carries the lane clause — **F98**)*

*(**Why this lane exists.** Chris used Mock Draft Mode on 2026-08-20 and ruled that **the launcher of a mock is the commissioner of it**: *"in a mock my assumption was that the solo person is the commish so the user running the mock should be able to make it as fast as possible IMO and pause it if they need to do something."* That overturns the **conclusion** of D103/D110(1) — which closed the whole §8.7 surface on mocks — while keeping its **reasoning** intact: D103 was right that a control on somebody *else's* practice is interference, and right that an unguarded `draft_reset` was a live-proven `leagues` write. What it missed is that launcher and commissioner are the same person in a mock. **§8.8's zero-side-effects rule is not weakened — it becomes the explicit gate on every control**, and which controls can pass it is settled by measurement, not by reading. This survey found **four** controls that fail §8.8 as the code stands, not one: `draft_reset`, the autopick toggle (`set_team_autodraft` writes the real `league_members`), seat reassignment (the league's invite surface), and — **the worst shape, because it is MIS-TARGETED rather than blocked** — `draft_set_order`, whose mock guard is real and never runs because the order PATCH carries no `draft_id` and `patchDraftOrder` resolves the league's REAL draft instead. **Three are excluded; the fourth is FIXED AND ENABLED.** Chris ruled the parity principle after this breakdown's first review — *"if real leagues can a mock league should as well so everyone can simulate their actual draft position or test different ones if they have a choice"* — so **a mock gets whatever a real league gets, not whatever is safe to give it** (**D222**). That reversed an earlier revision's decision to exclude the order control: *"this is unsafe"* is a reason to fix, not to withhold. Two tasks were added — **MS.7** (the service-layer targeting fix) and **MS.8** (choose your slot at launch, **D223**) — and the commissioner **swap** Chris named next is filed as **F101**, real-league scope, explicitly not built here. **Real drafts do not change at all** — D141 + F57 ALIGN stand exactly as ruled, and the carve-out is `is_mock`, never `draft_type`. **Copy is RULED and closed (Chris: "no")** — the tools are present and work; nothing explains them.)*

**Sequencing:** MS is a **peer of `AP.*` and `DR2.*` and blocks neither** — no auction-pacing surface, no room layout. Shared surfaces are this file and the migration/pgTAP band (**093 / 041** at fold time; confirm next-free at task time, D161). **MS must land before `L.C6.1`**, whose gate composes the lane suites by name (F84's obligation, extended).

## 3. Spec questions

*Anything where the spec is ambiguous, silent, or seems wrong. Write it here and STOP rather than improvising — per CLAUDE.md. Move to "Resolved" once Chris answers; the answer should also get folded back into the spec itself as a changelog entry.*

### Open

**Q39 — THE PLAYOFF BRACKET NEEDS FIVE DEFINITIONS THE LAW DOES NOT SUPPLY — AND ONE OF THEM (`total_points` brackets) THE CHAIN CANNOT FINALIZE OR SCORE AS BUILT. ~~OPEN~~ **RULED (A)–(E) by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, one sub-question at a time (the Q30/Q31 shape); B9 clears when the rulings are APPLIED (spec fold-back §11.5/§11.7/§7.3.1 + changelog) and 118 builds.** Filed 2026-09-05 by the halted L.D1.8 Builder (`halt/M4-L.D1.8-playoffs-Q39`). ~~BLOCKS~~ Blocked L.D1.8 and, through it, the rest of the M4 schema lane (L.D1.9 → L.D1.10) — blocker B9. L.D2.1 / L.D3.1 (the data lane) depend only on L.D1.1 and stay takeable; the L.D4.x / L.D5.x surfaces that read the bracket wait.** No migration was written — 118 / 066 stay reserved (heads confirmed 117 / 065 with `ls`). Every silence below was found by reading §11.5 / §7.3.1 / §11.7 / §7.3.7 / E38 against 109 / 110 / 116 / 117 before a line of 118 was authored; the house rule (tasks-M4 §11; the R801 / Q38 precedent — "a definition the spec lacks is a QUESTION, not an annotation") routes them here. Each is one sentence for Chris and one golden for the Builder.
- **(A) A playoff matchup that ends in a two-decimal tie — who advances?** **RULED (a) by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, verbatim: "A."** — the HIGHER SEED advances; the row's `result` stays `'tie'` (E38's letter holds — no hidden precision consulted, no score rewritten; only the ADVANCEMENT reads the seed). Scoped to this sub-question; (B)–(E) remain OPEN. Application: one sentence in §11.5 + one 066 cell with two scores tied at two decimals. ** The spec's only tie rule is E38 (`spec:1996` — "`result = 'tie'`; standings W-L-T and tiebreakers handle ties") plus §11.4's finalization sentence ("a two-decimal tie is a tie"); both are regular-season statements. §11.5's Playoffs bullet (`spec:744`) and §7.3.7 (seeding, "at end of regular season") say nothing about advancement, and a bracket cannot carry a tie forward. As built, 117's `matchup_result_internal` writes `'tie'` on a playoff row exactly as on a regular one (D313(7)(g): playoff rows finalize generically). Options: **(a) the higher seed advances** — ESPN/Yahoo/Sleeper's default; the seed is the regular season's own verdict, so no hidden precision is consulted and E38's letter holds (the row's `result` stays `'tie'`; only the ADVANCEMENT reads the seed); (b) bench points / a stat tiebreak — consults data E38 forbids ("no hidden extra precision"), rejected; (c) the commissioner decides — M6's override; the bracket sits stuck until a human acts, for every league on the same night. **Recommendation: (a)**, one sentence in §11.5; pinned by a bracket cell whose two scores tie at two decimals.
- **(B) `playoff_weeks_per_round = 2` — what decides a two-week matchup?** §7.3.1 (`spec:210`) says only "2 = two-week rounds". A pairing spans two `league_weeks` rows (110:757 writes a row for EVERY plan week, `first .. first + rsw + rounds × wpr − 1`) and 109's uniqueness is per (league, season, week, round_type, side), so the representation is two `matchups` rows of the same pairing, one per week, each finalized on its own with its own E38 `result`. Options: **(a) aggregate** — the higher SUM of the two weeks' scores advances (every incumbent's reading; a week-1 loss can be overturned); (b) best-of-two with (A) breaking 1–1 (no platform does it); (c) the second week alone (absurd). **Recommendation: (a)**, with (A) applied to a tied aggregate; the per-week rows keep their own `result` for the record and `team_week_results` is untouched. Golden: the week-1 loser wins the aggregate and advances. **RULED by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, verbatim: "in a 2 week playoff round the scores are added together and the winner is the team with the most points over both weeks."** Each week's row keeps its own W/L/T; the round's verdict is the two-week SUM. *Orchestrator's reading, offered for confirmation, not assumed: an exactly equal two-week total has no "most" and falls to (A) — the higher seed.* (C)–(E) remain OPEN.
- **(C) `total_points` leagues with `playoff_teams > 0` — §11.7's "H2H brackets from points-seeding" (`spec:778`; task item 3) cannot be FINALIZED or SCORED by the chain as built, and the fix is a per-WEEK mode across three lanes.** The mode is branched per LEAGUE everywhere: 110 writes no `matchups` for the mode (`110:772`); 117's `finalize_matchups` flips `matchups` only under `IF v_mode = 'h2h'` (`117:610`); `week_results_pending_internal` asks `pending_scores` only on the h2h side (`117:250`); `week_results_write_internal`'s `total_points` arm reads no `matchups` at all (`117:425-434` — it flips the worker's rows `is_final`); F241(a)'s door contract and F241(b)'s worker contract (rows in `team_week_results` only for a `total_points` league; R800: nothing writes them today) know no playoff arm. A bracket 118 writes for such a league would stay `live` forever. Options: **(a) per-week mode** — a playoff week of a `total_points` league IS an h2h week: 118 replaces 117's three helpers + `finalize_matchups` (against 117's file text, D137) to branch on "`playoff` rows exist for this week" rather than on `schedule_mode`, and the ruling's application files two F-rows — L.D1.9's door scores those rows, L.D2.2's worker writes matchup scores for them; `league_standings` is unchanged (E64's skip is the regular season's). **(b) narrow v1** — `total_points` + `playoff_teams > 0` refuses at creation/edit (`validateLeagueSettings` + the 060/105 SQL checks) and the shrink chain writes 0; a `total_points` league's only playoff is §11.7's "final-week points race" (the v1.x shape the paragraph says it replaced — but the three lanes stay untouched and the bracket for the mode returns as one task when a cohort league asks). (c) write the bracket and leave finalization to a later task — a bracket nobody can finish, rejected. **Recommendation: (b) for the 2026 cohort with (a) recorded as the return path** — the cohort's feedback focus is auction + custom scoring (CLAUDE.md Active Builds), the local dev restore holds 0 leagues of any mode (measured 2026-09-05 — hosted not queried), and (a) is three lanes of contract for the mode §11.7 itself calls the alternative. Nothing says WHEN `complete` happens, or — for an h2h league at 0 — whether "points-only" means the PF leader or `league_standings` rank 1 (Win % first). Options: **(a) rank 1 of `league_standings` at the last regular-season week's finalization, both modes** (§7.3.7: "exactly one ranking rule in the product"; in `total_points` the chain is PF-first so the readings coincide); (b) the PF leader regardless of mode (the literal "points-only" — an h2h league's champion may then disagree with its own standings table). **Recommendation: (a)**; `complete` + the champion land in the transaction that finds the last regular-season week `final`. **RULED (a) by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, verbatim: "a"** — with `playoff_teams = 0` (and, by (C), every `total_points` league) the champion is **standings rank 1 through the FULL tiebreaker chain** (`league_standings`, 117 — record, PF, H2H, PA, coin flip; for `total_points` the chain's own E64 skip makes this the points leader), and the league flips `in_season → complete` **at the instant the last regular-season week goes `final`** (`finalize_matchups`, via 110's F4 guard). Application: one sentence in §11.5, `leagues.champion_team_id` written at that flip, one 066 golden where rank 1 and the points leader DIFFER (an H2H league with playoffs off). (E) remains OPEN.
- **(E) The trigger instant — the task text (tasks-M4 L.D1.8 item 1: "when `league_week_advance` OPENS `playoff_start_week`: seed the bracket from `league_standings`") is unsatisfiable on the calendar as seeded.** `league_standings` reads `is_final` regular-season rows only (`117:1061`; §11.5 "never reads a provisional row"); a week opens at `nfl_weeks.starts_at` (Wed 00:00 ET) and the previous week finalizes at its `correction_window_ends_at` (Thu 06:00 ET — §23.4) — measured on the stack's 2026 rows: week 15 opens `2026-12-16 05:00Z`, week 14's window closes `2026-12-17 11:00Z`, **30 hours later**. At the open instant the standings are one week short (`weeks_final = rsw − 1`) and a bracket seeded then is wrong by construction. Options: **(a) seed when the LAST regular-season week goes `final`** — the hourly advance job (`:00`, after finalize's `:05`) writes round 1 and flips `in_season → playoffs` in ONE transaction the first run it finds the last regular week `final` and no `playoff` rows; round r+1 the same way once round r's weeks are all `final`; the champion + `complete` once the final round's weeks are `final`. The playoff week's `league_weeks` row still opens on its own boundary (auto-carry, the tick's locks and the door's `live` rows unaffected — the round's rows are inserted `live` when the week already is), and a late finalization (F238 / Q37) is a bracket NOT YET written, named hourly (`bracket_waiting` + the reason) — never one seeded from a provisional table. (c) seed inside `finalize_matchups` — immediate, but 117's text for a consequence D313(7)(g) / D314(6) assigned to L.D1.8's advance replacement. **Recommendation: (a)** — a mechanics ruling filed here only because it contradicts the task text's letter; tasks-M4 L.D1.8 item 1 is amended at application. **RULED by Chris 2026-09-07, in-session, verbatim: "i would build the playoff bracket immediately and then rebuild it after the final stat correction is made."** — a PROVISIONAL bracket the moment the playoff week opens, built from standings that INCLUDE the just-played regular-season week (its games are over and scored; its rows are `correction_window`, not yet `final`), then a REBUILD from the final standings when that week's correction window closes (Thursday 06:00 ET — before any playoff kickoff). *Orchestrator's reading, offered for confirmation, not assumed:* (i) if a correction moves a seed the pairings change and the playoff `matchups` rows are rewritten; saved lineups survive (keyed by team-week, not opponent); (ii) each later round is provisional when the prior round's games end and final when its corrections close; (iii) this REQUIRES standings that count a not-yet-final week — the projected/provisional arm L.D5.3 deferred as F253(a) — which now rides L.D1.8 (a 117 replacement or a `p_include_correction_window` argument) rather than waiting. **Q37 — A GAME THAT IS CANCELLED (never `final`, never moved to a later week) HOLDS EVERY LEAGUE WEEK FOREVER — AND FOR NFL WEEK 18 NOTHING CAN EVER RELEASE IT. OPEN, filed 2026-09-05 by the orchestrator from the #258 final re-review (R797). Ledger F243. BLOCKS NOTHING in M4** — the code posture is §23.2's (never advance on partial data) and it is named hourly, not silent; the escape today is an operator edit of `nfl_games` (M6's override reopens WEEKS, not games). The gap is vocabulary: the spec has no `cancelled` game state (its only `cancelled` is on claims/trades), `nfl_games.status` is an unconstrained `TEXT DEFAULT 'scheduled'` (001:92), and E43 defines "out of the week" only as a kickoff moving past a later `nfl_weeks.starts_at` — which week 18 has no row after. Demonstrated rolled-back by the reviewer: week 18 with one `final` + one `postponed` game reads `open 1, all_final false` whether the kickoff is in-week or moved to March. A league CAN reach NFL week 18 (`playoff_start_week` ≤ 16 + three rounds).
- **(a) E43-with-zero:** ingestion writes `status = 'cancelled'`; the gate treats a cancelled game as "left the week" and finalizes without it, its players scoring 0 (their locks release, E43's lock half). The NFL's own 2022 Bills–Bengals precedent (the game was cancelled, not made up, and every platform scored it as a no-play). **Recommendation.**
- **(b) Commissioner act only:** no new state; a cancelled game stays `open` and the commissioner reopens/force-finalizes the week through M6's audited override. Honest but manual for every league in the app on the same night.
- **(c) Both:** (a) as the automatic rule, (b) as the escape when ingestion is late. Cheapest to build on top of (a).
The owner is L.D2.1's ingestion for the status vocabulary + a one-line E43 erratum; the code in 116 needs one more arm. Answerable from this file alone.

**Q34 — RULED (Chris, 2026-09-05, in-session via the orchestrator — the C34/C41 precedent). Two rulings, recorded verbatim and scoped as given.**

**Q34(A) — RULED (a), ERRATUM.** *`lineup_lock = first_game_of_week` is retired; `per_player_kickoff` becomes the only lineup lock. A player's lineup slot locks at his own kickoff — a whole-week freeze triggered by the league's first game is not a real fantasy convention and no platform implements it.* Chris's own words, given in the context of Q34(A) and **explicitly scoped to that question by him** (do NOT record them as a general law — he corrected an over-reading): *"players lock by their own kickoff not by anything else. there is no league or team wide locking."* and, when told the mode's provenance: *"there is no such thing as 'first game of the week' locking anything. that's not a thing."* **APPLIED on the L.D1.5b PR** (`feat/M4-L.D1.5b-retire-first-game-of-week`, migration 114 + pgTAP 062, spec v2.16.20, D311; F230 ✅). Provenance (verified 2026-09-05 by a seven-reader investigation with adversarial fact-checks — D311(2)): no reason for the mode was ever recorded; the identifier entered in the spec's creation commit `a7ff30a` (2026-07-02) and was untouched for 62 days until 112 built it; no changelog entry, decision row or ruling discusses it across 82 changelog entries; sole provenance the competitor-parity cell at App A.1; every platform checked (ESPN, Yahoo, Sleeper, NFL, CBS, MFL, Fleaflicker) locks per player at his own kickoff, none at the week's first game.

**Q34(B) — RULED. Verbatim:** *"once a player has kicked off for that weeks games they are locked until all players go to waivers"* — amended in the same breath: *"or free agency depending on league settings"* — and then made precise: *"players unlock after the last game has finished for the week. usually midnight PST Monday."* **The orchestrator's reading (recorded beneath the verbatim, not as the ruling):** the drop lock binds on the player's own kickoff and is **not** defeated by `player_game_lock`; the release is the week's **last game finishing** — `nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at` (migration 039, already written by L.D2.1's ingestion at the all-final instant, read by NOTHING today) — not `correction_window_ends_at`, which 113 currently reads and which is a scoring boundary; NULL `last_game_ends_at` means "the week isn't over, still locked" and must not raise. What a dropped player becomes (waivers vs FA) stays the existing `free_agency` / `fa_hold_hours` machinery. **Task filed, NOT built in this PR: L.D1.5c** (§2; tasks-M4 §6 — sequenced before L.D1.6). **APPLIED 2026-09-05 — L.D1.5c, migration 115 + pgTAP 063, spec v2.16.21 (D312): both gates unconditional, the release `nfl_weeks.last_game_ends_at`, NULL = locked without a raise — the orchestrator's reading above was verified against 039 / 113 / `ingest-week.ts:288` and built as read; its one stated consequence (a past week whose stamp is never written keeps binding) is F238.** ~~**Open sub-question: Q35** (above) — whether `player_game_lock` survives for the ADD half.~~ **[Q35 RULED (a) 2026-09-05 — the setting retires entirely, applied by L.D1.5c — recorded at `5b6b55f`, R780 struck the leftovers.]**

**Q34 — THE `first_game_of_week` LOCK MODE DOES NOT FIT THE PLAYER-LEVEL MODEL CHRIS RULED IN Q32, AND THE SAME RULING'S "OFF" CASE GIVES A MANAGER A DO-OVER ON A PLAYED SLOT — TWO PRODUCT CALLS, ONE ROW. ~~OPEN~~ RULED above (2026-09-05: (A)(a) applied by L.D1.5b; (B) → L.D1.5c + Q35), filed 2026-09-03 by the L.D1.5 fix-round Builder on PR #254 (`feat/M4-L.D1.5-pool-add-drop`) from the re-reviewer's R762 (the missing F-row) and R759 (the missing consequence). BLOCKS NOTHING TODAY** — 113 ships the settings' letter unchanged and both behaviours are pinned; the ledger row is **F230**, discharged by Chris or by an Architect docs task **before L.D1.6 renders the mode**.

**(A) `first_game_of_week` — erratum or Q30-shape cut?** Q32's amendment is verbatim: *"there really isn't a such thing as a 'lineup locking' players lock and once a player has locked because their game has started they can't be moved."* §7.3.6's `first_game_of_week` says the opposite — the WHOLE lineup freezes at the week's first kickoff, so a Monday-night bench player cannot be moved on Sunday morning, which is exactly the case the ruling's own example says must work. 112 ships the mode (060 pins it), 113 does not read it for droppability, and 061 §H1 carries its one composition cell. **Nothing was cut or altered in this PR** — the mode is untouched pending this answer.
- **(a) ERRATUM — retire the mode, `per_player_kickoff` becomes the only `lineup_lock`.** Matches the ruling exactly. Cost: a settings-column migration + the §7.3.6/§11.2 rewrite + 060/061's mode-specific cells re-cut; any league already created with it is migrated (none exist — the cohort has no league on it). **The reviewer's and this Builder's recommendation** if Chris confirms the amendment is meant to be the whole model.
- **(b) Q30-SHAPE CUT — keep the column, pin the select to one option.** The divisions precedent (Q30(d)): the mode stays in the catalog, the UI shows one choice, §7.3.6 is marked inert for v1, and 112's code path survives untouched for a later revisit. Cheapest, reversible, and it needs no migration.
- **(c) KEEP BOTH MODES and treat Q32's amendment as scoped to `per_player_kickoff`.** Honest only if Chris actually wants a whole-week freeze available; it leaves the spec self-contradictory for anyone reading §7.3.6 beside §13.1.

**(B) Should the player-level drop lock bind REGARDLESS of `player_game_lock`?** With the toggle OFF (a commissioner setting, `settings-panel.tsx:961`) and the DEFAULT `per_player_kickoff`, the shipped verb does this — measured, pinned in 061 §H3: a manager drops a starter whose game has already been PLAYED, the slot clears, and the very next `set_lineup` re-seats it with a player who has not kicked off. So the team loses the played player's points *and* chooses again for that slot after seeing his result. §7.3.4 calls this config "lax incumbent behavior" — but incumbents keep the played player's points in the locked slot (that is E34); here the points are lost and the slot is re-opened, which no incumbent does.
- **(a) MAKE THE DROP LOCK UNCONDITIONAL** — one clause in 113 (`IF v_game_lock AND (v_drop_lock ->> 'locked')` → drop the `v_game_lock AND`), plus the §7.3.4 row's "off" sentence and one 061 pair. `player_game_lock` then governs ADDS only. Never-weaken direction; kills the do-over. **This Builder's recommendation** — the amendment ("once a player has locked … they can't be moved") reads as a statement about players, not about a setting.
- **(b) LEAVE IT AS THE SETTING'S LETTER (what ships today)** — "off reproduces lax incumbent behavior" is §7.3.4's own sentence, the default is ON, and the cohort's leagues use the default. Now disclosed in spec §13.1 (v2.16.19) and pinned, so nobody is surprised by it.
- **(c) MAKE THE OFF CASE MATCH E34 INSTEAD** — keep the drop legal but freeze the emptied slot for the week (a 112 reservation). Restores the incumbent shape, but it re-introduces exactly the phantom-slot machinery Q32 removed, so it is the most expensive of the three and the reviewer's R753 argument applies to it again.

**Recommendation: (A)(a) or (A)(b) — whichever matches Chris's intent, both are cheap — and (B)(a).** Nothing is built on this answer until it exists; the fix round took R759's fixable half (the missing 061 cell + the record correction) and left the clause alone, per the standing rule that a product semantic is never Builder-decided.

**Q32 — RULED (Chris, 2026-09-03, in-session via the orchestrator — the C34/C41 precedent). Verbatim: *"a user can drop a player as long as that player hasn't locked. for example, if its mid day sunday and all the users starters are locked due to games starting but they have a player on their Bench that doesn't play until Monday night, that player can be dropped."* AMENDMENT, verbatim: *"there really isn't a such thing as a 'lineup locking' players lock and once a player has locked because their game has started they can't be moved. so if they are on the bench they are stuck on the bench, if they are in the lineup they are stuck in the lineup."*** **Applied on PR #254 (the Q10-application shape): the lock model is PLAYER-LEVEL — a player locks at his own kickoff (until the week clears, E32's window) and then cannot move in ANY direction (not bench→lineup, not lineup→bench, not into another slot, not dropped); a player whose game has not started moves and drops freely regardless of what else is locked. For 113: a drop is refused iff the player's OWN game has kicked off (E32, both settings' letter); the `kept_in_locked_lineup` phantom branch is REMOVED (a droppable player has not played — nothing to keep); a dropped player's `slot_map` entry is ALWAYS cleared; E34 stays M5's `bench_lock`-off claim-processing path. For 112's merged `set_lineup`: `per_player_kickoff` already IS the player-level model (a locked slot's player never moves — 060 E5; a kicked-off BENCH player cannot enter a slot — 060 E4, re-pinned in 061 F6 as the composition after a drop), so NO 112 change was needed. The `first_game_of_week` mode (§7.3.6) does not fit the model — NOT cut or altered here (112's semantics untouched, no new mode-specific pins beyond those already passing); its fate is pending Chris — **now a filed question, Q34, with its own ledger row F230** (R762: a hand-off with a named actor and no F-row is itself a finding, §6's rule). Under `per_player_kickoff` (the DEFAULT) the next `set_lineup` RE-SEATS the emptied slot with a player whose own kickoff is ahead — 061 §H3 pins the refuse-then-accept pair on a new lax × per_player_kickoff league.** The ruling was given for the on-by-default case; whether the lock should bind drops regardless of the toggle is **Q34/F230**, Chris's call. **Q32 — DOES THE LINEUP LOCK (§11.2) BLOCK DROPPING A PLAYER WHO SITS IN A LOCKED SLOT OF THE CURRENT WEEK? — ~~OPEN~~ RULED above, filed 2026-09-02 by the L.D1.5 Builder on PR #254 (`feat/M4-L.D1.5-pool-add-drop`) from the reviewer's BLOCKER R753. ~~BLOCKS L.D1.5's merge and, through it, the M4 schema lane (L.D1.6 → L.D1.10) — blocker B8.~~**

**The premise, quoted so it can be checked.** §7.3.4 `player_game_lock`: *"a rostered player locks for drops at their kickoff, until the week clears … off reproduces lax incumbent behavior."* §13.1: *"with `player_game_lock` on, a player cannot be added or dropped from their kickoff until the week's correction window closes … Both settings off reproduce incumbent-lax behavior."* §11.2: *"Locked slots are read-only to managers."* E34: *"Player dropped mid-week after starting (bench_lock off, incumbent-lax config) → The locked starter's stats still count for the dropping team's matchup that week; the player enters waivers; edge documented in UI copy."* §7.3.4 `bench_lock`: *"A waiver claim whose drop player has already played this week fails at processing."* tasks-M4 §4 rule 9: *"Dropping a player who is a locked STARTER (§11.2) — decide from the spec text whether the lineup lock also blocks the drop, cite it, pin it; if the spec is silent, STOP and file."*

**What 113 built (D309(3)) and what the reviewer measured (R753).** The Builder read E34 as the general consequence of dropping a locked starter and built: the lineup lock does NOT block a drop — only E32 does — and a dropped player whose slot is LOCKED at the instant is KEPT in `team_lineups.slot_map` (`kept_in_locked_lineup`) so his stats count for the dropping team. The reviewer measured a §11.2 bypass BY COMPOSITION: under `lineup_lock = per_player_kickoff` + `player_game_lock = false`, a manager drops a locked starter (kept), and the very next `set_lineup` re-seats that locked slot with an unstarted bench player, because 112 skips a stored player who is no longer rostered (112:894 *"dropped since (113) — nothing to lock"*) — evidence: `set_lineup` moving QB2 into qb:0 while QB1 rostered → refused "slot qb:0 is locked"; drop QB1 → `kept_in_locked_lineup: true`; `set_lineup` re-seating qb:0 with QB2 → ACCEPTED. That destroys the very E34 guarantee the keep exists for (the stored starters no longer carry him; F227(b)'s fan-out would score the replacement). And E34's own scenario names **`bench_lock` off** — a WAIVER-CLAIM processing setting (M5's path) — not the manager's direct drop, so the text the reading leaned on is narrower than the reading. The spec is therefore SILENT on the direct-drop × lineup-lock interplay — rule 9's STOP condition, applied late.

**Options.**
- **(i) The lineup lock blocks the drop** — `roster_add_drop` refuses dropping a player who sits in a LOCKED slot of the current week (per_player_kickoff: his stored slot's kickoff has passed; first_game_of_week: the week's first kickoff has passed), naming the slot and the instant; E34 stays exactly what its trigger says — M5's `bench_lock`-off claim-processing path — and the `kept_in_locked_lineup` branch is removed. Never-weaken direction (refuse more); no phantom, no double-count edge in M4; one refusal + its one-unit twin in 061; no 112 change. **The reviewer's recommendation and this Builder's.**
- **(ii) 112 treats a kept phantom's slot as read-only** — the keep stays; `set_lineup` reserves a locked slot whose stored occupant is no longer rostered (a submit may omit the key, the canonical map re-inserts it, the fit reserves the slot); a 060 phantom cell + a 061 composition cell; F227(b)'s fan-out duty stands. Preserves the lax-league "his stats still count" reading at the cost of a phantom that every later surface (L.D2.2 scoring, L.D5.1 editor, L.D1.6 auto-carry) must understand.
- **(iii) Lineup lock blocks the drop only when `player_game_lock` is ON** — rejected by both parties: under lax + per_player the same bypass remains, and it invents a coupling neither table prints.

**Recommendation: (i).** It matches §11.2's letter ("locked slots are read-only"), keeps E34 in the scope its trigger names, and removes the composition hole without touching 112. If Chris prefers (ii), the resume builds the 112 reservation and both cells. Either way: a 061 composition cell, a 060 phantom (or refusal) cell, and the rewording of spec §13.1 (v2.16.17's "lineup interplay" sentence — marked PENDING now), D309(3), F224(i), F227(b).

**Q33 — `free_agency = continuous`: IS A LAPSED `waivers_until` FCFS-ADDABLE, OR CLAIM-ONLY FOR A PROCESSOR THAT DOES NOT EXIST UNTIL M5? — ~~OPEN~~ RULED above, filed 2026-09-02 by the L.D1.5 Builder on PR #254 from the reviewer's should-fix R756. ~~Held with Q32 under blocker B8.~~**

**The premise, quoted.** §7.3.4 row: *"`free_agency` | `immediate_after_waivers` | immediate / continuous | Unclaimed players become FCFS."* — the row's ONLY note. §13.1: *"Managers add an unowned player (FCFS after waivers clear)."* D294: *"a lapsed `waivers_until` is FCFS-addable per `free_agency` — state evaluated at read, no sweeper needed in M4."* tasks-M4 §1: waivers/FAAB claim PROCESSING is M5's.

The reviewer's objection: that is a Builder-decided PRODUCT semantic written into the spec — §7.3.4's only note says unclaimed players become FCFS, and no claim processor exists until M5, so in a `continuous` league every dropped player is unaddable by everyone for the rest of M4 (a stranding, not a lock). The STOP rule was not applied.

**Options.**

- **(c) Cut `continuous` from v1** — pin the select to one option (the Q30 shape) until M5 defines it.

**Recommendation: (a).** It is the spec's letter today, it cannot strand a test-cohort league, and M5 — the first task that can give `continuous` a meaning — decides its meaning with the processor in hand. Fold-back: the §7.3.4 note gains "(M4: FCFS at the lapse under both values; M5 defines `continuous`)" and v2.16.17's `free_agency` sentence (marked PENDING now) is rewritten; D309(4) and F227(a) follow.
