**Q30 — TEAM→DIVISION MEMBERSHIP HAS NO DATA MODEL, SO "DIVISIONS 2×" CANNOT BE BUILT AS WRITTEN — ~~OPEN~~ RULED above, filed 2026-09-02 by the halted L.D1.2 Builder (`halt/M4-L.D1.2-schedule-engine-Q30`). ~~BLOCKS L.D1.2 and, through it, the whole M4 schema lane (L.D1.3 → L.D1.10) — blocker B7.~~ L.D2.1 and L.D3.1 depend only on L.D1.1 and stay takeable.**

**The premise, quoted so it can be checked.** tasks-M4 §6 L.D1.2 item 2: *"`league_generate_schedule` per D289: … **divisions-2×-first**; …"*; item 4: pgTAP 058 pins *"division-2× when weeks permit + the validator's report when they don't"* at **every** v1 size. D289 prices the engine on a *"divisions-2× preference"*; D297 orders standings by *"division record"* with *"division grouping"*; D299's gate matrix runs *"divisions 1/2"*; spec §11.7 *(Generation)*: *"**Divisions (if 2):** intra-division pairings are scheduled twice before any pairing repeats cross-division … weeks permitting; the validator reports if the week count can't satisfy it"* (spec:756); §7.3.7 chain entry (5) *"Division record (if divisions)"* (spec:406); §16 renders *"division tags"* on the schedule view and *"standings grouped w/ division tags"* (spec:1734, 1843).

**The measurement: the COUNT of divisions exists everywhere; the MEMBERSHIP exists nowhere.** (1) The spec's §12 data model prints no team→division column or settings field: `grep -n division spec-redraft-leagues.md` hits lines 206, 406, 445, 734, 742, 756, 820, 1734, 1769, 1828, 1843, 2521 — every one is a setting row, an invariant, a UI note or a changelog line; **none is inside a DDL block** (§12.1's `settings` comment at :820 lists `divisions` as long-tail CONFIG, i.e. the count). (2) The live stack agrees: `select table_name||'.'||column_name from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and column_name ilike '%division%'` → **0 rows**; `teams` (001, never ALTERed for it) carries no such column; migrations 001–109 mention "division" exactly once (091:266, a NUMERIC division). (3) The code agrees: `league-settings.ts:326` carries `divisions: z.number().int().min(1).max(2).default(1)` and the settings panel renders a 1/2 select (`settings-panel.tsx:696–704`); the only other hits are the tiebreaker LABEL (`settings-panel.tsx:1221`), the round-trip fixture's `divisions: 2`, and NFL-team pages. **No RPC, route, hook, or UI assigns a team to a division**, and no fixture anywhere has ever needed one. (4) So `divisions = 2` is a number a commissioner can set today whose consequence — which four of your eight teams are "your division" — is defined by nothing. The engine cannot schedule intra-division pairings twice without knowing the pairs; standings (L.D1.7) cannot group; the §7.3.7 chain's entry (5) has no record to compute; L.D5.2/5.3 have nothing to tag.

**Why this is a spec question and not a Builder-finalized field shape (D60's class).** D60 finalized SHAPES of fields the spec NAMED (`waiver_process_time`, `stat_correction_window`). Here the spec names no field: inventing one means choosing (i) a storage home (a `teams` column vs a settings-JSONB map of team uuids vs a new table), (ii) WHO assigns membership and WHEN (commissioner UI pre-draft; engine auto-split at `in_season` entry; either), (iii) what an uneven/partial assignment does at generation (refuse vs auto-complete), and (iv) whether Remix may re-split — each product-visible on the standings and schedule surfaces. A halt done properly is the cheap moment: nothing of the engine is written yet (the Q7/Q9 precedent).

**Options.**
**(a) Column + commissioner assignment, engine REFUSES when unassigned.** `ALTER TABLE teams ADD COLUMN division SMALLINT CHECK (division BETWEEN 1 AND 2)` (NULL = unassigned) in 110; a commissioner "assign divisions" arm on the settings/schedule surface (a NEW UI+RPC task — not in tasks-M4 §6); `league_generate_schedule` and `draft_start` refuse loudly when `divisions = 2` and the assignment is not an even split. Honest and explicit; costs a task the breakdown does not have, and a cohort league that never visits the control cannot draft.
**(b) Column + engine AUTO-SPLIT when unassigned (recommended).** Same column; at `in_season` entry, when `divisions = 2` and every team's `division` is NULL, the engine splits the SEEDED permutation into halves (first half → 1, second → 2 — deterministic per `schedule_seed`, auditable exactly like the schedule, pinned) and **writes `teams.division`** so standings, seeding, tiebreakers and UI read ONE stored truth; an uneven or partial assignment (some NULL, or 5/3) REFUSES by name; Remix regenerates the schedule AROUND the stored assignment and never re-splits (a division is a standings fact, not a schedule fact). A commissioner "assign/rename divisions" control is filed as a follow-on UI task (rides L.D5.3's schedule/remix surface) — the cohort gets divisions with zero new UI, and the control, when it lands, edits the same column.
**(c) Settings-JSONB map.** `leagues.settings.division_assignments: { <team_id>: 1|2 }` through the existing settings PATCH path. No schema change, but team uuids inside a settings blob (no referential integrity; the round-trip fixture and Zod must carry a uuid map; a retired/succeeded franchise leaves a dangling key), and every reader re-derives membership from JSON.
**(d) Cut divisions from v1.** Spec erratum pinning `divisions` at 1 for v1 (the setting stays in the catalog, its select shows one option; the §7.3.7 chain entry (5) stays inert; §11.7's divisions clause and D289/D297/D299's division arms are struck for M4). Cheapest by far; the cohort is friends-only test leagues (plan v1.4) and "build for flexibility" argues for not carrying a feature nobody has asked for — but it is a product cut across four spec sections, and it is Chris's cut to make, not a Builder's.

**Recommendation: (b).** One column, ~30 engine lines, a deterministic seeded split pinned like the rest of the schedule, one truth for every downstream reader, and no new UI on the critical path; (a)'s control lands later on the same column. If Chris would rather not carry divisions into the feedback year at all, **(d)** is the honest alternative and this Builder builds the engine with the divisions arm struck. Under either answer the fold-back rule applies (a §7.3.1/§11.7/§12 changelog entry naming the storage, or the v1 cut) before 110 is authored. **Under (b) the resuming Builder also needs the two-liner: does the auto-split happen ONLY at `in_season` entry (recommended — divisions are fixed for the season), and may a commissioner reassign after it (recommended: not in M4; M6's override family).**

**Q31 — RULED (Chris, 2026-09-02, in-session via the orchestrator — the C34/C41 precedent): option (b), the recommended option taken as offered, riders included.** A mid-season league's effective season may be engine-shrunk below the catalog's 12 to a **floor of 4 regular-season weeks**, with the shrink CHAIN: regular season shrinks first, down to the floor; then playoff rounds drop (`playoff_teams` 6 → 4 → 2 → 0); refuse only when floor + 0 playoffs cannot fit (entering at NFL week 16 or later). Riders, all ruled as recommended: (1) `draft_start` runs the same fit check as a loud pre-flight (refuse to START a draft whose season cannot fit at start time); completion SHRINKS silently to fit; completion refuses only when the draft itself crossed the boundary (rare, named, in-txn). (2) The datum fallback in the engine, each arm pinned: `COALESCE(nfl_weeks.first_kickoff_at, (select min(kickoff_at) from nfl_games for that week), nfl_weeks.starts_at)` — conservative, never maps to a week under way. (3) The typed columns hold the EFFECTIVE plan: §7.3.1's R column becomes "12–15 at creation; a mid-season league's effective length may be engine-shrunk to ≥ 4", with the matching Zod (`league-settings.ts` `min(12)`) and SQL range checks (060 `create_league`, 105 `update_league_settings`) relaxed for engine-written rows — the resuming L.D1.2 Builder carries the Zod/SQL changes; this PR records the obligation (§2 L.D1.2 row). `playoff_start_week = regular_season_weeks + 1` continuity is kept in LEAGUE-week terms; NFL week = first week + league week − 1; `league_weeks` rows materialize the plan. **L.D1.2 and the M4 schema lane are UNBLOCKED** (with Q30 above; blocker **B7 CLEARED**; applied on **#248** — spec erratum **v2.16.12** folds Q29's mapping + this floor/chain/riders into §7.3.1, §7.3.8 and §11.7; the Zod/SQL range relaxation is L.D1.2's deliverable, recorded in its §2 row and tasks-M4 L.D1.2 item 2; **D305** records the one-step derivation for non-default `playoff_teams` values). ~~OPEN … same branch, blocker B7. Wants ruling BEFORE 110 is authored~~ *(The original question — the ruling quoted, the floor-12 arithmetic, the three riders, options (a)–(c) and the (b) recommendation — is kept below as the trail.)*

**Q31 — Q29's "MINIMAL SEASON" HAS ONLY ONE LITERAL READING (THE CATALOG'S 12), AND UNDER IT EVERY COHORT LEAGUE THAT DRAFTS AFTER NFL WEEK 4 IS REFUSED AT ITS LAST PICK — ~~OPEN~~ RULED above, filed 2026-09-02 by the halted L.D1.2 Builder alongside Q30 (same branch, ~~blocker B7~~ B7 cleared). ~~Wants ruling BEFORE 110 is authored;~~ the engine is one constant away under any answer, but the answer decides a catalog erratum, a shrink chain and where the refusal fires.**

**The ruling, quoted.** Q29 (Chris, 2026-09-01): *"the settings validator shrinks-or-refuses the season length so first week + regular season + playoff span end ≤ 18 (refusal only when a minimal season plus playoffs genuinely cannot fit)."* The ruling names no floor; the only floor the spec carries is §7.3.1's R column — `regular_season_weeks` **12–15** (spec:207; `league-settings.ts:327` `min(12).max(15)`; `playoff_start_week` 13–16 range-checked in `create_league` 060 and `update_league_settings` 105). So "a minimal season" = 12 is the literal reading, and this Builder will apply it unless told otherwise.

**The arithmetic under floor 12 (measured against 039's seed).** Last NFL week used = `s + rsw − 1 + rounds × weeks_per_round` where `s` is the league's first NFL week and rounds = ⌈log₂ playoff_teams⌉ (`derivePlayoffRounds`). With the DEFAULTS (6 playoff teams → 3 rounds × 1 week) and rsw shrunk to 12: `s + 14 ≤ 18 ⇒ s ≤ 4` — **NFL week 4 starts 2026-09-30**; from **week 5 (2026-10-07)** the default league cannot fit and is REFUSED. 4 playoff teams: s ≤ 5; 2 teams: s ≤ 6; no playoffs: s ≤ 7 (2026-10-21); 6 teams at 2-week rounds: s ≤ 1. **The cohort timeline:** L.D1.1 landed 2026-09-02; 23 M4 tasks remain and M5 (waivers/trades) precedes real play per plan v1.4 — the first cohort draft realistically lands in October or later, i.e. inside the refusal band for every configuration with playoffs. Plan v1.4's own rule is that the cohort drafts *whenever a milestone is ready*, so under the literal floor the ruling's "refuse" arm — which Chris accepted only for when *"a minimal season plus playoffs genuinely cannot fit"* — becomes the cohort's DEFAULT outcome. That reads as unintended, which is why it is asked rather than shipped.

**Three consequences that ride on the same answer (each Builder-carriable once the floor is ruled, stated so the ruling covers them).** (1) **Where the refusal fires.** The mapping instant is `in_season` entry, which is draft COMPLETION inside `draft_complete_internal`'s txn (086:394; C60/D289) — days after `draft_start` and weeks after settings were validated. A refusal there aborts the draft's LAST PICK (the manager on the clock sees "the season cannot fit"). Recommended: `draft_start` runs the same fit check as a loud pre-flight (refuse to START a draft whose season cannot fit *at start time*), completion SHRINKS silently to fit, and completion refuses only when the draft itself crossed the boundary — rare, named, in-txn. (2) **The datum.** "The next NFL week whose first kickoff is still ahead" has no data today: `nfl_weeks.first_kickoff_at` is NULL in all 18 rows (039:38's banner; pinned `tests/003:64`) and `nfl_games` has ZERO writers until L.D2.1 (C58). Recommended fallback, in the engine, with each arm pinned: `COALESCE(nfl_weeks.first_kickoff_at, (select min(kickoff_at) from nfl_games for that week), nfl_weeks.starts_at)` — `starts_at` is the Wednesday 00:00 ET before the week's first game, so the fallback is CONSERVATIVE (a league entering between Wed 00:00 and Thursday kickoff maps one week later than the ruling's letter; it never maps to a week already under way). (3) **The stored representation of a shrunk season.** Q29 says the VALIDATOR shrinks, i.e. the stored `regular_season_weeks`/`playoff_start_week` change. Under floor 12 the shrunk values stay inside the catalog's 12–15 / 13–16 and every reader (`mergeSettings`' Zod `min(12)`, the 060/105 range checks) keeps working. **Under any lower floor the typed column would hold a value the catalog rejects — `mergeSettings` THROWS on such a row (the D58 loud-failure doctrine) and every settings read for that league fails** — so a lower floor is necessarily a §7.3.1 R-column erratum (e.g. *"12–15 at creation; a mid-season league's effective length may be engine-shrunk to ≥ N"*) plus the Zod/SQL range changes, and the engine writes the effective plan into the typed columns (`playoff_start_week = rsw + 1` continuity kept in LEAGUE-week terms; NFL week = first week + league week − 1; `league_weeks` rows materialize the plan).

**Options.**
**(a) Literal — floor 12, no spec change.** Cohort leagues drafting after NFL week 4 (defaults) are refused; the commissioner's remedy is `playoff_teams = 0` (fits through week 7) or not playing in 2026.
**(b) A mid-season floor below the catalog (recommended: 4 regular-season weeks), with a shrink CHAIN: regular season first, down to the floor; then playoff rounds (`playoff_teams` 6 → 4 → 2 → 0); refuse only when floor + 0 playoffs cannot fit (entering at NFL week 16 or later).** Example at defaults: enter week 10 → 6 regular + 3 playoff; week 13 → 4 + 2 (`playoff_teams` 6 → 4); week 14 → 4 + 1 (→ 2); week 15 → 4 + 0; week 16+ → refuse. Requires the §7.3.1 erratum in (3) above. The floor 4 is chosen because it is the smallest season in which §11.7's "repeat gap ≥ 3" can still mean something and a standings race exists; Chris may pick any N.
**(c) Floor 12 but shrink playoffs too** (no catalog change; the chain 6 → 4 → 2 → 0 before refusing). Extends the default's reach from week 4 to week 7 (2026-10-21); still refuses from week 8.

**Recommendation: (b) with N = 4**, plus the three riders in the paragraph above ((1) pre-flight at `draft_start`, shrink at completion; (2) the conservative datum fallback; (3) the typed columns hold the effective plan under a widened R column). It is the only option under which the 2026 cohort can draft when its milestones are ready, which is the whole reason Q29 exists. If Chris prefers (a), say so and the engine ships literal with the refusal message naming the remedy.

**Q29 — RULED (Chris, 2026-09-01, on the breakdown's approval — the C34/C41 precedent): a mid-season league STARTS AT THE NEXT NFL WEEK**, the recommended option taken as offered — the league's first week is the next NFL week whose first kickoff is still ahead at `in_season` entry, and the settings validator shrinks-or-refuses the season length so first week + regular season + playoff span end ≤ 18 (refusal only when a minimal season plus playoffs genuinely cannot fit). **L.D1.2 and the M4 schema lane are UNBLOCKED.** ~~OPEN … BLOCKS L.D1.2~~ *(original question kept in tasks-M4 §9 C50/D288 as the trail).*

**The evidence.** `056_league_weeks.sql:70` carries `FOREIGN KEY (season, week) REFERENCES nfl_weeks(season, week)` — a league week IS an NFL week by schema — and §7.3.1's catalog (`regular_season_weeks` 12–15, `playoff_start_week` 13–16 = regular+1, "must leave room for playoffs within weeks 1–18") plus §11.7's generation are all written against the identity mapping starting at week 1. That is coherent for every 2027 GA league (everyone drafts before week 1). But delivery plan v1.4 rules that **2026 test-cohort leagues draft whenever a milestone is genuinely ready** — i.e., mid-season. A league entering `in_season` at NFL week 5 with `regular_season_weeks = 14` has no legal schedule under the spec as printed: weeks 1–4 are in the past, and `playoff_start_week = 15` can't both mean "the 15th league week" and "NFL week 15."

**Options.**
**(a) Late leagues start at the next NFL week; the validator shrinks-or-refuses length to fit** — keep the NFL-week identity (the FK stands); a league's first week = the first NFL week whose first kickoff is still ahead at `in_season` entry; league creation/draft-start validation requires `first_week + regular_season_weeks + playoff span − 1 ≤ 18` and prompts the commissioner to shorten the season (or refuses) when it doesn't fit. `playoff_start_week` becomes first_week-relative in the engine's arithmetic while the stored setting keeps its §7.3.1 meaning (regular+1, continuity preserved).
**(b) League-relative weeks with a stored offset** — league week 1 is "the league's first week," mapped to NFL weeks via an offset column; every §7.3.1 number reads as printed. Costs: a second week vocabulary in every table, job, and UI surface forever, to serve a cohort-only situation.
**(c) Forbid mid-season starts** — a league can only enter `in_season` before NFL week 1. This contradicts the plan v1.4 ruling directly (the test cohort would be unable to play in 2026) and is listed only for completeness.

**Recommendation: (a).** It keeps one week vocabulary (the schema already enforces it), reads identically to the spec for every on-time league, costs one derivation plus one validation clause, and gives the test cohort real seasons this fall. The M4 GATES are unaffected under any option — the harness seeds its leagues before the replayed week — so this blocks the schedule-engine build (L.D1.2+), not the gate design.

**Q28 — RULED (Chris, 2026-09-01): "zero scoring is a user problem."** No guard is owed at any layer — a scoring document that scores nothing (empty, or every value zero) is the commissioner's business, the same doctrine as the drafts ruling (*"that's known as a 'personal problem'"*, v2.13.4). **Consequences: no shape guardrail in `scoring_rules_validate`, the TS validator, Zod, or any route — R643's re-sited clause is CLOSED-WON'T-BUILD; the M4-live framing (a league experiencing 0.00 every scored week) is answered — the product renders what the document says.** The service docblock's observation (SE.6) stands as description, not warning. *(Original question and the M4-live addendum kept below as the trail.)*

~~Q28 — a league scoring document that scores 0.00 for every player passes SQL validate, TS validate, Zod AND wall 1. Is "the document must be able to score something" a guardrail family, and where does it live? — OPEN, filed 2026-08-26 by the SE.5 Builder at the reviewer's direction (R643). NOT decided in SE.5's PR, and deliberately not improvised around.**~~

**The measurement.** `scoring_rules_validate('{}'::jsonb)` returns cleanly: `{}` is a format-1 flat map, and every one of the five §7.3.3.1 guardrail families is satisfied **vacuously** by a document with no keys. So is the TS twin (`validateScoringRulesDoc({})` → `{valid: true, violations: []}`) and so is the Zod schema (`scoringRulesDocSchema.safeParse({}).success` → `true`). A league's `{format: 2, base, positions, tier_cuts}` fork document can therefore be replaced wholesale by `{}` — or by any flat format-1 map — and every layer reports it valid. `scorePlayerWeek` then iterates an empty rules object and returns 0 for every player, with no throw: **an entire league scores 0.00 and nothing anywhere says so.** That is CLAUDE.md's *"never let 'nothing happened' mean 'it worked'"* shape exactly.

**Why this is a spec question and not a defect in SE.5's PR.** `tasks-SE-scoring-editor.md` §5(2) specifies `scoring_update_rules`' body as exactly `PERFORM scoring_rules_validate(p_rules)`, and §7.3.3.1's guardrail list has **no shape-preservation or minimum-content family**. Adding one is a change to what the spec says a valid document is — Chris's call, not a Builder's.

**Where the clause would go, and it is NOT the save RPC.** Measured: the same downgrade is reachable with no RPC at all — `UPDATE public.scoring_systems SET rules = '{}' WHERE id = <fork row>` as `authenticated` with the commissioner's own JWT returns `1 rows`, because wall 1 fires, calls the validator, and the validator passes. A guard in `scoring_update_rules` alone would be a fig leaf. If the answer is yes, the clause belongs in **`scoring_rules_validate` (103) / wall 1 (104)**, phrased against the population that can be harmed: *a document referenced by a live league may not be empty, and may not drop its format-2 envelope while referenced.*

**Two consequences originally filed with this are STRUCK, because a reviewer measured them false** — recorded so nobody re-spends the effort: **(a)** the `tier_cuts` harm is unobservable (nothing in production reads `tier_cuts`; `DEF_PA_BUCKETS`/`DEF_YA_BUCKETS` are supersets of both published families, so the two readings agree by construction — 19 tests in `tier-cuts.test.ts` pin it); **(b)** the fork-idempotency consequence is true of *every* save, including the intended ones, so it is not a property of this hole.

**The counter-case, which is strong and belongs in the ruling.** A fully format-2, fully normalized envelope with `base: {}` is equally accepted and scores identically zero — so "the league scores 0" is a **coefficient-value** question, and there is no non-arbitrary minimum. The spec also blesses the resulting state twice: `spec:1489` *"`rules` **may be** the format-2 envelope"* and the v2.11 changelog *"flat maps stay format 1 and valid forever"*. A shape check would forbid a state the spec explicitly permits.

**Why it cannot wait indefinitely: SE.6's route delegates to the same validator**, so the shipping editor will accept `{}` too. Reachable today only by a commissioner, on their own league, inside the setup/scheduled window — which is why it is not a blocker.

**Recommendation (the Builder's, for Chris to accept or reject):** rule it as a **narrow live-reference clause in 103/104**, not as a general minimum-content family — *a document that is referenced by a live league must contain at least one scorable key with a non-zero coefficient* — because that is the smallest statement that closes the measured harm without forbidding the states the spec blesses. If Chris prefers, the alternative is to rule it **not a defect** and let the editor UI warn, which costs nothing server-side but leaves the direct-write path silent.

**[Addendum 2026-08-26 — SE.6 SHIPPED, and it shipped to the validator as it exists. STILL OPEN; nothing was improvised around it.]** `PUT /api/leagues/[id]/scoring/rules` parses `rules` through `scoringRulesDocSchema`, which delegates to `validateScoringRulesDoc` — so `{}` is accepted by the route exactly as this question predicted, and `scoring-service.test.ts` records that as the shipped behaviour rather than pinning a guardrail nobody has ruled. **What changed is only the reach:** the hole is now reachable through a route as well as through `psql`, on the same population this question already names (a commissioner, on their own league, inside the `setup`/`scheduled` window), so it is still not a blocker. **What did NOT change:** the recommendation stands unaltered — if Chris rules it a defect, the clause belongs in `scoring_rules_validate` (103) / wall 1 (104), because the direct-table-write path this question measured is untouched by anything in SE.6. Chris's call.

**[Addendum 2026-09-01 — M4 makes this question LIVE for the first time, and it should be ruled before the cohort's first scored week (the M4 Architect, tasks-M4 §11).]** Until now the zero-scoring document was a pre-draft hypothetical. M4's `score-league-week` worker turns it into a **weekly experience**: a cohort league that froze such a document scores **0.00 for every team, every week, all season** — and the worker's corrupt-snapshot quarantine (tasks-M4 D292) cannot catch it, because the document is *valid*: the pipeline computes an honest zero, which is exactly CLAUDE.md's "nothing happened looked like it worked" shape stretched over eighteen weeks. The recommendation on file (the narrow live-reference clause in `scoring_rules_validate` (103) / wall 1 (104)) stands unaltered; **no M4 task builds or improvises a guard** — the worker treats a valid zero as a valid zero until Chris rules. Still not a blocker (same reachable population: a commissioner, their own league, setup/scheduled window); now carrying a deadline-shaped consequence.

**Q17 — the auction bid clock: how short should the opening window be, and does the 10-second floor on the setting move with it? — RULED 2026-08-20 (Chris): NOT one of the four options as framed — the league default and the MOCK default SPLIT. `AP.4` is UNBLOCKED.**

**The ruling.** League bid clock **stays 20s** (option (c)); a **mock** launches at **10s**. The nomination clock is ruled explicitly at **30s** — *"yes fine default 30 seconds for a nomination."* The floor is **NOT** lowered (option (d) not taken; he never raised it).

**Provenance, stated plainly because half of it is an accepted recommendation rather than a number he named.** Chris first said *"20 seconds is good"* **before AP.3's measurement existed**. After the measurement (75m10s at 20s; bid-clock run-out = **82%** of all remaining time; bidding itself **0.0s**) the orchestrator put the split to him — keep 20s for a real league because twelve humans need a beat to react, run mocks at 10s because a mock has nobody to wait for — and he answered *"yes fine default 30 seconds for a nomination."* He was then shown the resulting table (nomination 30 · bid 20 league / 10 mock) with an explicit invitation to correct it if "yes fine" had been read too broadly; he did not correct it and moved on. **Treat the 30s as his own number and the 20/10 split as a recommendation he accepted.**

**What he said matters more than the defaults, and it reframed the task.** *"every league is going to customize the clocks and probably change them multiple times during the draft. so more importantly is does that work?"* — and, on mocks, *"these mocks just get deleted when they're done so it really doesn't matter."* So AP.4 is a **small** task: the defaults are a starting point nobody keeps, and the durable question is whether mid-draft clock edits work. They do, **pause-first** (D141), for real drafts. In a **mock** they were refused entirely — which is what the **MS lane** (D216–D223, spec v2.15) now overturns, with `MS.3` making clock edits live in a mock.

*(Original question text follows, for the evidence and the arithmetic.)*

**Q17 (as filed)** *(2026-08-20, AP Architect session. Chris ruled the DIRECTION in-session ("propose a shorter default"); the number is his.)*

**Evidence.** `auction_bid_seconds` defaults to **20s** (`league-settings.ts:222`; the SQL fallback is `085:485`) and `auction_anti_snipe_seconds` to **10s** (`:223`; D128's floor at `085:778`). Anti-snipe only re-floors a clock a bid lands *inside*, so the two numbers make the **dull case cost double the exciting one**: an uncontested nomination pays the full 20s of silence, a contested one resolves on the 10s reset. On the default roster (`DEFAULT_ROSTER_SETTINGS`, `league-settings.ts:164–177` ⇒ 9 starters + 6 bench ⇒ **15 draftable slots** ⇒ **180 nominations** at 12 teams) the opening windows alone are `180 × 20s =` **60 minutes** before anyone types anything. Chris's targets, from real use on Sleeper: a live draft **under 90 minutes**, a mock **under 45**. Appendix A.3/A.4: ESPN opens a 30s bid timer, Yahoo 20s, Sleeper configurable — and **all three anti-snipe to 10s**.

**Options.** **(a) default 10s, range unchanged at 10–60** · **(b) default 15s** · **(c) leave 20s and accept the arithmetic** · and, orthogonally, **(d) lower the range's floor below 10s.**

**Recommendation: (a), and NOT (d).**
- **(a):** at 10s every bid window in the product is the same 10 seconds — the opening one and every anti-snipe reset — so the inversion disappears by construction rather than by tuning, and the rule becomes one sentence a commissioner can hold in their head. Estimated effect (an estimate, to be replaced by AP.3/AP.4's measurement): a real 12-team draft ≈ **55 min** (from ≈ 85), a mock with AP.3's reactive CPUs ≈ **42 min** (from ≈ 67) — **which is what puts the §8.8 45-minute bar in reach at all** (F85). 10s also matches the number all three incumbents already chose for their anti-snipe window, so it is not an experiment.
- **Not (d):** the 10-second floor is the *human-reaction* floor — see the page, read the name, decide, click — and the tick enforces expiry with up to a 5s lag, so most of a 5-second clock would be lag rather than clock. Lowering it buys little and lets a league configure an auction nobody can play. If a faster **mock** is wanted, that belongs to the `fast` CPU toggle (bot think-time only, §8.8's letter), not to the human's clock.
- **Stored values are not migrated under any option** — a league that chose 20 keeps 20; only new leagues get the new default. A cohort fix-up is available and is Chris's call, exactly as with AP.1's stored min-bids.

**Q18 — the uncontestable-award copy: "to the Nominator", or the team's name?** *(filed 2026-08-20 by the AP Architect session. NON-BLOCKING — `AP.2` ships the recommendation behind a single constant, so the ruling is a one-line change.)*

Chris's own words for the §8.6.9 message were *"No one can bid. Awarding Player Name to the Nominator."* The alternative names the team: *"Awarding Bijan Robinson to Team Chris."* **Recommendation: the team's name.** It reads better in the chat log and to anyone who glanced away — "the Nominator" is a role that requires you to have been watching to resolve, while a team name is self-contained, and every other award line in the room already names a team. The counter-argument is real and is why this is a question rather than a decision: *"the Nominator"* explains **why** the award happened (they nominated it and nobody could answer), which is the one thing a room that just watched a player vanish without a bid clock actually wants to know. A message that does both — *"No one can bid. Awarding Bijan Robinson to Team Chris, who nominated him."* — is longer than a 3-second beat comfortably carries.

**Q22 — should a mock's system chat posts stay?** *(filed 2026-08-20 by the MS Architect session. **NON-BLOCKING** — every MS task ships today's behaviour, which is that they do.)*

**Evidence.** Every enabled §8.7 control posts a `league_chat` system row into `draft:<mock_id>` in the same transaction as its write (D97; **re-measured: 11 of 11**, not the nine an earlier draft said — `SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE prosrc ~* 'INSERT INTO\s+public\.league_chat') FROM pg_proc WHERE prosrc ~ 'mock drafts have no commissioner controls'` → 11 of 11; it strengthens the recommendation rather than flipping it). In a real draft that is §8.7's transparency requirement (*"Pause/Play, Reset, and every commissioner action remain visible to all users"*). **In a solo practice there is nobody to be transparent to** — the launcher is the only human in the room and the post tells them what they just did.

**Options.** **(a)** keep them unchanged · **(b)** suppress them on mocks · **(c)** keep them but default the room's chat closed on a mock.

**Recommendation: (a), keep them.** The posts are **in-transaction** (D97), so removing them means branching nine write paths for a cosmetic gain; `delete_mock_draft` already sweeps the mock's chat rows explicitly (§8.8's chat-FK note), so they cost nothing at the end of a practice; and §8.8's own promise is *"Same engine, literally"* — the transcript is part of what draft night looks like. **It is a question rather than a decision** because it is the one place where Chris's ruling that a mock is where you learn what a commissioner does and his ruling of *"no"* on explanatory copy point in slightly different directions: a system post is not explanation, but it is the closest thing in the room to a narration of what a commissioner tool did. *(The COPY question itself is **CLOSED** — tasks-MS §3 ruling 3. Tooltips, teaching labels and onboarding hints are ruled out and must not be re-filed as questions.)*

*(The draft-room redesign's three questions — **Q12** chrome-free scope · **Q13** Exit Draft · **Q14** the two-tabs guard — were all **RULED by Chris 2026-08-17** and folded into the spec the same day; see Resolved below. No DR task was ever gated on them.)*

**Q24 — where do mock reports live: a PRIVATE app surface, or the user's PUBLIC profile?** *(filed 2026-08-21 by the MP Architect session. **NON-BLOCKING** — every MP task ships the recommendation, so a ruling the other way is a route move and a visibility predicate, not a redesign.)*

**Why it is a question.** Chris's two rulings point at two different places and both are reasonable readings. *"mocks should go to something on the **User's profile**, not at the league level"* — and FieldScout profiles are **public, server-rendered** surfaces (`/u/[username]`; CLAUDE.md's SEO rule; the More sheet's own *My profile* row links there, `more-sheet.tsx:101–107`). But also *"under the **More...** section there can be a Mock Drafts tab"* — which is **private app chrome**. **A mock report shows your strategy** — which players you paid up for, where you reached — and that is competitive information a league-mate could read the week before draft night.

**Options.** **(a) Private only** — `/app/mocks` + `/app/mocks/[id]`, reachable from More…, RLS-scoped to the launcher. **(b) Public profile tab** — `/u/[username]/mocks`, server-rendered, world-readable. **(c) Private by default with an explicit per-report share.**

**Recommendation: (a).** It satisfies the More… ruling exactly and satisfies the profile ruling's *intent* — the reports belong to the **user**, not to a league, which is the contrast that ruling was drawing (*"However, real drafts should have a place at the league level"*). It is also the only option that needs no new visibility decision: `delete_mock_draft` is already launcher-keyed (`071:500–504`) and `drafts` RLS already scopes reads. **(c) is the natural follow-up if sharing is wanted** and is cheap from (a) — a column and a predicate — whereas **(b) makes every past practice public by default**, which nobody asked for and which cannot be walked back for reports already published.

**Q26 — RULED (Chris, 2026-09-01): custom brackets are ALLOWED.** His words verbatim: *"Allow custom brackets for defensive scoring, thats what other platforms do."* The allowlist gives; a commissioner's own cut points may generate their own tier names. **Mechanism: recommendation (b) stands** — guardrail 1 carves `def_pa_*`/`def_ya_*` out and delegates them wholly to guardrail 2 (the document's own cuts), the smallest change and the one the R604 scope diagnosis points at; (a) remains the recorded alternative if the F59 Architect finds (b) wanting. **Consequence, said out loud: the live wall's (c)-shaped behavior is now a KNOWN GAP, not a shipping default** — F59's build must open guardrail 1 at both layers (TS + SQL, the mirror moves together) before any boundary input ships, and Q27 (the cut-list length cap) travels with it. ~~Which one gives?~~ *(Original question and analysis kept below as the trail.)*

**~~Q26 — a commissioner may cut their own PA/YA tiers (§7.3.3.1(a)/(c)), but the guardrail-1 allowlist is §23.5's CLOSED list of the 20 PUBLISHED tier names. Which one gives?~~** *(filed 2026-08-25 by the SE.4 Builder + its review round, R605. **NON-BLOCKING for SE.4/SE.4b/SE.5** — no code is owed today, because §7.3.3.1(a) says "a fork always writes the inherited family's cuts", so no SE-lane task can construct the case. It BLOCKS **F59**, the boundary editor, which is the first build that can. **The live wall already behaves as option (c), so silence ships (c) by default** — which is why this is filed rather than left in the ledger.)*

**The tension, measured on both layers (7 documents, 0 disagreements — this is not a mirror defect).** §7.3.3.1(a) reserves `tier_cuts` per league *"even though the UI ships later"*, and §7.3.3.1(c) prints the input shape F59 will take: *"A single ascending integer list per table — e.g. `0, 7, 14, 18, 28, 35, 46`"*. That list is legal today and generates seven tiers. Six of them are published names and are payable. The seventh — **`def_pa_0_6`, the first tier the spec's own example creates** — is refused by **guardrail 1** in both languages, because §23.5's `scoring_surface: 'scorable'` set is a closed list of exactly the 20 names the three *published* cut lists generate. So: **a commissioner who cuts PA where the spec says they may cannot pay the tier that cut creates.**

**The mechanism is SCOPE, not order** (R604 — an earlier reading of this said "guardrail 1 runs ahead of guardrail 2", which is true and is not the cause). Guardrail 2 has no complaint about `def_pa_0_6` at any position in the sequence: it *is* in the set the document's own cuts generate, and both layers `continue` on a generated key. Measured: the document draws exactly **one** violation, the allowlist one; the control that pays the same key under the *published* cuts draws **two**. Guardrail 1 is a membership test against a closed list, so it refuses a re-cut name wherever it runs — reordering the families changes nothing.

**Options.**
**(a) Make §23.5's scorable set a PREDICATE, not a list** — "scorable" becomes *"in the registry, **or** generated by this document's own `tier_cuts`"*. Guardrail 1 keeps a subject for every non-tier key; tier keys are validated by the guardrail that owns them.
**(b) Carve `def_pa_*` / `def_ya_*` out of guardrail 1 entirely and let guardrail 2 own them.** Mechanically the smallest change (one condition in each language, plus pins), and it follows directly from the diagnosis above: the two guardrails currently both claim jurisdiction over tier names and the closed-list one wins.
**(c) Rule that per-league cuts are restricted to the published families** — i.e. `tier_cuts` is a *choice among families*, not a free cut list. **This is what ships today if nobody rules.**

**Recommendation: (b).** It is derived from the mechanism rather than from convenience — guardrail 1's job is *"is this a stat we can score?"*, and for a tier key the honest answer is *"if your own cuts generate it, yes"*, which is exactly guardrail 2's question. It leaves guardrail 1's closed list intact for the 28 non-tier keys, where a closed list is the right instrument. (a) is the same idea expressed in the registry instead of the validator and is strictly more work for the same outcome. A finite `STAT_KEYS` enumeration can never cover free cut lists in any case — measured: a 20,000-cut list generates **20,000** tier keys and **20,011** derived indicators; a 200,001-cut list generates **200,001** and **200,012**.

**⚠ (c) IS NOT A BUILDER'S TO TAKE — it needs Chris.** It reverses two rulings he recorded in the v2.11 changelog (`spec-redraft-leagues.md`, the v2.11 entry): *"(2b) first-version UI **inherits** boundaries… no preset-set dropdown"* and *"(3) when F59 builds, boundaries are entered as **ascending cut points, never ranges**"*. Choosing (c) would make the preset-set dropdown the only possible UI — the shape (2b) explicitly declined. Recorded here per CLAUDE.md's stop rule, and ledger **F137** carries the build hook pointing back at this question.

**Q27 — should §7.3.3.1(c) cap a cut LIST's length? (the second unanswered question the F59 row carries, filed alongside Q26 for the same reason)** *(routed by D269/SE.3's R595, never filed; surfaced by R605. **NON-BLOCKING** — F59 owns the surface that can produce a long list.)*

**Why it is a question.** §7.3.3.1(c) states exactly three residuals — *ascending, integers, ≥ 2 cuts* — and a 20,000-cut ascending integer list satisfies all three. SE.3 capped the *validator's output* at 50 violations (R595) but deliberately did **not** cap the input, because capping it is a spec amendment rather than a validator's call. Measured cost of not capping: **20,000 cuts → 20,000 generated tier keys → 20,011 derived indicators** per D/ST week; **200,001 cuts → 200,001 → 200,012**. *(Correcting the number as it was first written: 200,012 is the 200,001-cut figure, not the 20,000-cut one.)*

**Options.** **(a) No cap** — the residuals stay as §7.3.3.1(c) states them. **(b) A stated cap** (e.g. ≤ 32 cuts per table, comfortably above the published 7/8/9) folded into §7.3.3.1(c) as a fourth residual, enforced in both validators with the usual one-unit pins. **(c) Cap at the UI only** — F59's editor refuses, the validators do not.

**Recommendation: (b).** The whole posture of §7.3.3.1(c) is *make the bad state unconstructible rather than validation-caught*, and an unbounded list is the one input where that posture is currently not applied. (c) is the weakest: §7.3.3.1(5) is explicit that client validation is UX only. **This one is a genuine spec gap rather than a reversal — a Builder could carry a ruling either way once it exists, but not choose it.** *(SE.4 note: unrelated to Q26's domain cap. SE.4 caps a cut's MAGNITUDE at 2^53 because above that `numeric` and IEEE-754 double disagree about which integer a cut is — a correctness bound, not a size policy, and it is orthogonal to how MANY cuts a list may hold.)*

**Layer 1 — the ROUTE. Real, cheap, and exactly what MP.6 describes.** `(room)/leagues/layout.tsx:18` redirects every `/app/leagues` URL when `featureFlags.leagues` is off. One new gate + one new page under `(room)/mocks/`, plus the `route-groups.test.ts` / `room-entry.test.ts` / `room-exits.test.ts` re-points. **No question here — this half is ready to build.**

**Layer 2 — the COMPONENT'S DATA SPINE, and it is not a layout matter.** `DraftRoom` resolves everything non-draft from `useLeague(leagueId)` → `LeagueDetail` (`use-league.ts:27–70`) and **returns `DraftRoomProblem` when `detail.data` is absent** (`draft-room.tsx:271–283`) — so with no league the room renders an error card and stops. Measured in `draft-room.tsx`: **42 lines mention `detail`**, **48 mention `leagueId`**, and the field reads are `detail.teams` ×6 (the seat map and every team name on the board), `detail.settings` ×4 (`roster_settings` for the tracker and the autopick shape, `regular_season_weeks`), `detail.members` ×2 (the §16.5.4 autodraft seat badges), `detail.my_role` ×2, `detail.league` ×2 (`name`, `scoring_system_id`). `DraftRoomLive` takes **`detail: LeagueDetail` as a required prop** (`:490`) and hands it to `DraftChat` (`:1016`), `CommishDraftPanel` (`:999`) and the dock (`:1315`). **None of this is a region, a zone or a breakpoint** — so §4 rule 15's "that is a DR2 question" does not fit it, and DR2 could not answer it. It is a *source* question, and D229(5)/§4 rule 12 is the doctrine that governs sources.

**Layer 3 — THE WRITE PATH, which nothing in the lane mentions at all, and which is the finding.** Every action the room performs posts to `/api/leagues/[id]/draft/*`, and **all 17 of those service verbs funnel through one resolver**: `resolveDraftForAction` (`draft-service.ts:328–350`), whose only draft lookup is `.from('drafts').eq('league_id', leagueId)`. The room's own eight league-keyed hook call sites are `useLeague` `:196` · `useLeagueLists` `:550` · `usePauseResumeDraft` `:705` · `useDeleteMockDraft` `:727` · `useMakePick` `:778` · `useNominate` `:803` · `usePlaceBid` `:804` · `useUpdateDraftQueue` `:841`.

**LIVE-PROBED, not inferred** (local stack at 095; whole probe inside a transaction that ended `ROLLBACK` — residue re-counted at **0**: `SELECT count(*) FROM drafts WHERE league_id IS NULL` → **0** after):

```
NOTICE:  MINTED standalone mock 431ac09d-… — drafts.league_id = NULL
NOTICE:  resolver query (eq league_id, any league in schema) -> 0 row(s); by draft id alone -> 1 row(s)
```

**So a standalone mock room, even once it renders, cannot make a pick, place a bid, nominate, pause, resume, or write a queue.** Every one of those returns `resolveDraftForAction`'s 404 (`NO_ACTIVE_DRAFT_MESSAGE`), because a `league_id = <uuid>` predicate can never match a NULL — **and there is no `[id]` value the client could supply that would change that.** The *RPCs themselves already work* (095 dropped the four `NOT NULL`s and amended the in-body auth), and `resolveActingSeat` already has its league-free mock arm (`:379–386`). **The only thing standing between a standalone mock and a working room, server-side, is that one `.eq('league_id', …)` and the URL shape wrapped around it.**

**WHY THIS IS A QUESTION AND NOT A BUILD.** Two reasons, and the second is the one I cannot settle:

1. **Nothing in the lane owns layer 3.** MP.7(4) asserts *"the launch succeeds, **and the room loads**"*; MP.11(1) asserts *"Home → launch → **draft** → complete → report"*. Both are true only if someone builds a standalone action surface. `tasks-MP` §5 assigns it to no task, §6.2's out-of-scope list does not mention it, and §7's MS table does not claim it (MS is *authority inside the room* on **league-attached** mocks). **An obligation two tasks depend on and no task owns is the R51 shape, and filing it as an F-row against myself would be MP.6 silently absorbing three tasks' worth of work.**
2. **The URL shape is a lane-level design decision with a stated doctrine on both sides.** MP.3/MP.4/MP.5 each ruled *"Two questions, two endpoints — deliberately NOT the league route widened"* (`api/mocks/route.ts:13–17`, and again on the DELETE at `[mockId]/route.ts:15–19`). Applied literally, layer 3 means **six new routes** (`pick`, `nominate`, `bid`, `pause`, `queue`, `queue/from-list`) under `/api/mocks/[mockId]/…` plus their service arms. Applied the other way it means widening `resolveDraftForAction` to `leagueId: string | null`. **Improvising between a stated house rule and its cheaper alternative, across six server routes, is exactly what "never improvise around the spec" forbids.**

**THE GENERAL FAILURE, because it is the third time this lane has hit it and the shape is now unmistakable.** D231(3a) recorded: *"a release-independence claim is a claim about ROUTES as well as components, and the route layer had a guard the component layer could not see."* §2.2 recorded the same species one level up (an inherited threat model nobody re-derived). **This is the same thing one level DOWN: the fix for the route guard was itself scoped as a route matter, and the component layer and the action layer each carry their own copy of the coupling that the route layer's fix cannot see.** *Independence is a property of every layer a request passes through, and it has to be measured at each one rather than argued from the topmost.*

**OPTIONS.**

- **(a) Split MP.6 into three tasks and build them in order.** **MP.6** = layer 1 only (the route + the gate + the three test re-points), landing **behind** its siblings so it does not ship a door onto a room that cannot act — or landing with the `/app/mocks` Resume control left disabled (F119's mechanism, already in place). **MP.6b** = layer 3, the standalone action surface (server + hooks). **MP.6c** = layer 2, the league-optional data spine + F114 + F117 + the standalone exits. **MP.7/MP.10/MP.11 depend on all three.**
- **(b) Leave MP.6 as one task and re-scope it honestly to all three layers**, accepting that it is a two-to-three-day task rather than the *"≤ half a day"* §5 promises, and that its diff spans `src/app/app/(room)/`, `src/app/api/`, `src/lib/leagues/api/draft-service.ts`, `src/hooks/` and `draft-room.tsx`.
- **(c) Ship layer 1 now and DEFER layers 2–3 with the room**, i.e. accept that a standalone mock is launched and listed but not *played* until a later lane — which contradicts ruling 3.2 (*"I want to practice drafting these players"*) and would make MP.7 and MP.11 unbuildable as written.

**RECOMMENDATION: (a), and with the layer order 1 → 3 → 2.**
- **Three tasks, because the three layers fail differently and would be reviewed differently.** Layer 1 is a route pin (source-level, cheap, RED-able today). Layer 3 is server-contract work whose review question is *"is this no more permissive for a row that HAS a league?"* — **D233(5)'s question, one layer up from where MP.1 answered it**, and it deserves the same treatment rather than being a paragraph inside a UI PR. Layer 2 is launch-facing UI with states, and gets the one review pass UI work gets. **Bundling them means one of the three gets the wrong kind of review**, which is the MS.1 precedent (*a task that audits and enables will report on its own work*).
- **3 before 2** because layer 2's browser verification — *"watch bots act, pause/resume, the chat posts must render"* — **cannot be performed until layer 3 exists.** Built the other way, MP.6c would have to claim its states from intent, which §4 rule 9 forbids.
- **On the layer-3 URL shape my recommendation is `/api/mocks/[mockId]/…` (the house rule as stated), NOT widening `resolveDraftForAction`** — but I am recommending, not ruling: the widening is genuinely cheaper (one signature, one `.is('league_id', null)` arm) and the counter-argument is that six thin wrappers around a shared resolver is the same code with more files. **Whoever rules this should say so explicitly, because MP.8's report route and any future standalone verb will inherit it.**
- **F114 and F117 travel with layer 2, not with layer 1** — both are room data hooks, and re-keying them against a room that cannot mount proves nothing. **F119's room half stays blocked until layer 2 lands**, which is precisely what D242/R515 built `openBlockedReason` to express.

**What this session did NOT do, deliberately: no code.** A layer-1-only PR would have removed F119's *"Opens when the practice room lands"* reason and pointed a live **Resume** at a room that renders an error card and cannot pick — **which is R515's finding verbatim, one task later.**

**Q23 — a mock's bid clock: does the 10-second mock number OVERRIDE a league that chose its own? — LAPSED 2026-08-21. The question no longer has a subject: the design changed underneath it. `AP.4` closes with no code; **B5 clears**.**

*(**Merge note, because the question's own filing text is not on `main`.** Q23 was filed by the halted `AP.4` Builder on PR **#186** (`halt/AP.4-mock-bid-clock-Q23`) with **D224** and blocker **B5**, and that PR is still open. This entry is the disposition, filed by the MP Architect session against `main`. Whichever PR merges second removes the standing Open copy / the standing blocker; this entry is authoritative either way. §5 carries the same note.)*

**LAPSED, not answered — and the distinction matters.** Q23 asked whether a **mock-specific 10-second bid clock** should override a league that chose its own. Chris's rulings of 2026-08-21 removed **both halves of the question**: **a mock is now STANDALONE, so there is no league to inherit from**, and he ruled the defaults directly — *"the default clock time shouldn't change for mocks, just let the user make the clocks what they want. **Use the same default** … Everyone is going change the clock times so the defaults are merely a suggestion."* **There is no mock-specific default to override with, and no league to override.** Recording this as "answered" would misdescribe what happened: nobody chose between the options; the design moved.

1. **The ruled numbers, identical for mocks and real leagues: nomination 30s · bid clock 20s · a bid inside the last 10s re-floors to 10s (anti-snipe).** **All three are the shipped values — swept, not sampled:** `grep -rhoE "auction_bid_seconds'\)::int, *[0-9]+" supabase/migrations/*.sql | sort | uniq -c` → **9 occurrences, all 20**; the same for `auction_nomination_seconds` → **8, all 30**; anti-snipe defaults to **10** (`league-settings.ts:223`, D128's floor at `085:778`), and anti-snipe *is* "a bid inside the last N seconds re-floors the clock to N". Ranges and the 10s floor already match §7.3.8. **Zero lines change.**
2. **§8.8's fidelity sentence is UNTOUCHED and DORMANT.** *"A mock is slow when the league's clocks are slow, and that is correct"* is a statement about a league-attached mock; those are **deferred, not cancelled**, and it is exactly the sentence that half returns with. Not amended, not weakened, not deleted.
3. **AP.4 has nothing left in it** — the ruled half ships, and the override that was its whole remaining content no longer exists as a concept. **AP.4's record is NOT edited by this PR**: its disposition is escalated (R472), and a lane document must not close another lane's task by assertion. **F106** files the obligation with a named actor and carries Chris's ruling as its evidence.
4. **F85 is DE-TARGETED by the same session, and it is Chris's ruling rather than an Architect's read:** *"My point about finishing a mock in 45 minutes was just an example not a target because previously it was 3 hours which basically makes it useless. with all the other fixes we've put in I think we're good."* **The under-45-minute bar stops being a gate**, spec §8.8's acceptance-bar sentence is amended to say so, and **no MP or AP task is measured against it.** **F92 survives on its own merits** — the CPU nomination still rides the 5-second sweep, measured at 13m17s on the default shape — but as a pacing cost worth fixing, not as a term in a bar.

**Q16 — §16.4's split columns: ship the SIX that have data now, or hold all nine until the volume fields land? — RULED 2026-08-20 (Chris): SHIP THE SIX.** *"Ship with 6, maybe we can calculate our own projections or derive them."* The gate moves from per-GROUP to **per-COLUMN**; rushing/receiving/passing yards and TDs (plus `receptions`) render now, the three volume fields stay gated on **F81**. The Architect's call within the ruling — the six ship under **flat stat labels** rather than under a group header that would promise a missing third column — is **D202(2)**, and the grouped presentation reassembles when F81 completes each triple. Folded to spec **v2.13 §16.4**; built by **AP.7**. *(His "derive them ourselves" aside is filed as an IDEA, not a task — tasks-AP §8 item 1.)* **BUILT 2026-08-25 by AP.7 (D257) — the seven columns (the ruled six + receptions) render in both room worlds under flat labels; Q16 is fully closed.**

**Q15 — §8.8 `fast` mock auctions: accept +$1/pass pacing for v1, or rule on a lever? — RULED 2026-08-20 (Chris): none of the three levers as framed; the CADENCE itself changes.** Verbatim: *"On other platforms the auto draft bots bid like normal people would so if a player is valued at $40, two things can happen. 1 a bot can bid $35 or $40 immediately if they want, just like a real person can. They also bid super fast in $1 increments, like real players do."* The question offered (a) jump-bids, (b) n raises per pass, (c) a shorter clock under `fast`; the ruling takes **(a) AND something the question did not ask for** — a CPU raise is **provoked by the bid it answers rather than by the 5-second sweep**, which is why (b) becomes unnecessary and the global sweep is never made faster. **(c) is explicitly NOT taken** — it touches the human's clock, against §8.8's printed letter; the clock is instead addressed at the league level (**Q17**). Chris also set the acceptance bar the question lacked: **a mock under 45 minutes, a live draft under 90.** Folded to spec **v2.13 §8.8/§8.6.3**; built by **AP.3** (which discharges **F76**), with the clock half at **AP.4**. **BUILT AND MEASURED 2026-08-20 (AP.3, migration 091) — this question is now closed by evidence, not only by ruling.** Both mechanisms shipped: a CPU response runs in the transaction that provoked it (`draft_mock_cpu_respond_internal`, called from the ONE bid writer and BOTH nomination paths — the sweep untouched at 5s, pinned as a stored literal in pgTAP 039 §A), and the raise amount is a seeded jump toward `LEAST(value, max_bid)` (`draft_mock_cpu_raise_amount`; **P(jump) = headroom / ceiling**, no tunable constants). The two textures Chris named are both present and both pinned: on a $50 ceiling opened at $1 a CPU answers with **$35** (pgTAP 038 §E, a stored literal — his own example), and at $36 on a $40 ceiling the same curve nibbles to $37 in over 85% of 2 000 seeded draws (039 §B). **The pacing, MEASURED on the same 8×2×$20 mock through the real 5-second cron: 11m37s before, 6m41s after (1.74×), on an identical board.** The default 12×15×$200 shape was measured separately — see AP.3's §2 row and **F92**; the <45-minute bar remains AP.4's (F85).

**Q14 — The two-tabs guard: hard takeover, or two live tabs? (filed by the draft-room redesign Architect session, 2026-08-17; spec §9.3's v2.12 note + tasks-DR D156. Does NOT block any DR task — DR.6 builds the recommendation and a reversal is a small change.)**

**Evidence.** Chris ruled that in-app desktop entry opens the room in a **new browser tab** (§16.1). A user can therefore trivially hold two tabs of one draft — and nothing today notices. Each tab opens its own socket and its own `draft:<id>` subscription (`use-draft.ts:244` — the only `.channel(` call in `src/`), runs its own 15s `draft_touch` liveness heartbeat (`use-draft.ts:394–413`), and tracks presence under the same key (presence is keyed by team id), so the room's presence list shows one manager twice. §9.3's budget is written per *client* — "one socket per client, ≤ 3 channels" — and says nothing about one user holding several. **Correctness is not at risk** (the server is authoritative per §8.1, so a stale tab's action is refused by the ordinary validators); what is at risk is fan-out, quota, and a presence list that lies.

**Options:**
- **(a) Hard takeover — newest tab wins (recommended).** The newest tab of a draft holds the connection; older tabs unsubscribe, stop the heartbeat, and show a plain "This draft is open in another tab" state with a **"Use this tab instead"** button. Client-local coordination (`BroadcastChannel` keyed by draft id, `localStorage` fallback), scoped **per browser profile** so a laptop and a phone are untouched. One live room per browser: presence is honest, fan-out is bounded, and the failure mode is a screen that tells you exactly what happened and how to fix it.
- **(b) Both tabs stay live; dedupe presence only.** Nothing is taken away from the user, but the fan-out doubling stays, the heartbeats double, and the presence dedupe has to be right or the list is wrong anyway — most of the work of (a) for less of the benefit.
- **(c) Do nothing.** Defensible on correctness grounds alone, and wrong on draft night: a manager with two tabs open sees themselves twice in the room and does not know which tab is real.

**Recommendation: (a).** It is the option that makes the presence list true, and the takeover button means a user who lands on the stale tab is never stuck. Flagged for you because it is a visible behavior — one of your tabs going quiet is something you would want to have chosen.

**What's gated:** nothing. DR.6 builds (a) unless you say otherwise.

**RULED 2026-08-17 (Chris): option (a) — hard takeover, newest tab wins.** Verbatim: *"The most recent one takes over and the others disconnect."* Build exactly as recommended: the **newest tab of a given draft holds the connection**; older tabs **unsubscribe the `draft:<id>` channel and stop the `draft_touch` heartbeat**, then render the plain "This draft is open in another tab" state with a **Use this tab instead** button that takes the connection back. Coordination is a `BroadcastChannel` keyed by draft id with a `localStorage` fallback, scoped **per browser profile** — a laptop and a phone remain two legitimate live clients and are untouched. Nothing about the mechanics changes from the recommendation, so the spec text folded at v2.12 stands as written and is now a **ruling rather than a working assumption** (§9.3's two-tabs guard, marked in place). **DR.6 builds it** (tasks-DR §5; D156).

**Q13 — Exit Draft: where does it go, and should leaving mid-draft warn? (filed by the draft-room redesign Architect session, 2026-08-17; spec §16.4 zone 1. Does NOT block any DR task — DR.2 builds the recommendation.)**

**Evidence.** You ruled **Exit Draft appears in the top bar for both commissioner and non-commissioner** — everyone must be able to leave. With the room in its own browser tab (desktop), "leaving" has two plausible meanings that the shipped **Exit room** link (`snake-draft-room.tsx:704–706`, a plain link to `/app/leagues/[id]`) never had to distinguish: navigate this tab back to the league, or close the tab. There is a hard constraint on the second: **`window.close()` only works on a tab a script opened**, so it would work when you came from the in-app CTA and **fail silently** on a deep link, a refresh, or a bookmarked room — the worst kind of button.

**Options:**
- **(a) Navigate in place to league home; never close the tab; no confirmation (recommended).** One behavior on every entry path, no silent failures. No warning on the way out because leaving costs nothing real — the draft continues without you and autopick covers your picks (§8.4), which is exactly what it is for.
- **(b) Navigate in place, but confirm when it is YOUR turn.** Honest about the one moment leaving is expensive. Costs a modal on the room's most time-pressured surface, and the clock keeps running while you read it.
- **(c) Try to close the tab, fall back to navigating.** Rejected: the same button does two different things depending on how you arrived, and users learn buttons by what they did last time.

**Recommendation: (a)**, with (b) available later as a small addition if test-cohort feedback says people leave by accident. Flagged because "Exit" doing something you did not expect is a trust problem, not a polish problem.

**What's gated:** nothing. DR.2 builds (a).

**RULED 2026-08-17 (Chris): option (a)'s MECHANICS — navigate in place to league home, never `window.close()`, no confirmation — but the REASON is different from the one recommended, and the reason is what gets built.** Verbatim: *"Exit draft just exits you from the draft room and after a certain amount of time puts you into 'auto draft' mode. Which is how all mock drafts work."*

**The recommendation's rationale is corrected here.** It said "no warning because leaving costs nothing real". That is wrong: **leaving DOES hand your picks to the engine — and that is intended and expected**, the incumbent mental model Chris is naming (you leave, the bots draft for you). The mechanics are unchanged; what changes is that the behavior is a *stated feature*, not a cost to be papered over.

**Which mechanism — the load-bearing half of this ruling.** Two distinct autopick paths exist and **Exit triggers only the first**:
- **The D102 away path (§8.5.5's v2.8.13 erratum, migration 068) — THIS is what Exit fires.** The room's `draft_touch` heartbeat stops when you leave; after the 45s freshness constant (`draft_liveness_freshness()`, `068_draft_tick_autopick.sql:347–355` — 3 × the 15s room cadence) the seat reads **STALE**; at each of that manager's deadlines the pick is then **held open for `disconnect_grace_seconds`** (§7.3.8, default 30) and autopicked from queue → primary board → Big Board → ADP (§8.4). **Returning to the room restores manual control immediately** — the next heartbeat re-freshens the seat, and a manager who returns mid-hold may still pick by hand (E3).
- **The persistent `is_autodraft` toggle** (`league_members.is_autodraft`, §8.4's "Auto-draft me"; §12.2:762). This keeps autopicking **even after you come back**, until it is explicitly switched off.

**Exit must trigger the first and must NOT write the second.** `is_autodraft` is a deliberate, sticky choice a manager (or a commissioner on their behalf) makes; setting it on exit would silently strip a returning manager of manual control and make them hunt for a toggle to get it back. The heartbeat/staleness machinery already delivers exactly what Chris described, with the strictly better return-to-control property. **DR.2 must not touch `is_autodraft`**, and needs no new mechanism at all — Exit is a navigation.

**Verified against the code 2026-08-17 (the ruling depended on it, so it was checked rather than assumed).** The heartbeat is a `useEffect` at `src/hooks/use-draft.ts:394–413`; its cleanup (`:409–412`) calls `clearInterval(id)` and removes the `visibilitychange` listener. Navigating away unmounts the room, React runs that cleanup, and **no further `draft_touch` calls are made** — so leaving genuinely stops the heartbeat today. (The effect is additionally gated on `heartbeatActive` — defined at `:393`, early-returned at `:395` — so it never runs outside `live`/`paused`; and closing the tab stops the interval with or without the cleanup.) **There is no gap to close — DR.2 inherits working machinery** rather than owning a fix.

**Consequence for copy (part of the ruling, not a nicety).** Exit's affordance must say what actually happens. "Exit Draft" alone is not sufficient: the control states that **picks will be made from the manager's Targets while they are away, and that returning restores manual control**. The vehicle is the Builder's within the no-confirmation ruling — a `title`/tooltip on the control, a short line in the command bar, or a brief toast on the way out — but a confirmation modal is explicitly not one of the options (§16.5.4's designed-copy rule). Folded into spec §16.4 zone 1; **DR.2 owns it**.

**Q12 — Does the chrome-free full-screen treatment extend to the LOBBY and the RECAP? (filed by the draft-room redesign Architect session, 2026-08-17; spec §16.1's v2.12 note. Does NOT block any DR task — DR.1/DR.7 build the recommendation.)**

**Evidence.** Your ruling names "the Draft Room". Two neighbouring surfaces are not obviously in or out. **The lobby is not a choice:** it shares the `/draft` route and the room flips lobby→live **in place** (D120), so it inherits the chrome-free frame by construction — the only alternative would be splitting the route, which would break the in-place flip that makes draft-night feel live. **The recap is a real choice:** `…/draft/recap` (`src/app/app/leagues/[leagueId]/draft/recap/page.tsx`) is a separate route serving both the real and mock variants — a post-draft *reading* surface people revisit days later, where the nav, search and the right rail are useful rather than noise.

**Options:**
- **(a) Lobby chrome-free (forced), recap stays in the app shell (recommended).** The chrome-free treatment is for the live, time-pressured experience; the recap is a document. Keeping the recap in the shell also means the way *out* of it is the app's own nav rather than a bespoke exit.
- **(b) Both chrome-free.** Consistent — "everything under `/draft` is full-screen" is an easy rule to remember — but it puts a reading surface in a frame with no navigation, so every route out has to be rebuilt inside it.
- **(c) Lobby in the shell, room chrome-free.** Rejected on the mechanics above: it would break the in-place lobby→live flip.

**Recommendation: (a).** Recorded in spec v2.12 as the working assumption so the DR tasks have something to build; say the word and (b) is a small change to one route group.

**What's gated:** nothing.

**RULED 2026-08-17 (Chris): option (a) — the lobby and the live room are chrome-free; the recap keeps the app shell.** Verbatim: *"having a bunch unnecessary UI mid draft doesn't make sense… you need all the space you have for the draft surfaces"*, naming ESPN, Yahoo and Sleeper as doing exactly this.

**The framing above is replaced — Chris pushed back on it and he was right.** The full-screen treatment exists for **one reason: the live draft is space-hungry, and any app chrome on screen mid-draft is space taken from a draft surface.** That is a UX reason and it is the whole reason — not a route-mechanics argument, and not an open architectural question about where the app shell belongs. The lobby and the live room share the `/draft` route and are both part of that live surface, so both are chrome-free. **The recap was never in scope of the ruling**: it is not a draft surface at all — it is a post-draft reading page people revisit days later — so it keeps the app shell, and the app's own navigation is the way out of it.

Recorded as **a rule with its reason** in spec §16.1 (the v2.12 note's last paragraph rewritten in place) and in the **DR.1** / **DR.7** banners. *(If consistency is ever wanted, flipping the recap to full-screen is a one-route-group change — it moves from `(shell)` to `(room)` and nothing else changes.)*
