- **D310 — L.D4.2 build mechanics: the layering, the family's SQLSTATE split and why it differs from members/draft, §9.3's second channel, the activity feed's scoping decisions, and what was deliberately not built.** (1) **Layering is the D68/D71 house pattern, extended not forked:** four Route Handlers that do auth + param plumbing only (pinned by `inseason-routes.test.ts`, the `scoring-routes.test.ts` shape), three services over an INJECTED client (`transactions-service.ts` · `schedule-service.ts` · `activity-service.ts`), and ONE shared SQLSTATE mapper `inseason-errors.ts` that L.D4.1 composes onto rather than re-typing. Nothing in `app/` names an RPC, a table or a rule (pinned). (2) **The family maps `P0001 → 409`, and the difference from members/draft (`→ 400`) is deliberate and recorded rather than smoothed over.** Two ledger rows written by two different Builders — **F224(e)** (L.D1.4's lineup-route contract) and **F227(f)** (L.D1.5's transactions contract) — print the same mapping, so it is a family contract, not a slip; both cite "the members-api precedent", which maps P0001 → 400 (`members-service.ts:56`, `draft-service.ts:124`), and the tension is named here so a reviewer can rule it either way with one line changed. The substantive argument for 409: every P0001 that 111/112/113 raise is a refusal ABOUT LEAGUE STATE — this player is on another roster, his game kicked off, the roster is full, the week is live, the league is not `in_season` — none of which is a defect in a perfectly well-formed request that simply lost a race; 22023 (a genuinely malformed argument) keeps 400, which is what makes the split carry information. The MESSAGE is passed through verbatim on every raised arm either way (F227(f)'s clause; `client-fetch.ts:userFacingMessage` strips the raiser's prefix and the §-citation at the one surfacing layer). (3) **§9.3's SECOND `.channel(` in `src/`, opened deliberately and reviewed with this PR.** The budget pin in `single-room-tab.test.ts` said a second hit "is a §9.3 budget event that needs its own review, whoever adds it" — this is that event. §9.3's own budget line names the league channel as one of the three a client may hold ("one socket per client, ≤ 3 channels (current league, current draft, notifications)"), so this is the spec's shape, not an extension of it; the draft spine's topic is `draft:<id>` and structurally cannot carry `league:<id>` events. The pin was rewritten as ONE CHANNEL PER TOPIC and now names both spines. The rule that did NOT move: a consumer never opens its own channel — `use-league-channel.ts` registers every `LEAGUE_CHANNEL_EVENTS` member once and dispatches to the caller's handler map (D109(1)), so L.D4.1's matchups/standings hooks add handlers, never a channel (**F233(a)**). Handlers live in refs so the effect depends only on `leagueId`; the D109(9) stale-registry sweep, the pre-join `setAuth`, `private: true`, refetch-on-every-confirmed-join, refetch-before-resubscribe and the capped backoff are all carried from the draft spine. (4) **Freshness is refetch-on-event, not cache patching (D298), and the decision of WHICH events is pure and pinned.** D296's payloads are column-selected DB-side, so an event cannot reconstruct a feed row; `activityEventInvalidates` admits `transactions` (117/L.D1.9) and `league_chat` (070 — LIVE TODAY: a non-draft context broadcasts to `league:<league_id>`, so a Remix confirmed in one browser already reaches another member's open feed) and refuses everything else, so a `matchups` score tick every few seconds never re-fetches a paged list. The four unshipped D296 events are registered NOW on purpose: the listener costs nothing and the feed starts moving the moment 117 lands, with no edit here. (5) **The activity feed's two scoping decisions, both no-leak.** (a) System posts are filtered to `context = 'league'` — the literal every league-room D97 post carries (111:749, 111:1124, 112:1141). Taking "every system post of this league" instead would publish one member's SOLO MOCK practice to the whole league, because a mock draft's posts carry the launcher's `league_id` with a `draft:<id>` context; the draft room and the recap render their own posts. Non-system chat is never in the feed (chat is its own surface). (b) A non-member reads NOTHING and gets an empty feed rather than a 404 — the established posture for league reads (D114(5)); a transport error is a 500, never an empty list (rule 10). (6) **Paging is measured, not inferred (CLAUDE.md's 1000-row rule).** `limit` ≤ 100 with an over-fetch of `limit + 1` PER SOURCE, so the union's top `limit` is provably the true top `limit` and `has_more` is a measurement; the ceiling plus the over-fetch cannot reach PostgREST's cap, which is asserted in the suite rather than assumed. A NULL or unparseable `created_at` sorts LAST, never as the newest event. (7) **`Date.parse` inside `src/leagues/**` is legal and checked:** the M0 fence bans `Date.now`, argless `new Date()`, bare `Date(...)`, `Date['now']`, `globalThis.Date` and constructor aliases — not a pure parse of a value the database wrote. Lexicographic string compare was rejected as only accidentally correct while every row carries the same UTC offset. All entropy (both `action_id`s and the Remix seed) is minted in the HOOKS, outside the fence (the D112(3)/D114(5) precedent); the seed goes through the catalog's own `mintScheduleSeed`, so the wire value is always inside §11.7's space. (8) **The F65(b) identity guard, applied at BOTH verbs.** 113's replay is kind- and team-scoped (R732) but not ARGUMENT-scoped, and 111's is kind-scoped but not SEED-scoped: reusing your own `action_id` for a different move — or a different seed — returns the FIRST result with no error, and answering 200 would report something the caller never did. Both results carry what the check needs (`team_id`/`add_player_id`/`drop_player_id`; `schedule_seed`), so it costs no extra query. Both are pinned live, with the negative control (the second player really was not added; the board really is still the first seed). (9) **What was deliberately NOT built, each with its reason:** no `GET …/schedule` route (§15.3 prints none — `use-schedule` reads `matchups` + `league_weeks` under the member SELECT policies, D92); no `transactions` READ hook separate from the feed (one read of that table in the app, not two that can disagree); no commissioner-action ENRICHMENT (`commissioner_actions` does not exist — the task text says M6); no `schedule_edit_matchup` route (the drag arm is L.D5.3's UI task, not in this task's four); no live-realtime DELIVERY test (the `draft-realtime-db` harness budgets ~224s of retry for the boot-window race and R163 already records what parallel load does to it — the wiring is source-pinned here and L.D6.2's E2E is the end-to-end proof; **F233(c)**). (10) **§15.6's hook list was CHECKED, not missed:** it names 15 hooks and has never been amended for the ~35 that landed since (`use-draft-bids`, `use-draft-controls`, `use-mock-drafts`, `use-scoring-templates` are all absent), so it is indicative and no erratum is owed — the spec needed no change for this task at all. (11) Action-id prefixes **af7** (transactions-api-db) and **af8** (schedule-api-db) — the D108(14) registry, swept 2026-09-03 (af0–af6 taken). **(12) The #255 fix round (R768–R775), and what each one changed.** **R768 — the one real defect: a COMMITTED move reported to the caller as a failure.** The F65(b) guards at both verbs compare client strings byte-for-byte against uuids POSTGRES wrote, and Postgres renders `uuid` lowercase while `z.uuid()` is case-INSENSITIVE — so an UPPERCASE `team_id`/`action_id` (a body the route's own schema accepts) reached the RPC, the add/drop COMMITTED (roster row + transactions row), and the guard then answered **409 'That didn't go through'** with the `action_id` spent, so the retry the copy asks for could not work either. CLAUDE.md's "never let 'nothing happened' mean 'it worked'" run in reverse, by the very guard that exists to prevent it. Fixed at the SCHEMA, once, in a new shared `inseason-ids.ts` (`normalizedUuid = z.uuid().transform(v => v.toLowerCase())`) applied to `team_id`/`action_id` on add/drop and `action_id` on the Remix confirm — so the RPC and the guard both see the form the database returns. The guards keep every tooth: a reused id naming a different move, or a different seed, is still 409, pinned uppercase in both stack suites. **R769 — the `league:<id>` spine was per-hook-instance, and its D109(9) stale-registry sweep evicted OTHER LIVE INSTANCES OF ITSELF.** Latent (one caller today) and guaranteed the moment L.D4.1 followed F233(a): the supabase browser client is a singleton so `getChannels()` is shared, realtime-js returns the existing channel for a held topic, and B's mount removed A's channel → A saw CLOSED → `onDrop` (an invalidate) + reopen in 1s → A's sweep removed B's → forever, two invalidations per cycle, with `attempt` reset to 0 on every SUBSCRIBED so the backoff never grew out of it. The spine is now a **module-level refcounted room per topic** (`leagueRooms` / `joinLeagueRoom` / release), fanning ONE channel out to N handler maps — which is what the file's docblock had claimed all along, so the code was made true rather than the claim weakened. Still exactly one `.channel(` in the file, so both budget pins hold unchanged. A late joiner gets `onJoin` on attach when the room is already live (its cache may predate the room), and the room closes only on the LAST release. **R770 — the activity cursor was `created_at` alone against a `(created_at DESC, id DESC)` order**, so every item sharing a page-boundary instant was served on NO page, silently, forever. No M4 writer produces such a tie; §13.2/§14's waiver processor (N claims resolved atomically) and M6's `commissioner_move` (a transactions row + a system post in one txn) both will. The cursor is now composite — `before` + `before_id`, applied as PostgREST `or(created_at.lt."T",and(created_at.eq."T",id.lt."ID"))` on BOTH source queries, with `next_before_id` beside `next_before` and a lone `before_id` refused by name rather than paging as if no cursor were sent. `activity-service.test.ts`'s header had already CLAIMED this coverage (its tie test proved determinism, not cursor survival) — the claim is now true. **R773 — three guards that could not fail** (`isLeagueChannelEvent(event)` on a value drawn from `LEAGUE_CHANNEL_EVENTS`; `activityEventInvalidates('transactions'|'league_chat')` inside handlers that only existed for those two events). Taken the second way D272(20) allows: the feed's handler map is now DERIVED — `LEAGUE_CHANNEL_EVENTS.filter(activityEventInvalidates)` — so the predicate SELECTS the events rather than decorating them, and `isLeagueChannelEvent` was deleted as dead (the unknown-event-inert property holds by construction: only known events are bound, and dispatch is an optional call). **R771/R772/R774/R775 were record corrections**, each fixed at its site: a docblock pointing at `schedule-routes.test.ts`, which does not exist; F227(f)/F224(e) citing "the members-api precedent" for a P0001 → 409 mapping that precedent does not carry (the CODE is right — 409 governs the in-season family per the #255 ruling — the CITATION was false); F233(c) implying nothing about realtime delivery was provable when the `league_chat` arm was; and F233(f), the new row routing the source-pinned ANON arm to a future Route Handler harness (the reviewer verified the DB defence in depth: anon reads 0 rows on all four tables, no anon EXECUTE on the three RPCs).

- **D309 — L.D1.5 build mechanics: the number note, the verb's shape (and why the idempotency key is a STAMP, not a third ledger), E32 as built (which weeks, which datum, which edges), the lineup-lock question decided from the text (E34), the `free_agency` reading, fa_hold's inclusive boundary, caps by payload key, the CHECK, fixture discipline, the proof chain, and what was deliberately not done.** **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-02 on `origin/main` @ `a5ee6bd` and `origin/docs/DR2-draft-room-v2`, the only other open branch):** `D309` / `F227` / `R753` → **0** on both ⇒ D309 and F227 taken here (no R taken — no review yet; no Q filed — nothing halted); chain heads at task time: `ls supabase/migrations/ | tail -1` → `112_lineups.sql`, `ls supabase/tests/ | tail -1` → `060_lineups.sql` ⇒ **113 / 061**, the tasks-M4 §7 reservations CONFIRMED; spec header 2.16.16 ⇒ **2.16.17** (a PATCH: §13.1 / §12.9 / §12.19 annotations the build measured — no ruling touched). D137 provenance: NO function is replaced — 112's `lineup_kickoff_internal` (the per-player kickoff for a player's NFL team) and `lineup_current_week_internal`, 111's `schedule_window_internal`, 052's `is_league_member` are CALLED by name. **(1) The shape — one verb, one seam, two lock helpers, one stamp.** `roster_add_drop` (DEFINER, `search_path=''`, REVOKE FROM PUBLIC/anon) reads transaction `now()` and calls `roster_add_drop_internal(…, p_at)` (plain, triple-REVOKEd — the D307(3)/D308 seam 061 drives at kickoff±1s and close±1s); `pool_game_lock_internal` (E32 for one week) and `pool_game_lock_any_internal` (every week that could still bind). **Why the idempotency key is a column on `transactions` (`action_id` + a partial UNIQUE on `(league_id, action_id)`) and not a third ledger table:** D307(2)'s argument for `schedule_actions`/`lineup_actions` was that those verbs' domain rows are deleted/overwritten by later actions, erasing a stamp; a `transactions` row is APPEND-ONLY (§12.9 — M6 may flip `status`, the row never goes away), so the stamp survives every later action, exactly the 099 `draft_budget_adjustments` shape; `payload` IS the returned document, replayed byte-identically (061 D2 text equality + a four-table digest unchanged); a refused call writes nothing so the retry re-evaluates; replay is kind-scoped (a `trade` row with the same id refuses by name — R732) and team-scoped (another team's id refuses). One more ledger for M6's fold (F223(a)/F224(f)) avoided. **(2) E32 as built.** The lock is evaluated PER PLAYER from `nfl_games.kickoff_at` at the instant, over the set of NFL weeks `w ≤ current` whose `correction_window_ends_at > at` (or is NULL) — the current week AND the previous one when its Thursday-06:00 window is still open (a week's window closes inside the NEXT week; 061's calendar closes week 2's window before the fixture instant so the no-game-rows fallback of an earlier week cannot bind — the first cut's calendar had it open and locked everyone, which is how the two-window shape was found; the two-window claim was UNMEASURED in the first cut (R754) and is now pinned in 061 §F5/E7: NE played in week 2 and is a week-3 bye, week 2's window at close−1s refuses BOTH the add and the drop naming week 2, AT the close and at +1s both live and the result reports the current week's bye datum). Per week: 112's `lineup_kickoff_internal` (bye = game rows but none for the team → never locked; NO game rows → the week datum for EVERYONE, the R740 posture, arm named `nfl_weeks.starts_at` — which on the REAL calendar is a full-season FREEZE of add/drop until game rows exist: the reviewer measured hourly over 2026 from week 1's start with 0 `nfl_games` → free 0 of 2,709 hours, and 270 of 2,709 with only `first_kickoff_at` seeded; local stack and production carry 0 games for 2026 — the dated dependency on L.D2.1/L.D3.1 is F228 (R755)) and the week's `nfl_weeks.correction_window_ends_at` (D294's letter; a NULL window after a kickoff refuses BY NAME — never an unbounded lock read as free, 061 E6). Locked iff `kickoff ≤ at < window_end`: closed AT the kickoff (the E41 convention), OPEN at the close ("until the week clears" is strictly before) — 061 E1/E2 (add) and F1/F2 (drop) pin −1s/AT/+1s at BOTH edges; the two sides are independent clauses and the DoD probe removes the drop clause alone. **Probe figures, corrected 2026-09-03 (R761 — the number written here was the FIRST CUT's and three rounds stale):** the CURRENT figures are **10 drop-side cells red (49/50/52/57/67/75/76/84/86/87) and the file ABORTS at cell 88 — 87 of 160 ran** (the accepted drop's state breaks a later fixture), every add-lock cell green. The trail: 7 of 130 (first cut) → 8 of 139 (review round) → 10 of 150 (Q32/Q33 application) → 10 of 160 (this fix round). `league_player_pool.locked_until` and the `locked_in_game` state are NEVER read (pinned by prosrc) — 114's `lineup_lock_tick` maintains them for the pool VIEW (D291); an add evaluates the games table whatever the stored state says. **(3) The lineup-lock question — RULED BY CHRIS 2026-09-03 (Q32 + its amendment, §3, verbatim there) and APPLIED: the lock is PLAYER-LEVEL.** A player locks at his own kickoff (E32's window) and then cannot move in ANY direction — not bench→lineup, not lineup→bench, not into another slot, not dropped; a player whose game has not started moves and drops freely regardless of what else is locked ("if its mid day sunday and all the users starters are locked … a player on their Bench that doesn't play until Monday night … can be dropped"). 113 as landed: the drop is refused iff the player's OWN game has kicked off (both settings' letter); the `kept_in_locked_lineup` branch of the first cut is REMOVED (a droppable player has not played — nothing to keep; the reviewer's R753 bypass-by-composition cannot arise); a dropped player's entry is ALWAYS cleared from every row from the current week on (F1/F2/H1 re-pinned). 112 needed NO change: `per_player_kickoff` already is the player-level model — a locked slot's player never moves (060 E5) and a kicked-off BENCH player cannot enter a slot (060 E4; re-pinned in 061 F6 as the composition after a drop: RB1 drops, rb:0 empties, FA3's game kicks off, `set_lineup` moving FA3 into rb:0 refuses); the emptied slot re-seats only with a player whose own kickoff is ahead (061 F6). **`first_game_of_week` (§7.3.6, shipped in 112) does not fit the model** — per the orchestrator's direction it is NOT cut or altered in this PR (112's semantics untouched; the one first_game_of_week cell 061 §H1 carries is 112's existing whole-week refusal, already passing); its fate is PENDING CHRIS (an erratum or a Q30-shape cut as a separate docs/task). **RESIDUAL, recorded not asked (the D220 shape for Chris's read):** with `player_game_lock = OFF` §7.3.4/§13.1's letter is lax incumbent behaviour — a PLAYED player may be dropped and his slot clears. **What that costs, MEASURED and corrected 2026-09-03 (R759 — this entry previously stopped at "his slot clears", which reads as "the slot then stays empty"; it does not):** the emptied slot stays empty for the week ONLY under `first_game_of_week` (112's whole-week lock refuses the re-seat — 061 §H1 on L2). Under `per_player_kickoff` — the DEFAULT `lineup_lock`, and the pair that had NO 061 cell until this round — the very next `set_lineup` **re-seats** the emptied slot with a player whose own kickoff is still ahead, because 112 has nothing to lock once the stored occupant is unrostered (112:894 *"dropped since (113) — nothing to lock"*): the team loses the played player's points AND gets a do-over on the slot after seeing his result. Now pinned end-to-end in **061 §H3** on a new lax × `per_player_kickoff` fixture league (L5): the identical re-seat is REFUSED while he is rostered and ACCEPTED after the drop. The ruling was given for the on-by-default case; whether the player-level lock should bind drops regardless of the setting — one clause (`v_game_lock AND` → unconditional) plus the §7.3.4 row's "off" sentence — is a PRODUCT CALL FOR CHRIS, filed with `first_game_of_week`'s fate as **F230** / **Q34**. Not made here: R759's fixable half (the cell + this correction) is taken, its substantive half is his. E34 stays M5's `bench_lock`-off claim-processing path; F227(b)'s fan-out duty LAPSES (no phantom exists). The first cut's text-derived reading (E34 generalized) is superseded — kept only in the #254 review record and Q32's trail. **⟨SUPERSEDED FIRST-CUT READING BEGINS — everything from "Read:" to "(F227(b))" below describes the REMOVED `kept_in_locked_lineup` build and is kept verbatim ONLY as the trail. Every present-tense claim in it is FALSE of what ships, and the 061 cells it cites now assert the opposite: 061 F2 reads "his slot is CLEARED in both rows — no kept phantom exists" and 061 H1 reads "his week-locked slot is CLEARED — no phantom". Marked 2026-09-03, R761.⟩** Read: §7.3.4 makes `player_game_lock` the ONLY lock on drops ("a rostered player locks for drops at their kickoff … off reproduces lax incumbent behavior"), §13.1 repeats it, §11.2's "locked slots are read-only" governs lineup EDITS, and **E34 states the consequence of a locked starter being dropped** — "the locked starter's stats still count for the dropping team's matchup that week; the player enters waivers". So: the lineup lock does NOT block the drop; E32 does when on. On a drop, every `team_lineups` row of the team from the current week on has the player's `slot_map` entry CLEARED (slot empty, `starters[]` element emptied with `["empty"]`, bench trimmed — F224(i)) UNLESS the slot is LOCKED at the instant (per_player_kickoff: his game for that week kicked off; first_game_of_week: that week's first kickoff passed), where the entry is KEPT and the result says `kept_in_locked_lineup` (061 F1 cleared / F2 kept in the STRICT league after the window closed / H1 kept in the LAX league under the week lock — the lineup byte-unchanged while the roster row is gone). Under `player_game_lock = true` + `per_player_kickoff` the kept case is unreachable (E32 refuses first — same datum); it is reachable under lax (E34's own config) and under `first_game_of_week` for a starter whose own kickoff is still ahead. **Said for Chris's read (the D220 shape):** E34's accepted edge — the dropping team keeps his points and, once his waivers lapse, a pickup team could start him the same week if his kickoff is still ahead — is the spec's, not new; and L.D2.2's fan-out must map a locked week's stored starters as well as `league_rosters` or the dropping team's score loses him (F227(b)). **⟨SUPERSEDED FIRST-CUT READING ENDS — the sentences that follow are current.⟩** A player on a RESTRICTED IR spot may be dropped (§7.3.2's stint binds moving him OUT of the spot into the roster; a release is not a move — 061 F4). **(4) `free_agency` — RULED 2026-09-03 (Q33, §3, verbatim there): the pair `free_agency` / `waiver_period_hours` is PROVISIONAL — Chris's two real leagues (daily 09:00-PT waivers with a Sunday-06:00 → Monday-night FA window; Tuesday-midnight waivers then FA all week; re-waiver on no valid claim) fit neither — and F229 files the waiver-scheduling investigation (Architect, before M5). THE M4 INTERIM (ruled by the orchestrator under Chris's direction, recorded as such): a lapsed `waivers_until` is FCFS-addable under BOTH values — the `continuous` claim-only refusal of the first cut is REMOVED, the pool vocabulary kept, 061 §H2 pins −1s refused / AT adds under `continuous` and §G3 under `immediate_after_waivers`; a player with no pool row adds under both. The first cut's reading, superseded and kept as the record:** §7.3.4 prints `immediate_after_waivers` / `continuous` with "Unclaimed players become FCFS"; D294 says a lapsed `waivers_until` is FCFS-addable PER the setting. Built: `immediate_after_waivers` (default) ⇒ addable the instant `waivers_until` passes (state evaluated at read, no sweeper — pinned at −1s refused / AT lapsed lives); `continuous` ⇒ a lapsed player is NOT FCFS-addable (the incumbent meaning keeps unclaimed players on waivers for the processor, which is M5's — refused by name), while a player with NO pool row stays addable under both (§13.1's "add an unowned player" is unconditional). Whether `continuous` should make FRESH free agents claim-only too is M5's decision (F227(a)); this reading never lets a lapsed player through under `continuous` — the never-weaken direction. **(5) fa_hold, caps, capacity, the transactions row.** `fa_hold_hours` applies to `acquisition_type = 'free_agent'` rows (a drafted player is never held — pinned): dropped at `acquired_at + hold − 1s` ⇒ FA (`early: true`), AT the hold ⇒ waivers (inclusive). Caps are counted from `transactions` — this team's `complete` rows whose payload carries `add_player_id` (drop-only never counts; an add+drop counts one; M5's claim rows must carry the same key — F227(a)); weekly by `week = current`, season by league (one season) — 061 J pins 2nd-of-2 lives / 3rd refuses / drop-only at the cap lives / the calendar moved → weekly restarts, season 3rd lives, 4th refuses. Every executed move writes ONE row with `type = 'add_drop'` (§13.1's letter for this verb whatever the shape — the §12.9 `add`/`drop` types stay for other writers), `week` = current, `payload` = the result; the whole payload is pinned as a LITERAL built against now() minus the random `transaction_id` (061 D1). **(6) The CHECK (F222(a) taken).** `pool_waivers_until_iff_on_waivers`: `(state = 'on_waivers') = (waivers_until IS NOT NULL)`, two-sided because §12.19's own comment says "NULL unless on_waivers" (an `on_waivers` row without an instant is a player nobody can add; a stale instant on another state is invisible to the partial waiver index) — 061 C pins both directions. The stack suite creates its league on `SYNTHETIC_SEASON` (2099), sets it `in_season` directly (no `DRAFT_INSTANT` — nothing for pg_cron's draft_tick to start), places NO game rows (the contested player's made-up team `VPA` is a bye or under the 2099 datum — never locked), upserts its own two players, and its cleanup releases `transactions` + `league_player_pool` before `teams` (the FK on `initiator_team_id` has no cascade). 057's `columns_are` on `transactions` gains `action_id` (the pin's purpose — an exact set — moved). 045's census is UNCHANGED (no new table). - **D308 — L.D1.4 build mechanics: the number note, the six-function shape and why a second ledger table, the F18 swap and the legacy-row disposition, the fit as built (and the measurement that shaped its golden), the lock law's datum chain, the current-week read, the IR contract and the designation bridge, `allow_illegal_lineups` as built, the commissioner arm, idempotency, and what was deliberately not done.** **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-02 on `origin/main` @ `4fd3f8a` and `origin/docs/DR2-draft-room-v2`, the only other open branch):** `D308` / `F224` / `R736` → **0** on both (the one `Q32` hit on main is D306's own number-note text, not a filed question) ⇒ D308 and F224 taken here (no R taken — no review yet; no Q filed — nothing halted); chain heads at task time: `ls supabase/migrations/ | tail -1` → `111_schedule_remix.sql`, `ls supabase/tests/ | tail -1` → `059_schedule_remix.sql` ⇒ **112 / 060**, the tasks-M4 §7 reservations CONFIRMED; spec header 2.16.15 ⇒ **2.16.16** (a PATCH: §11.2/§12.13 annotations the build measured — no ruling touched). D137 provenance: NO function is replaced — `schedule_window_internal` (111) and `is_league_member`/`is_league_commish` (052) are CALLED by name; 001's two `team_lineups` policies are DROPPED by name (the swap). **(1) The shape — one verb, one seam, four helpers, one ledger.** `set_lineup` (DEFINER, `search_path=''`, REVOKE FROM PUBLIC/anon) reads transaction `now()` and calls `set_lineup_internal(…, p_at)` — plain, triple-REVOKEd, the postgres-only seam pgTAP drives at kickoff±1s (rule 10 / D307(3): a client-facing verb never takes a caller-supplied instant — a manager could pick the free window). Helpers, all plain + `search_path=''` + REVOKEd: `lineup_fit_internal` (the pure E16 matcher), `lineup_kickoff_internal` (the per-player datum), `lineup_current_week_internal`, `lineup_designation_internal`; plus `team_league_id`, a DEFINER policy predicate deliberately WITHOUT a REVOKE (the 052:27–29 documented deviation — it is evaluated as the calling role by the RLS policy). **Why a second ledger TABLE (`lineup_actions`) rather than a stamp:** a lineup's domain row is OVERWRITTEN by every later set, so an action_id stamped on `team_lineups` would be erased by the next edit and a stale retry of an EARLIER submit would re-execute over the newer lineup (exactly D307(2)'s argument for `schedule_actions`); the ledger row survives every later action, the replay is byte-identical (060 pins text equality + digest unchanged), RLS on with ZERO policies (060 walks manager/commish/anon: SELECT 0 while postgres sees N, INSERT 42501, UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING 0). Not an audit; M6 folds it with `schedule_actions` (F224(f)). **(2) The F18 swap (C12), and the legacy rows.** DROP `"Lineups follow team visibility"` (001:853–854, USING (true)) and `"Users can manage own team lineups"` (001:856–861, keyed on `teams.owner_id`); CREATE one SELECT `is_league_member(team_league_id(team_id))`; NO write policy for any role. 060 pins both directions (the 052/019 pattern): a member with NO teams row reads every lineup in the league; the C12 ghost (owns a teams row in the league, not a member) reads NOTHING and his INSERT raises 42501 — both of which 001 GRANTED; the manager who owns T2 reads but gets UPDATE/DELETE RETURNING 0 and INSERT 42501; the commissioner's direct UPDATE touches 0. **Legacy rows:** MEASURED on the local stack 2026-09-02 — `team_lineups` holds **0** rows (0 on standalone teams, 0 on league teams; `teams` holds 0). Production was NOT queried from this session (the Builder cannot) and may hold pre-league rows on standalone teams (`teams.league_id IS NULL`). Disposition: **EXPLICITLY ORPHANED**, not owner-readable — after 112 no policy reaches such a row (060 pins the standalone owner reading 0 of his own legacy row while postgres sees 1). Safe under either population because NO application code reads or writes `team_lineups` (`grep -rn team_lineups src e2e scripts` → only `src/types/database.ts`; 053's banner: no app code writes teams), so an orphaned row is one no product surface could show before either; if the standalone teams feature returns it gets its own policy then (F224(g)). **(3) The fit as built — and the measurement that shaped the E1 golden.** `lineup_fit_internal(slots, players)` is a BFS augmenting-path matcher over ≤ ~12 slot instances × ≤ ~11 starters. The submitted `slot_map` KEYS are the manager's placement: every per-slot-valid placement is SEEDED verbatim (fixed/locked players first) and kept unless an augmenting path needs to move it; a per-slot-invalid placement is re-seated along an augmenting path if ANY legal arrangement exists and the canonical map is returned (`rearranged: true`, `moved[]` named); a player with no augmenting path is refused BY NAME with the slot he wanted and what it accepts (E16's "names the unfillable slot"). Locked players are FIXED vertices: no path may traverse a slot a locked player owns (060 §D pins the fixed shape unplaced beside its unlocked twin re-seated). Greedy first-eligible (no augmentation) fails the two-flex trap — the DoD probe. **Measured while pinning the RPC golden:** the first cut of E1 left SUPERFLEX empty, and the matcher placed the mis-keyed RB1 THERE (the shortest augmenting path is a free eligible slot, no displacement) — correct, but not the trap; the shipped E1 fixture fills SUPERFLEX (TE2) so the only route is the displacement (WR1 → W/T, RB1 → W/R/T), and the stored map is pinned as a literal. Positions are normalized DEF → DST (the 086 shape); `players.position` is single-valued, so the spec's per-player multi-position eligibility array is not consulted (none exists — F224(h)). **(4) The lock law's datum chain (§11.2/§7.3.6/E42/§23.3; rule 9).** Every instant is read from `nfl_games.kickoff_at` at evaluation time; `locked_at` is the RECORD of the earliest instant any slot of the lineup locks (the week datum under `first_game_of_week`, the earliest started player's kickoff under `per_player_kickoff`), never the decider — 060 E6 moves KC's kickoff to now+1h and the "locked" slot re-opens with `locked_at` still saying otherwise, then to exactly now() and it locks again (E42 both ways; AT the kickoff is locked — closed on the kickoff side, the E41 convention). `per_player_kickoff`: (a) every stored starter whose game has kicked off must sit at the same key (replace / move / bench all refuse naming slot, player, instant and datum arm); (b) a played player never enters a slot he was not stored at; every unlocked slot of the same lineup stays editable (pinned by editing wr:0 beside the locked qb:0). The per-player datum `lineup_kickoff_internal(season, week, nfl_team, at)`: min kickoff of the team's game(s) that week (`players.team` ↔ `nfl_games.home_team/away_team`, both the Sleeper vocabulary L.D2.1 writes); a week WITH game rows but none for the team = BYE (no lock, flagged `bye`); a week with NO game rows at all falls back to `schedule_window_internal`'s chain (`nfl_weeks.first_kickoff_at` → `starts_at`) for EVERY player — the conservative direction (D307(3): the window only narrows) — 060 §H pins week 4 locked for every slot once `first_kickoff_at` passes, the arm NAMED in the refusal. `players.bye_week` is NOT read (§23.3: kickoff-driven). `first_game_of_week`: after the week datum ANY change refuses; an identical submit under lock is `no_changes`, never a refusal (pinned). **(5) The current week, the IR contract, the designation bridge.** `lineup_current_week_internal(league, at)` = the league's greatest `league_weeks.week` whose `nfl_weeks.starts_at` ≤ at, clamped to the first week before the season — a read of the calendar TABLE at the §23.3 boundaries 114's `league_week_advance` will flip `league_weeks.status` on, not wall-clock arithmetic; `league_weeks.status` is NOT read for tenure because it has no writer on this chain (R730's lesson) — F224(a) hands 114 the choice of switching the read or keeping it (they derive from the same rows). IR spots are ROSTER-level state, so an IR move is judged against the current week whatever `p_week` the submit names, and the submitted map is the WHOLE picture: IR spots ride `slot_map` as `"<ir_key>:0"` and an absent IR key is a REMOVAL (the contract L.D4.1/L.D5.1 inherit — F224(e)). Placement requires the designation NOW; a spot change is a placement on the new spot (restricted tenure re-checked); Restricted sets `ir_lock_until_week = current + min_weeks` and removal refuses while `current < lock` (060: placed week 3 with min 4 ⇒ 7; refused at 3 and at **6**, ACCEPTED at **7** — the calendar moved inside the txn with the weeks' `first_kickoff_at` arm kept ahead so tenure, not lock timing, is what those cells measure); an IR'd player who turns Active is KEPT and flagged `ir_ineligible`; IR + starter in one map refuses ("exactly one slot"); an IR move on a played player refuses on lock timing. **The designation bridge, measured:** `players.status` on the stack carries the FEED's spellings (Active 720, Questionable 85, IR 71, Inactive 10, PUP 7, Sus 1, DNR 1, NA 1 — `sleeper.ts:202` collapses `injury_status` into it, C56) while the catalog's `IR_DESIGNATIONS` are OUT/IR/Doubtful/PUP/NFI/Suspended (§7.3.2); `lineup_designation_internal` maps case-insensitively with `Sus` → Suspended and everything else (Active, Questionable, Inactive, NA, DNR) → no designation. Pinned (`Out` → OUT accepted on an OUT/IR spot; Questionable refused by name; `Sus` → Suspended). F224(b) asks the sync layer to normalize at ingestion so the bridge becomes the identity. **(6) `allow_illegal_lineups` as built (§7.3.6).** Flags per starter: `bye`, `out` (designation in the non-playing set OUT/IR/PUP/NFI/Suspended — Doubtful/Questionable PLAY as far as the lock is concerned), `empty` (an empty instance is allowed under BOTH settings — the setting governs byes/OUT, not vacancies; an empty slot scores 0 like everywhere in the industry); `ir_ineligible` on IR entries; `illegal` = any bye/out/ir_ineligible. TRUE: accepted, flags stored on `starters[].flags` and returned. FALSE: a bye/OUT player in an UNLOCKED starting slot blocks the submit BY NAME (a locked slot's bye/OUT player is not the manager's to change — flagged only); pinned both ways on L2 with the benched twin succeeding. **(7) The commissioner arm.** D293's "(or commissioner)" is built: a commissioner may set ANY team's lineup under the SAME lock law (no past-lock, no past-week edit), and the row records `edited_by_commish = TRUE` (the manager's own set FALSE — both pinned); tasks-M4 §12's audited past-lock/retroactive override is M6's and does not exist here (F224(c)). **(8) Idempotency, loud emptiness, `slot_key`.** `p_action_id` REQUIRED (22023); replay returns the stored jsonb byte-identically and writes nothing; an identical canonical map with no IR move is `no_changes: true` BY NAME (returned, ledgered, `set_at` and the roster digest unchanged — pinned). The lineup row is created on first touch (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, then FOR UPDATE, FOUND asserted); every UPDATE's row count is asserted; a week off the calendar, a PAST week (current is 3, week 2 refuses naming the M6 override), a closed week (`correction_window`/`final`), a league not in season, a team of another league, a retired team, an empty roster, an unknown slot key (naming every slot the roster has), an unrostered player, a duplicated player, a non-object map, a non-string value — every one refused by name (060 §G/§H). `league_rosters.slot_key` (072's "M4 manages"): when `p_week` is the current week, starters take their instance key and the rest `bn` (counts asserted against the roster); IR keys are written on placement and `bn` on removal whatever the week; a future-week submit leaves the starters' `slot_key` alone (pinned by digest). Lock order: `leagues` FOR UPDATE, then the lineup row FOR UPDATE, then roster UPDATEs; held lock pinned as the min RTT of three `set_lineup` calls < 50 ms (060 §K). **(9) Fixture discipline (F215/R724; F199).** 060's 2026 calendar is RELATIVE to now() (week w starts (w−3) weeks − 1 day ⇒ current week 3), all 2026 `nfl_games` rows are its own, and every boundary is `now() ± 1s` on the DATUM inside the frozen txn. The stack suite creates its league on `SYNTHETIC_SEASON` (2099), seeds it idempotently, places two 2099 week-1 game rows with FIXED literals (2001-09-09 locked / 2099-09-13 open — transaction `now()` lies between them for the life of the repo, no clock read), upserts its OWN nine players on made-up NFL abbreviations (VLA…VLI — only the intended players can ever lock) and deletes players, games, league graph and users in cleanup (the D306(6) order). 045's census literal grows 63 → 64 (`lineup_actions` sorts between `leagues` and `list_comments` — measured with `string_agg` on the stack); its §C/§E allowlists are re-derived UNCHANGED (only the DEFINER verb writes the ledger, `in_season|playoffs`-only — unreachable from a mock; the delta cells passed). D137 provenance: NO function is replaced — 110's `schedule_build_internal` is CALLED by name, never copied (rule 11). **(1) The shape — one plan, three doors.** `schedule_remix_plan_internal(league, seed, at)` is the single place a proposed schedule is computed: the league's seated franchises (110's own team source, same-league by construction), its EFFECTIVE `regular_season_weeks`, the first week (= `min(league_weeks.week)`, so a mid-season league regenerates NFL weeks 10..15, not 1..6), the pure builder with the candidate seed over the WHOLE regular season, then a per-WEEK classification — regenerable iff the `league_weeks` row is `upcoming`, the week's OWN first kickoff is still ahead at call time (R730 — the same datum as E41's, per week), and every row is `scheduled`, un-overridden and unscored (R733). Preview returns the plan; confirm writes from the SAME plan (a client-supplied schedule is never read — D289's "confirm regenerates from the previewed seed in-body"). The diff is one row per (week, game type, team) whose opponent or side changed, with a human line in two shapes ("now plays X instead of Y" / "now hosts|visits X (was away|home)"), `change_count`, and an EXPLICIT `no_changes` for an identical seed (rule 10 — never an empty array read as success). **Why per week, whole:** the spec's "replaces all `scheduled` matchups" cannot be read per ROW without breaking §11.7's own uniqueness invariants — a week with one `final` row and three `scheduled` ones cannot take three generated rows without double-booking the final row's two teams — so a week holding ANY non-`scheduled` row is frozen whole, named in `weeks_frozen[].reason` (`week_live` / `week_final` / `week_correction_window` / `week_kicked_off` / `matchup_not_scheduled` / `matchup_overridden_or_scored`); the never-weaken direction (freeze more, never less). A Remix's domain rows are the matchups it writes — and the NEXT Remix deletes every one of them, so a stale retry of the earlier action_id would find no stamp and RE-EXECUTE (regenerating over the later schedule and posting twice); an edit's two stamped rows are erased by any later edit of the same rows the same way. A ledger row survives every later action, so the replay is exact: the stored `result` jsonb is returned byte-identically (059 pins text equality, the post count, the ledger count and a five-table digest unchanged — and that the replay WINS even when the retry carries a different seed: the action_id identifies the SUBMIT, 099/E2). So the verbs read `now()`, and 059 applies D146's one-unit rule to the DATUM instead of the clock: inside a transaction `now()` is frozen, so `nfl_games.kickoff_at = now() ± 1s` IS kickoff−1s / kickoff+1s exactly, and `= now()` is AT the kickoff (closed — "until" is strictly before). The sim/e2e drive the window the same way (move `nfl_games.kickoff_at` on the synthetic season — F223(f)). **(4) The seam a post-kickoff Remix leaves, said so nobody reads §11.7's Generation invariants as promises across it.** Frozen weeks keep their rows (pinned BYTE-IDENTICAL over `m::text` — id, scores, updated_at, everything — R601) and the regenerable weeks take the builder's rows for THOSE week numbers from the new seed (pinned ≡ the builder restricted to those weeks — the season stays ONE generation with weeks carved out, never re-numbered). Both verbs refuse outside the space by name (22023) with the one-unit twins pinned (−1 / 0, 2^31−1 / 2^31). **(6) The permutation — a design claim measured FALSE before it shipped (D276).** A pairing change is never a single-row write: every team plays exactly once per week per game type, so the new teams' vacated slots must take the displaced teams (home-slot displaced → the new home team's slot, away → the new away team's; a side flip displaces nobody; two new teams from one sibling swap the pairings; two from two siblings touch three rows). - **D306 — L.D1.2 build mechanics: the number note, the engine's shape and why, what was MEASURED rather than assumed, the range-relaxation finding, the F215 measurement, the fixture blast radius, and what was deliberately not done.** **Number note (D161 — measured 2026-09-02 on `origin/main` @ `1d89890` and `origin/docs/DR2-draft-room-v2`, the only other open PR):** `D306` / `F222` / `R724` / `Q32` → **0** on both ⇒ D306 and F222 taken here (no R taken — no review yet; no Q filed — nothing halted); chain heads at task time: `ls supabase/migrations/ | tail -1` → `109_inseason_tables.sql`, `ls supabase/tests/ | tail -1` → `057_inseason_tables.sql` ⇒ **110 / 058**, the tasks-M4 §7 reservations CONFIRMED; spec header 2.16.12 ⇒ **2.16.13** (a PATCH for the two §7.3.1 annotations the build measured — no ruling touched). D137 provenance: `draft_complete_internal` from **086:394–454** (3 hunks: signature, the PERFORM, the REVOKE), `draft_start_internal` from **098:164–438** (4 hunks: signature, two DECLAREs, the pre-flight, the REVOKE) — both DROP+CREATE because a defaulted parameter cannot be appended by CREATE OR REPLACE (the 102/D201(2) shape; 022/033/035's signature pins moved with them), `draft_resolve_order_internal` from **102:65–178** (1 hunk, same signature), `leagues_snapshot_guard` from **059:126–142** (1 hunk; the trigger untouched). **(1) The engine's shape.** Park–Miller LCG (state × 48271 mod 2^31−1 — bigint-safe, explicit, never `setseed()`), Fisher–Yates over its stream for the permutation, then the circle method (team 1 fixed, the rest rotate). One cycle of n−1 rounds is a 1-factorization of K_n, so plain cycling gives balanced repeats (spread ≤ 1) with every repeat exactly n−1 weeks later — that is ≥ 7 for every v1 size, so the spec's "≥ 3" holds with room, and 058 pins the MEASURED minimum (7/9/11/13) rather than the construction. Home/away: a pair's base side is (round, position) parity — stable per pair because a pair meets at exactly one (round, position) — and flips on every later meeting of that pair in that game type (a jsonb counter). `second_opponent` = round (r + offset) of the same factorization with offset drawn 1..n−2, so the secondary round shares no edge with the primary round: E40 by construction, pinned by measurement (and the break probe skews exactly that offset). Input-order independence is designed in (the ids are sorted before the seed acts) and pinned. The seed folds mod 2^31−1 with a 0 → 1 map (R727 — was mod 2^31−2, which aliased 0 ≡ 2147483646 and 1 ≡ 2147483647): the one unavoidable collision of a 2^31 seed space onto 2^31−2 states is seed 0 ≡ seed 1, said out loud and pinned beside seed 0 ≠ seed 2147483646. NO divisions arm; the writer never reads the key (pinned by prosrc + by byte-equal generation at 1 vs 2). **(2) The chain, the datum, the write-back — all built to the ruling's letter and each pinned at its boundary.** `schedule_fit_internal` reproduces the §11.7 worked examples as an 18-row literal (week 10 → 6+3 … week 15 → 4+0, week 16+ refuses) and the D305(5) drop steps (12/10 → 8 → 4, 8 → 4 → 2); the floor−1 cell (week 13: rsw 3 would fit, the chain keeps 4 and drops a round) is its own pin. The chain is ONE-DIRECTIONAL (R726, spec v2.16.14): `regular_season_weeks` is never re-grown after a playoff-round drop, so with `playoff_weeks_per_round = 2` a drop frees two weeks and the plan may end at 17 (058 pins 10/14/6/2 → 4 + 2 rounds, last 17, where 5 + 2 rounds would also have fit) — the ruling's letter, not a re-optimizer. `schedule_first_week_internal` is STRICTLY ahead (at the datum instant the week is under way) — each COALESCE arm pinned on a synthetic 2077 season whose arm instants all sit AFTER that week's `starts_at`, so a lost arm reds by name. The writer writes the EFFECTIVE columns back only when the plan shrank (or a seed was minted), asserting exactly 1 row; `league_weeks` materializes the WHOLE plan incl. playoff weeks (D288 — `playoff_start_week` continuity is visible in NFL weeks); playoff `matchups` rows are 116's. A minted seed is 31 bits of `gen_random_uuid()` (not `random()`), written back so the schedule stays reproducible — 058 reproduces a minted schedule through the pure builder. **(3) The entry-instant lesson, said so nobody repeats it — WITH ITS ARM LABEL (R725).** The datum decides the window: "enter at NFL week W" is any instant in [datum(W−1), datum(W)). Under the datum's THIRD arm — `nfl_weeks.starts_at`, the Wednesday 00:00 ET fallback, which is what 039's seed and every fixture here carry (`first_kickoff_at` NULL, no `nfl_games`) — noon on Wednesday of week W is ALREADY week W+1 (the smoke test and the first draft of 058 both had that wrong; the engine was right). In production L.D2.1's `ingestWeek` writes `first_kickoff_at` = the week's earliest kickoff, so the window is [kickoff(W−1), kickoff(W)) and Wednesday noon of week W maps to W — the first arm, pinned in 058 §E with the same −1s/+0s twins. 058's 2026 goldens use Thursday noons of the prior week under the starts_at arm, and the two twins are 2026-12-15 23:59:59 ET (week 15, fits 4+0) / 2026-12-16 00:00:00 ET (week 16, refused) — for both the writer and completion; the sweep's `entryInstant` docstring says the same. **(4) The range relaxation, measured — and why the SQL is unchanged.** The §2 row/spec asked that the 060/105 SQL range checks "accept engine-written rows". Measured: both are checks on RPC PARAMETERS (`p_playoff_start_week` 13–16) — creation never sees a stored row, and `update_league_settings` is status-gated to `setup|scheduled` at step 3 BEFORE its step-4 range check (105:895–900), so an engine-written row (which exists only at `in_season`+) can never reach either. They already accept such rows, vacuously, while creation and settings edits keep 12–15 / 13–16 EXACTLY as the ruling requires; relaxing them would weaken creation for nothing (never-weaken). Left byte-unchanged; 058 §M pins a stored rsw-4/psw-5 row living and a settings PATCH on that league refusing by the STATUS gate. The TS half was the real hazard (Q31's measured `mergeSettings` throw): the Zod parse range is now ≥ 4 / ≥ 5 (`MID_SEASON_REGULAR_SEASON_FLOOR`), the 12–15 / 13–16 creation ranges moved into `validateLeagueSettings` (every create/PATCH runs it) with one-unit twins pinned, `league-settings.test.ts`'s parse-range rows moved with the schema (the pin's purpose moved), and the settings arbitrary draws 4..15. Recorded in the spec as v2.16.13's §7.3.1 note; M6's override path inherits the effective ranges (F222(c)). **(5) `schedule_seed` — minted from the action_id, not from randomness.** The first draft minted from `crypto.getRandomValues` and the L.A0.3/R22 determinism guard refused it (lint). The landed rule: `mintScheduleSeed(actionId)` = the UUID's first 32 bits masked to 31 — deterministic (a D68 replay stores the same seed), no clock, no random source, and a v4 UUID's leading bits are as unpredictable as a seed needs to be; `leagues-api-db`'s round-trip pins now expect the stored blob = the submitted blob + the minted key. Zod: `schedule_seed` nullable, default null (= not yet minted; the engine mints). **(6) F215, measured — TWICE, because the first measurement was completion-only (R724).** The Q31 rider-(1) pre-flight makes draft START calendar-bound as well (a season-2026 fixture is refused from 2026-12-16 00:00 ET under the `starts_at` arm and dead from 2027-01-06), and the first discharge measured only completion sites. **2026-09-02 — Builder (L.D3.1, the nflverse data adapter — the F11 parallel data PR; branch `feat/M4-L.D3.1-nflverse-adapter`; **TS only — no migration, no schema, no typegen**; takes **D304**; **FLIPS F11 ✅**; amends **F216** + **F211**; files **F219**)**

No migration, no pgTAP, no typegen — `git diff -- src/types/database.ts` empty; chain heads untouched (109 / 057); D137 n/a. Worked in the main tree on its own branch — no other builder was live (the schema lane is halted on #248). **(1) Composition, not a fork.** `NflverseProvider` (`src/lib/leagues/stats/nflverse/nflverse-provider.ts`, +`csv.ts`, +`eastern-time.ts`) implements the §23.1 `StatsProvider` interface unchanged, and the back-fill is `ingestWeek(provider, time, io)` exactly as L.D2.1 shipped it — `ingestWeek` is byte-identical on this branch, its contract needed no addition, and `nfl_games` keeps ONE writer (D303(3)). The stack suite composes the two the way production will. **(2) The files, pinned by path** (`NFLVERSE_URLS`; plain `fetch` of nflverse-data GitHub release assets, no HTML, no third-party API — the standing rule): `schedules/games.csv` (all seasons, one 2 MB file; 2026 = 272 REG rows, every `gametime` published, measured) and `weekly_rosters/roster_weekly_<season>.csv` (per (team, week, player) with roster `status` AND a `sleeper_id` column). Every column the adapter reads is required BY NAME (`requireColumns`) and every row is a Zod parse — a renamed column or a ragged row refuses before a single game is interpreted (pinned both ways). `injuries_<season>.csv` exists for 2025 but NOT for 2026 (404 at fetch time) and is not consumed: it is the Friday report (`Out/Doubtful/Questionable`), not inactives, and Q1 keeps Sleeper as the designation source. **(3) The Eastern→UTC seam (§23.3's load-bearing conversion).** `gametime` is a US/Eastern wall clock with no offset. `easternToUtc(gameday, gametime)` takes the offset from the platform's IANA data through `Intl` (`America/New_York`) — never a hard-coded −4/−5 and never the process zone — with a one-step re-check across the shift, so the fall-back of 2026-11-01 02:00 (INSIDE NFL week 8: Thu Oct 29 20:15 EDT → `2026-10-30T00:15Z`, Sun Nov 1 13:00 EST → `18:00Z`) resolves from zone rules; the ambiguous 01:xx hour (never a kickoff) resolves to its first occurrence. Ten literals pin it (the September opener, the week-8 Thu/Sun/SNF/MNF quartet, the week-9 09:30 ET Madrid game, a January week-18 slot, and the D146 pair 01:59 EDT / 03:00 EST), plus the raw offset read (240 on Oct 31, 300 on Nov 2). **(4) Status honesty.** nflverse can say only "a result is posted" — the adapter emits exactly `{scheduled, final}` (pinned over both fixture seasons), never `live` or `postponed`; a postponed/moved game arrives as a changed `gameday`/`gametime`/`week` and becomes a moved `nfl_games` row through `ingestWeek`'s diff (E42's mechanism is evaluation-time reads of that row). Live status comes from the composite's base tier (see (8)). **Regular season only** (`game_type = 'REG'`, like the sleeper tier's `/schedule/nfl/regular/`): postseason rows are counted and dropped — `nfl_games.game_type` defaults to `'regular'` and `ingestWeek` never writes it, so writing week 19–22 rows would have mislabelled them; D303's "once L.D3.1's feed carries 19–22" is therefore "it deliberately does not" (R707's skip stays dormant, still pinned by L.D2.1). **(5) Team vocabulary.** The house codes are `nfl-teams.ts`'s (Sleeper's schedule uses them too — measured on the 2025-wk2 fixture, `LAR`); nflverse's 2026 rows differ in exactly one code, `LA` → `LAR` (`NFLVERSE_TEAM_TO_HOUSE`, measured against all 32); any code outside the house set REFUSES (a relocation must be mapped deliberately, never written as a stray string). The nflverse `game_id` (`2026_01_NE_SEA`) is the `nfl_games.id` — stable, published, self-describing (F219 records that the table has no `source` column). **(6) Inactives — C56's site.** Measured on `roster_weekly_2025.csv` (46,849 rows): `status = 'INA'` appears for 3,593 rows, 5–6 per team per played week (KC 6 / ARI 5 in week 1, beside 48 `ACT`), ZERO for teams on bye, present weeks 1–18 — that is the game-day inactive list, published after the fact. 876 of those rows lack `sleeper_id` (OL/DL/LB — positions Sleeper does not track); the adapter drops and COUNTS them. `getInactives(season, week)` groups INA rows onto the week's game per team (`ProviderInactives` is per game) and sorts ids for determinism; `publishedAt` = the injected `time.now()` — D16's accepted limitation (a back-fill loses arrival timing), stated on the type, not hidden. A team with INA rows but no game that week is counted and named (never seen in 2025); a week with finals but zero INA rows is named as a feed that has not caught up. The 2026 file at land time carries pre-season week-1 rows only (`ACT/CUT/RES/W04/RET/EXE`, no `INA`), so the CLI's inactives pass for 2026 week 1 reports "no game of the week is final yet (nothing to declare)" — the fixture is the 2025 KC+ARI week for shape. Nothing writes inactives anywhere (no table exists; M5's consumer reads the feed — F211 amended). The adapter never touches `players.status`. **(7) What it does NOT supply, loudly.** `getWeekStats`/`getInjuries` return `[]` with the reason on the adapter's call log (`provider.reports` / `lastReport` — a provider method has no report channel of its own), and `ingestWeek` then names the empty section in its own report (`provider returned zero stat rows…`, `score_fanout: no scoring delta…` — both pinned over the stack). `capabilities` is the empty set: no §23.5 tier is claimed. A season the file lacks THROWS (`zero rows for season 2024 … refusing an empty schedule`), never an empty success. **(8) The composite.** `withNflverseCalendar(base, nflverse)` — name `<base>+nflverse`, capabilities the base's — returns nflverse's schedule with the base tier's status merged per game matched on `week:away@home` (rank scheduled < live < final < postponed; `postponed` is a positive claim a T+1 `scheduled` must not undo), base-only games counted (`lastScheduleReport`), `getGameStates` from the merged set, `getWeekStats`/`getInjuries` delegated to the base, `getInactives` to nflverse — pinned with a fake base incl. the LAR match on both sides. This is what L.D2.3 binds (F216 amended). **(9) The CLI and the one real run.** `npm run sync:nflverse -- <season> [week]` (`scripts/sync-nflverse.ts`; sync territory, service client, `.env.local` unless overridden) runs ONE `ingestWeek` poll with the standalone adapter — the schedule read is season-wide, so one run back-fills every game and every calendar week's bounds — then lists the week's inactives read-only. Run once against the LOCAL stack with the real files (the permitted one-off fetch): 272 games inserted / 18 weeks bounded (`first_kickoff_at` week 1 `2026-09-10T00:20Z` … week 18 `2027-01-10T18:00Z`; every week's first kickoff falls after 039's seeded `starts_at`, incl. the Wednesday slates of weeks 1 and 12 — the two independent derivations of the calendar agree, now a stack pin), 0 stats, 0 enqueues; the re-run: 0 inserted / 0 updated / 272 unchanged, 18 weeks unchanged. **Then RESTORED** (the safer default the task named): the 272 rows deleted by the nflverse id shape, the 18 bounds NULLed, census `nfl_games 0 / weeks non-NULL 0 / score_fanout 0` — pgTAP 003's NULL pin is untouched. "Retroactive back-fill of weeks already played" is vacuous at land time (the opener is 2026-09-09); when the cohort's first weeks are back-filled after the fact, `last_game_ends_at` stamps at the RUN instant per D303(4)'s rule (informational until a consumer exists) — recorded, not hidden. **(10) Proofs + probes as run.** Unit `nflverse-provider.test.ts` **44** (csv strictness; the ten conversion literals + offset read + malformed refusals; team map + refusal; fixture parse 94 rows; renamed-column refusal; `getSchedule(2026)` 77 games with stored literal rows; status set; REG-only with the 2025 WC row dropped and the 16 finals; zero-season refusal; empty `gametime` → null kickoff counted; game states; the `[]`-with-reason pair; `toGameRow` literal; idempotency 0/0/77; E42 one-row diff `2026-09-14T00:20Z`; day-move; result→final; inactives KC/ARI literal with the two OL drops named; the three empty/anomaly reasons; LA roster mapping; roster header refusal; merge table; composite merge + delegation; the transport's 404 message + the pinned URLs). Stack `nflverse-backfill-db.test.ts` **5** (golden 77/5 with literals + the 039 cross-check + zero stat/queue writes; idempotent re-sync; E42 real edition CHI@CAR 1:00→8:20 moves one row and not the week; the opener moved ONE minute moves `first_kickoff_at` and back; a posted result → `final` with `last_game_ends_at` NULL); fixtures restored by id + the restore asserted. **DoD probe** — `easternOffsetMinutesAt` hard-coded to 240 (every instant EDT): **9 of 49 RED** — six EST literals (`expected '2026-11-01T17:00:00.000Z' to be '…T18:00…'`), the offset read (`240 to be 300`), the `getSchedule` literal row, and the stack golden (`2026_08_BAL_BUF` kickoff) — reverted, sha identical before/after, 49/49. A first cut of the probe (hard-coding only the second offset step) redded ONE test because the round-trip guard fell back to the correct first guess — replaced by the function-level mangle and said (D267). **D3 fence probe:** `new Date(Date.now())` at `publishedAt` → 1 lint error at 359:34 (`src/lib/leagues/**` already covers the new directory), reverted. Full chain: `npm run test` **165 files / 3,132 tests, all passed** (L.D2.1 recorded 163 / 3,083 — +2 / +49 = exactly the two new suites; stack up, first attempt) · `test:db` **58 files / 3,854 asserts, PASS** (pgTAP 003's NULL pin green after both stack suites ran) · `test:gate` **24/24** · type-check clean · lint 0 · `database.ts` diff empty · stack census after: `nfl_games 0 / nfl_weeks 2026 non-NULL 0 / score_fanout 0 / syn players 0`. **(11) Residuals.** (a) `nfl_games` has no `source` column and `nfl_games.status` has no CHECK — **F219** (the schema lane's call). (b) The composite fetches the 2 MB games file per poll — F216 carries the memo note. (c) `getInjuries` is deliberately empty on this adapter; `injuries_2026.csv` does not exist yet anyway. **2026-09-01 — Architect (the M4 in-season task breakdown, `docs/specs/tasks-M4-inseason.md`; branch `docs/tasks-M4-inseason`; **DOCS ONLY** — no code, no schema, no spec text touched; takes **D287**; files **Q29**, the Q28 M4-live addendum, and **F210–F212**; reserves **D288–D301** for the breakdown's §3 decisions, which enter this section verbatim when Chris merges the PR — the tasks-M2/M3 precedent)**
- **D301 — Retire-and-succeed (F31/F1) lands in M4, and the FAAB clause is vacuously complete.** The `remove_manager(retire)` P0001 refusal (D42) becomes the real §7.2.1(b) outcome: seal the franchise (`teams.status='retired'`, `retired_at_week` from the league's current week), spin the successor into the slot, link `successor_team_id`, inherit roster (`league_rosters` re-point) and W-L record for seeding math only (`team_week_results` attribution rules recorded in-task), write `end_reason='seat_retired'`, and reject succession CYCLES in-body (**F1**, same PR). FAAB inheritance: no FAAB balance exists before M5's waiver build, so "inherits FAAB" is vacuously satisfied and M5's L.D2 adds the one-line transfer when the column is born — stated in the row flip, not left implicit.

---
- **D300 — Ingestion writes everything the jobs read; the delta queue only ever sees real changes.** L.D2.1 extends the ingestion path (the `sync-live` seam): `getSchedule` upserts `nfl_games` (idempotent, diff-aware) and maintains `nfl_weeks.first_kickoff_at`/`last_game_ends_at` (F9's columns — live-updated at last); `getWeekStats` upserts `player_stats` incl. the NEW `advanced` JSONB (C59) with **injected time on `updated_at`** (the D12 replay-determinism seam, already refactored in M0); unchanged rows are skipped and only real deltas enqueue to `score_fanout` (§23.2). Provider outage → after 3 failed polls the `stats_degraded` flag raises (a small flag surface the UI banner reads; never wrong numbers, E45). **F13 dispositioned here (its row names the M4 Architect): non-`'sleeper'` `source` values are CORRECT** — fixture/synthetic ingestion writes `source: provider.name` so a row's provenance is always honest; the gate's zero-real-data claim is asserted BY that column (`source = 'synthetic'` for every gate-written row), which turns F13's worry into the gate's own instrument.
- **D299 — Gate architecture: two gate tasks, the plan's order is the build order.** L.D6.3 is the synthetic gate (`test:gate:m4` = gate-m4.sh composing the M4 suites + `test:gate:m3` chain): 100 seeded leagues across a settings matrix (sizes 8–16 · h2h/total_points · median on/off · second_opponent on/off · divisions 1/2 · strict/lax locks · parity templates + a §7.3.3.1 custom-fork league), each §23.6 scenario asserted at LEAGUE level per D295's map, zero external calls. L.D6.4 is the real-replay gate: **calendar-blocked on the first recorded 2026 week (F10's ops window)**; cent-exactness proven against **hand-computed fixtures** (≥ 2 leagues × all teams × the full week, computed by hand on paper into stored literals — the D62 discipline — plus per-position spot checks), lock instants asserted against recorded kickoffs, Remix walked with its D290 posture. **The flexed-game clause (C55): asserted on the first recorded week that CONTAINS a kickoff move** — recorded reality decides which week that is; if the chosen replay week lacks one, the lock-move assertion runs additionally against the earliest recorded week that has one (E42's mechanism is evaluation-time reads, which a recorded move exercises exactly).
- **D298 — Where F167's freshness question lands for in-season surfaces.** In-season member views (matchups, standings, activity, lineup lock state) get their freshness from the **`league:<id>` broadcast + refetch-on-event** — the one mechanism F167's own row names as prompt and event-driven — so the SE-era "an open view learns nothing" limitation does not propagate into the season surfaces. **This does NOT close F167**: the scoring-DOCUMENT editor/member-view mechanism (a pre-draft surface) remains the row's open decision, Chris's/SE's, untouched here. Recorded so the next reader knows M4 chose the broadcast lane deliberately, not by accident.
- **D297 — Standings are a computed read over `team_week_results`; the results table is derived and rebuildable.** `league_standings(league_id)` orders by the league's stored `tiebreakers` chain (§7.3.7): Win% → PF → H2H (clean two-team ties only — 3+ groups SKIP it, E63; `total_points` leagues skip it entirely, E64) → PA (higher wins, deliberate) → division record → seeded deterministic coin flip. `matchups` stays the pairing/score/override source of truth; `rebuild_team_week_results(league_id, week)` re-derives a week from `matchups` + lineups for corrections/overrides (§12.18's precedence note) and is the write door's rebuild path. Points For counts **once per week** regardless of median/second games (§11.7); E38 two-decimal ties are real ties; E39 exact-median = tie.
- **D296 — In-season realtime: one compact event per league per batch; F42 dispositioned per table.** New Broadcast-from-DB triggers on `league:<league_id>`: `matchups` (UPDATE — the coalesced `scores_updated` carrier), `team_week_results` (finalization), `transactions` (INSERT — the activity feed's subscriber arrives in M4), `league_weeks` (status flips — the "week is final" moment). Payloads column-selected, nothing blind (never scores-by-player, never claim data). Of F42's six: `league_weeks` + (via `transactions`' feed) the activity surface gain their subscribers here; **`league_members`/`team_managers`/`teams`/`league_invites`/`league_lists` still have NO M4 subscriber and are re-waived per table again** (pgTAP 024's pin updates to the shrunken set with the same message discipline). **F9 (nfl_weeks trigger): decided NO trigger** — locks are server-evaluated and clients read week state through `league_weeks` (which now broadcasts); `nfl_weeks` stays reference data with zero subscribers, pinned trigger-less with its reason. Clients refetch box-score lines on `scores_updated` (§11.4); **no Postgres Changes anywhere** (§9 doctrine).
- **D295 — The correction-window split (C54, decided).** M4 owns the SEMANTICS: (a) a post-final-game delta arriving **inside** the week's correction window flows through the same fan-out and recomputes non-final matchups (they display `final (pending corrections)` — `league_weeks.status = 'correction_window'`); (b) `finalize_matchups` runs only after `correction_window_ends_at` AND all games final (§23.2 — no league state advances on partial data), flips `league_weeks → final`, and from then on the write door **refuses** auto-recompute for that week — a post-window delta lands in `player_stats` but changes NO league cell (the §23.4 "not auto-applied" half, proven by the `correction_post_window` scenario). M6's L.E2 adds the DETECTION artifacts (`stat_correction_events`, the corrections view, the flagged commissioner-apply path). Two-phase/charted semantics ride the same rails: a rules key with no delivered stat is **pending, never 0** (E61 — the worker carries delivered-key bookkeeping so `charted_late` renders pending and `charted_revision` recomputes in-window).
- **D294 — Pool discipline (L.D5): derived truth + lazy rows, one serialization point.** A player with no `league_player_pool` row is `free_agent` if unowned (§12.19); rows are created on first transition. `rostered` rows mirror `league_rosters` and the mirror is ASSERTED, not trusted — the reconciliation job (L.D2.3) checks it nightly, and the sim sweep checks it after every scenario. `roster_add_drop` is SECURITY DEFINER, locks the **league row** first (the house lock-order law: `leagues` before anything), then validates: exclusivity (072's unique — a friendly refusal, never a raw 23505), roster capacity, **E32 game-day locks** (`player_game_lock` on ⇒ add AND drop refuse from that player's kickoff until the week's `correction_window_ends_at`, evaluated per D291), waiver state (an `on_waivers` player with `waivers_until` in the future refuses; a lapsed `waivers_until` is FCFS-addable per `free_agency` — state evaluated at read, no sweeper needed in M4), acquisition caps (`acquisitions_per_week`/`per_season` counted from `transactions`), `fa_hold_hours` (an early drop of a held FA add returns the player to FA, not waivers), and dropped players enter `on_waivers` with `waivers_until = now + waiver_period_hours` (`none_fcfs` ⇒ straight to FA). Every executed move writes a `transactions` row (`type='add_drop'`) in the same txn. **Claim PROCESSING, FAAB, bench_lock (E33), priority orders — all M5**; the pool's state vocabulary ships complete so M5 adds writers, not columns.
- **D293 — Lineup law.** `slot_map` (`"<slot_key>:<index>" → player_id`, §12.13) is the canonical lineup representation everywhere; `starters`/`bench` JSONB stay as derived render state written in the same txn. `set_lineup` validates in-body: membership/ownership (or commissioner), every started player rostered by the team, **bipartite slot-fit** (E16 — each player fills exactly one slot; augmenting-path over ≤ ~10 starters, implemented in the RPC), per-slot eligibility from `roster_settings.starting_slots[].eligible`, lock state per `lineup_lock` (locked slots read-only — a change touching a locked slot refuses with the player and kickoff named; unlocked slots of the same lineup remain editable), `allow_illegal_lineups` semantics (TRUE: byes/OUT start and score 0, flagged; FALSE: blocked at submit). **IR enforcement lands here** (the columns already exist on `league_rosters`, 072): placement requires an eligible designation; Restricted sets `ir_lock_until_week = ir_placed_week + min_weeks` and early removal refuses (commissioner override is M6's). **Auto-carry is materialized by `league_week_advance` at week open**: the new week's row is written from last week's legal lineup (invalid/bye players kept and flagged, never silently dropped) so lock/scoring/UI all read explicit rows — no lazy "which week does this row mean" inference.
- **D292 — `score-league-week` is a TS worker, because the calculator is TS and one-implementation is LAW (D33/D57); its writes go through ONE SQL door.** The worker is a pure module (`src/lib/leagues/scoring/score-week-worker.ts`-shaped) with injected `TimeProvider`, provider-fed stats rows, and a service client; it drains `score_fanout` in batches, maps player deltas → affected (league, team) via the new `league_rosters(player_id)` index ∩ in-season leagues, recomputes affected teams **through the real pipeline — `resolveRules(snapshot, position)` with `deriveTierIndicators` composed BEFORE `scorePlayerWeek` (discharging F23 at the production call site, with the composition PINNED)** — and stores **JS-rounded** (`roundHalfUp`) totals so no path lets the DB round a divergent value (discharging **F22**). Writes land through one SECURITY DEFINER RPC (`score_write_week_batch`) that revalidates in-body: league in `in_season|playoffs`, week not `final`, **never a `final` matchup, never an overridden cell** (§22.2's rule), one coalesced write + one broadcast per league per batch. **Queue vehicle: a plain `score_fanout` table drained with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`** — pgmq does not exist on this stack (survey §6) and §22.3's claim pattern is already the house pattern; §22.2's "pgmq" is a vehicle erratum folded when built (C51, the D87 precedent). **Corrupt-snapshot posture (the F23 decision, made): quarantine the LEAGUE, never the batch** — a snapshot that makes `scorePlayerWeek` throw marks that league's week scoring-blocked (a loud worker-error row + skip), other leagues' batches proceed, and nothing writes a partial or zero score for the broken league (CLAUDE.md's "never let nothing-happened mean it-worked": absence of a score with a named reason, never a plausible 0.00).
- **D291 — Time discipline for in-season machinery: in-database jobs take `p_now`, TS takes TimeProvider.** Every M4 job RPC (`lineup_lock_tick`, `league_week_advance`, `finalize_matchups`) is an in-database RPC on pg_cron (the D87/draft-tick precedent — no Edge Function) whose signature is `(p_now timestamptz DEFAULT now())`: production cron passes nothing; the harness/sim passes the virtual instant, generalizing the `rewindDeadline` pattern into the front door instead of a column hack. Kickoff-derived locks are **always evaluated from `nfl_games.kickoff_at` at evaluation time** (§23.3 — never precomputed per lineup; `league_player_pool.locked_until` is maintained state for the POOL, refreshed by `lineup_lock_tick` each run, so a moved kickoff moves the lock, E42). All TS in-season code reads time only via TimeProvider (the M0 ESLint fence already enforces it).
- **D290 — Interim audit posture for post-kickoff Remix/matchup edits (the M3 F40 precedent, applied).** `commissioner_actions` is M6's table (Phase E). Until it lands: post-kickoff Remix and any manual matchup edit **require a `reason`**, refuse to touch `live`/`final` weeks (§11.7's own law), and post the D97 in-transaction system chat message (which §11.7 requires non-disableably anyway); **F40's control list GROWS** with `schedule_remix_confirm` + `schedule_edit_matchup` so M6 wires the audit rows. Free-window Remix (before the league's first kickoff, evaluated from `nfl_games.kickoff_at` at call time — E41) needs no reason. Recorded honestly in the PR body: "Remix diff/confirm audited" in the M4 gate means THIS posture plus the system post, not `commissioner_actions` rows.
- **D289 — The schedule engine lives in SQL, one implementation, exhaustively testable.** `league_generate_schedule(league_id)` implements §11.7's circle-method round-robin with a **deterministic seeded permutation** (explicit integer LCG/hash on `schedule_seed` — never `setseed()`/`random()`, which are session-scoped), divisions-2× preference, cycling with balanced repeats (max spread 1, repeat ≥ 3 weeks after first meeting), `second_opponent` per-week derangements materialized as `round_type = 'secondary'` rows, `median_game` as computation-only (results land in `team_week_results` at finalization, never matchup rows), and `total_points` generating **no matchups**. Remix preview is the same generator run WITHOUT writing (a function returning the proposed set + diff as jsonb); confirm re-generates from the previewed seed in-body and applies atomically. `schedule_seed` joins the settings catalog (stored on `leagues.settings`, §11.7). v1's team counts are a closed set (8/10/12/14/16 — §19.1), so pgTAP covers **every size exhaustively** and the plan-§4.1 property row ("schedule invariants over random seeds/team counts") runs as a seeded sweep through the real RPC over the wire — one implementation, no TS mirror, no parity burden.
- **D288 — A league week IS an NFL week; the schema already says so.** 056:70's `FOREIGN KEY (season, week) REFERENCES nfl_weeks(season, week)` binds `league_weeks` to the NFL calendar, and §7.3.1's `playoff_start_week ≤ 16` / "weeks 1–18" arithmetic assumes the identity. M4 keeps the identity: `matchups.week`, `team_week_results.week`, and every job key are NFL weeks. For a league entering `in_season` before NFL week 1 (every 2027 GA league) the spec reads exactly as printed. **For a league entering MID-season — the 2026 test cohort's actual life — the spec was silent; C50/Q29 is now RULED (Chris, 2026-09-01, at approval): the recommendation stands as law** (league's first week = the next NFL week whose first kickoff is still ahead at `in_season` entry; the settings validator shrinks/refuses season length so first week + regular season + playoff span end ≤ 18). L.D1.2 and everything downstream build to his ruling; the GATES are unaffected either way (the harness seeds leagues before its replayed week).

- **D282 — SC.3 build mechanics: the preselection as a pure DERIVATION (never a draft write), the ONE product-shape consequence flagged (the style step opens on No PPR), the B.5 card trim, and the shared-stack cross-lane finding every parallel builder should read.**
  **(2) THE PRESELECTION IS A DERIVED VALUE, NOT A DRAFT WRITE.** `WizardDraft.scoringSystemId` / `MockLaunchDraft.scoringSystemId` keep their explicit-pick-only semantics (init stays `null` — the F186 line numbers moved, the meaning did not): the mounts derive `effective = explicit ?? resolveDefaultTemplateId(rows)` at render (`effectiveTemplateSelection`, ONE rule in picker-ops shared by both league-less mounts) and hand the default into the submit builders (`toCreateInput(draft, defaultId)` / `toMockLaunchInput(draft, defaultId)` — new optional param, every payload still carries an EXPLICIT template id; `create_league`/`create_mock_draft` know nothing of preselection, D170's birth predicate untouched). No effect, no setState, no load-order race, and "explicit always wins" is structural rather than promised — with the edges pinned anyway (four-combo pins in both ops suites; render pin that `value` is law). **Resolution is by NATURAL KEY** (`name === 'Scout Scoring'` within the `is_template` fetch — the 058/106 seeds' partial-UNIQUE key; a uuid differs per environment) and a loaded row-set WITHOUT Scout degrades LOUDLY: `console.warn` naming migration 106, null default, and the surfaces fall back to the designed pre-SC.3 explicit-pick gates ("Pick a scoring template…" — what renders instead is stated and pinned, never a silent un-default). The settings mount never touches the resolver (pinned): a league's STORED reference is never defaulted over. `useScoringTemplates` gains an `enabled` option so the two dialogs — both mounted-closed on Home/leagues pages — don't fetch until opened; the hook's stale "6 v1 parity rows" docblock corrected in passing (F193's species, disclosed here).
  **(3) THE ONE VISIBLE PRODUCT-SHAPE CONSEQUENCE, flagged rather than improvised silently (the D277(3) posture): the wizard's style step now OPENS ON "No PPR".** §7.3.3's system-default bullet mandates the scoring step open with Scout preselected and the Scout card leading — and Scout is no-PPR **by ruling** (a STATED difference, B.5). The style step's old `'ppr'` default would have filtered the preselected card out of view: a selection the user cannot see is the CLAUDE.md "nothing happened" shape, worse than no default.
