> **(1) THE UNIFYING SHAPE, because these are six findings and one idea.** Every item in this round is **prose claiming more than the code beneath it** — the same class SE.6's own review round (D275(11)) named, arriving one level up: not a docblock over-claiming about a construction, but a docblock over-claiming about a TEST, a ledger row over-claiming about a TIMER, and a correction over-claiming about the thing it corrected. The rung this adds: **a correction is an assertion too, and it is the assertion nobody re-measures.** D275(2)'s replacement for the withdrawn *"up to ten minutes"* — *"a later mount refetches regardless"* — was written by a review that had just caught a wrong figure, and was itself wrong, and then propagated into E81, into two hook docblocks and into the permanent squash-commit title on `main`. **When you withdraw a figure, the replacement gets the same probe the original should have had.**
>
> **(2) F171 — A SOURCE PIN OVER AN ENUMERATED SET PINS ITS MEMBERS, NEVER ITS MEMBERSHIP.** `use-league-scoring-invalidation.test.ts`'s R666 cell said *"A fifth writer added without a line here is the defect this cell exists to catch."* **Measured false.** The cell iterates a literal `['useForkScoringTemplate','useUpdateLeagueScoring','useUpdateLeagueSettings']` and greps each body; a fifth writer appended to `use-league.ts` that PATCHes `{ scoring_system_id }` and invalidates only `leaguesKeys.detail` is **green** on the target suite, on the full unit lane and on `tsc --noEmit`, because no assertion ever asks the file what its writers ARE. **What the cell DOES guard is removal**, and that is real: deleting the shipped `invalidateLeagueScoring(queryClient, leagueId)` from `useUpdateLeagueSettings` reds exactly that cell — **1 failed | 8 passed** (probe A, below). The comment now says both halves, and the test's own NAME is changed from *"EVERY writer …"* to *"each of the three ENUMERATED writers …"*, because leaving the false claim in the headline while fixing the comment under it is the very defect F174 records. The name is referenced nowhere else (`grep -rn "EVERY writer of the league scoring document"` → that one line).
>
> **THE DERIVED-SET FIX WAS FLOATED AT THE GATE AND IS REFUSED ON MEASUREMENT, which matters more than the reword.** Deriving the writer list by grepping bodies for `scoring_system_id` would **(a)** miss `useCreateLeague` outright — it lives in **`src/hooks/use-leagues.ts:79`**, a file this pin never opens — and **(b)** reach `useUpdateLeagueSettings`, *the exact writer R666 was about*, **only through a comment**: within `bodyOf`'s slice (`use-league.ts:116–154`) the sole `scoring_system_id` is prose at `:146`, while the real wire field is at `:105` in `UpdateLeagueSettingsBody`, **outside** the slice. A derivation satisfied by prose is **D274/F159's defect wearing a fix's name**. The honest arrangement is what ships: a removal-guard in the test, and an explicit prescription in `use-league.ts`'s docblock (*"Adding a fifth writer means adding it here"*) that is honest **as a prescription** and makes no claim about a test.
>
> **(3) F173 — WHAT ACTUALLY BOUNDS THE STALENESS: NOTHING. Measured against the INSTALLED `@tanstack/query-core` 5.96.1** with a virtual clock (`Date.now` patched) and the browser branch forced via the library's own `environmentManager.setIsServer(() => false)`, using the production options (`staleTime: 10 * 60 * 1000`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, no `refetchInterval`, no `gcTime`):
>
> | probe | result |
> |---|---|
> | mounted, 60 virtual minutes, nothing focuses/reconnects/polls | **fetches 1 → 1** |
> | closed 4 min, reopened (data 4 min old) | **fetches 1 → 1**, entry still present |
> | 15 × 4-minute close/reopen cycles | **5 fetches**, on cycles 0, 3, 6, 9, 12 |
> | closed past `gcTime` (entry evicted), reopened | **fetches 1 → 2** |
>
> **Read at source rather than inferred:** `queryObserver.js` gates `refetchOnMount`, `refetchOnReconnect` and `refetchOnWindowFocus` **alike** through `shouldFetchOn → isStale → query.isStaleByTime(staleTime)`; `shouldFetchOnMount` short-circuits to an unconditional load **only while `query.state.data === undefined`**, i.e. only once the entry is gone; and `#updateStaleTimeout` calls `this.updateResult()` — it re-renders, it never fetches. So **a room closed and reopened inside 5 minutes over data younger than 10 minutes does NOT refetch**, and *"a later mount refetches regardless"* is withdrawn at all four sites (`use-league.ts`, `use-draft-pool.ts`, spec **E81** → **v2.16.8**, and D275(2) itself). So is *"Ten minutes overstated the closed case"* — it did not; the closed case has no bound either. **The `removable.js` quotation was mis-transcribed too** and is fixed to the real line: `newGcTime ?? (environmentManager.isServer() ? Infinity : 5 * 60 * 1e3)`.
>
> **The nuance is kept rather than traded for a cleaner sentence:** repeated close/reopen cycles **do** eventually refresh once the data crosses `staleTime`. The correct claim is therefore **"no timer guarantees a bound"** — never *"nothing ever refreshes"*, which would be the next wrong correction. **The gate's own figure for this was `~6` fetches over 15 cycles; re-measured here it is `5`.** It is stated as measured rather than inherited precisely because inheriting a number is what produced this whole round.
>
> **(4) F172 — THE ROW SE.9 ACTUALLY READS WAS THE LAST PLACE THE WITHDRAWN FIGURE WAS LOAD-BEARING.** Ledger **F167** was byte-identical across the entire SE.6 delta (md5 unchanged at `78bd6cc` and `e1819c7`), stated `staleTime` as "the bound" **three times including in its headline**, and cited **D275(2)** — the entry that retracts it — as its source. Worse, it handed SE.9 *"a `staleTime` change is the cheap answer"*: a **measured no-op** for the case the row is about, since `staleTime` is consulted only by a mount, a reconnect or a focus event and this app disables the third — lowering it changes nothing for a view that stays mounted and connected. The row's headline, body and hand-off are corrected, and the hand-off now names the three things that actually move an OPEN view (the §9.3 `league:<id>` broadcast; an explicit `refetchInterval`; re-enabling focus refetch on that surface) with their real costs. **A hand-off is the highest-leverage prose in this file, and it is the prose least likely to be re-read by the session that wrote it.**

The one at 10–11 is **wrapped across a line break** (`… for up to ten\n * minutes …`), which a naive `grep -n "ten minutes"` **cannot see**. So the rule, stated as a rule: **a withdrawn figure needs a WRAP-TOLERANT, CASE-INSENSITIVE, repo-wide sweep, run at the END of the change and reported with its output** — not a line-oriented grep for the phrase as you remember typing it. > **(7) THE SWEEP, MEASURED THREE WAYS, AND WHAT ITS ZERO MEANS.** Occurrence counts **of the withdrawn figure** on `main` @ `d1e0e9e`, repo-wide over tracked files (every row below quotes the retracted phrase — that is the point of the table, and the reason the invariant at the end of this item is what it is):

> | `git grep -Iiho "ten minutes"` — the phrase as you remember typing it | **12** | 5 |
> | `git grep -IihoE "ten[ -]minute"` — hyphen-aware, still line-oriented | **15** | **2** |
> | wrap-tolerant, over the whole byte stream: `/ten[\s\*\/#>\|_-]{0,12}minute/i` per file | **17** | 0 |

> **The two the hyphen-aware grep still misses are line WRAPS** — `use-league-scoring-invalidation.test.ts:10` (`… for up to ten\n * minutes …`) and `use-league.ts:348` — and one of them is the exact instance F174 was filed about. A sweep that is merely case-insensitive and hyphen-aware is **not** sufficient; it has to cross the newline. **Because the retraction sentences must themselves QUOTE the withdrawn figure, "zero occurrences" is not the achievable target and claiming it would be its own false claim.** The target is a **mechanical, checkable invariant**: *every surviving occurrence carries one of the literal markers `D276` / `RETRACTED` / `retracted` / `withdrawn` / `WITHDRAWN` within 300 characters*, so no reader can meet the figure without meeting its retraction in the same breath. The verification pass reports the occurrences that **VIOLATE** that invariant, and it is **0**. Both passes and their outputs are in the PR body.

Fixed: an empty DETAIL keys to `rules.`, a trailing empty segment, exactly as format 2 spells it. **And a false pin was corrected in passing, because discharging F138 while leaving it would be the worse outcome:** `validate-rules-doc.test.ts` asserted that a violation path *"never contains an empty segment"* — false, and green only because the corpus held no empty key. >
> | mutation of wall 3 | before this PR | after |
> |---|---|---|
> | *(control — no mutation)* | 93 / **0** | 93 / **0** |
> | lock deleted, no comment | 93 / **2** (A22 + K1) | 93 / **2** (A22 + K1) |
> | lock deleted **+ one prose line** `-- The reference is resolved WHERE s.id = NEW.scoring_system_id FOR SHARE (105 §5 / F147).` | 93 / **1 — A22 ALONE, K1 GREEN** | 93 / **2** (A22 + K1) |

A22 firing ALONE is therefore indistinguishable from ordinary churn, and the single cell that would have said *"the lock is gone"* said nothing. That is the exact hand-clearing window K1's own description says it exists to cover.

> **The fix is `regexp_replace(p.prosrc, '--[^\n]*', '', 'g')` on both cells** — line comments deleted, their newlines kept, so the multi-line anchors still span the statement (and an interleaved comment can no longer break a match either). It is **lossless ON THIS CORPUS — and that is a bounded claim, not a property of the technique (R662).** A `--` inside a STRING LITERAL is invisible to a line-based strip, so the strip can eat real code, and the direction it fails in is **masking on a BAN cell**: measured, a mutant carrying a genuinely banned lock and **no comment anywhere** — `RAISE NOTICE 'resolve -- step'; PERFORM 1 FROM public.scoring_systems s2 WHERE s2.id = NEW.scoring_system_id FOR UPDATE;` on one line — is **93 / 2 pre-fix (K2 correctly RED) and 93 / 1 post-fix (K2 GREEN)**. **It is unreachable today, and that is the claim that is defensible:** a SQL-aware lexer (single-quoted, dollar-quoted, quoted-identifier and nestable `/* */` aware) run over **all 124 `public` function bodies read from `pg_proc`** and over **all 245 dollar-quoted bodies in the 98 `supabase/migrations/*.sql` files** finds **zero** `--` inside any literal and **zero** `/* */` blocks, and the naive strip is **byte-identical to the lexer's output for all 369 bodies**. So: no permit cell can be defeated by this (a strip that removes real code makes a permit FAIL, not pass), and no ban cell can be masked by it **unless a body first grows a `--` inside a literal on the same line as the banned construct** — which nothing in the repo does. Every real mutation that red a cell before still reds it after.

> **(1) F147 — THE LOCK GOT WEAKER, AND THAT IS THE STRONGER ANSWER.** 104 shipped `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` and said in its own body that the STRENGTH was SE.5's to choose once a write pattern existed to measure it against. Measured, with `scoring_update_rules` in place:
> **(a) equally protective.** The seam — T1 makes an UNREFERENCED flat row invalid (wall 1 passes: outside the profile), T2 repoints a live league at it — run in BOTH orderings with the F21 double-pay PAIR as the invalid document (each key ALONE is legal, so the probe measures the defect and not the names): `FOR SHARE` refused both, `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` refused both, and **a no-lock control BREACHED both**. That control is what makes the other two rows evidence rather than decoration; without it "refused" is equally consistent with a race that never happened. The protective DIRECTION survives the weakening: a racing rules-UPDATE blocks for the holder's full duration (2017.9 ms under `FOR SHARE`, 1973.7 ms under `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`).
> **(b) the contention is on the hottest path in the product.** Wall 3's highest-frequency writer is `create_league`, whose INSERT arm locks the referenced row — and there are exactly **six** template rows, so every league creation in the app contends on one of six. **The axis is CONCURRENCY**: for each level W, W concurrent workers each issue 20 `create_league` calls against the same template row; the figure is mean ms/call, elapsed taken inside the database. Two reps per arm — `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` at W = 1/2/4/6/8/10 → **0.60 / 0.93 / 1.50 / 1.95 / 2.46 / 2.96 ms** (rep 2: 0.85/1.02/1.55/1.91/2.41/2.94); `FOR SHARE` → **0.85 / 0.70 / 0.66 / 0.74 / 0.82 / 0.81** (rep 2: 0.55/0.65/0.66/0.68/0.69/0.76). **`FOR NO KEY UPDATE` rises monotonically; `FOR SHARE` is flat.** That, not any single ratio, is the claim: each additional concurrent creator adds one full call to every other creator's wait, so the gap grows without bound in W (2.6× at W=6, 3.7× at W=10).
> **[RELABELLED 2026-08-26, review R647 — the correction this row exists to carry, because this block is the standing justification for weakening a security wall.** The first form printed `20/37/53/70/88/104 ms` beside `19/19/19/19/19/19` as though both were six comparable per-worker figures at a fixed W=6. They were the sorted **drain cascade** at one level — within a level the strong lock's per-worker elapsed is `[11 23 33 44 54 64]` at W=6 while `FOR SHARE` is `[13 13 13 14 14 14]` — and printing them side by side invited exactly the reading two reviewers gave them. Its headline "~5.5× at 6-way" was `104/19`: the last element of a cascade over a flat value, not a like-for-like ratio. **Nothing about the decision changes; the evidence for it is now stated on the axis it actually varies.** And the early 8-way run "discarded as `docker exec` startup noise" — justified in outcome, sloppy in process, because a discarded measurement needs a stated exclusion rule **or** a re-measurement and it had neither — now has the second: the sweep reaches **W=8 and W=10 and the sign holds in both reps**.]**
> **(c) the multixact trade, measured rather than named.** `FOR SHARE` is a SHARED lock, so concurrent holders go through a multixact. That it really happens is not assumed: `pg_get_multixact_members(s.xmax::text::xid)` → **`1454180/sh, 1454182/sh`**. Its COST is inside the **flat ~0.7 ms `FOR SHARE`** row of the W = 1..10 sweep in (b) above — it does not show up at this shape — **[repointed 2026-08-26, D274/R-item 3: this read "inside that 19 ms", and R647 had already retracted the 19 ms figure one bullet earlier without sweeping its own back-references, leaving a withdrawn number carrying the claim]** — and the risk it carries (member-space pressure) needs long-lived overlapping sharers, while every wall-3 writer in this repo is a short RPC transaction that releases at commit. **If a long-running league-write transaction is ever introduced, this is the thing to re-measure.**
> **(d) why it is safe to weaken at all — and the framing is the REVIEWERS', adopted because it is better than the one shipped.** Do not argue from the strength ordering; argue from the **conflict table**. Wall 3's premise is exactly *"the row I just resolved does not change under me."* `FOR SHARE` conflicts with `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` **and** `FOR UPDATE` — precisely the locks an UPDATE and a DELETE of that row acquire — so **every writer is excluded and the premise holds**. What `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` additionally excluded was *other wall-3 invocations, which are readers and cannot invalidate each other's premise.* **That extra exclusion buys nothing and costs the serialization.** Two transactions attaching leagues to the same VALID document is not a breach in any ordering.
>
> **(2) F151 — THE COVERAGE, AND THE CONTROL THAT MAKES IT MEAN SOMETHING.** F151's argument for deferral was true only until this task: no server function did DML on `scoring_systems`, so the reverse-order leg could not be assembled. `scoring_update_rules` assembles it. Swept: **0 deadlocks over 40 rounds across five interleavings** — save‖attach in both orderings, save‖raw-rules-UPDATE in both orderings, and all three at once — **and an inverted-order control pair that deadlocks 8/8.** A sweep that reports zero without a control that can produce a non-zero reports nothing. The structural premises underneath are pinned in 053 §G rather than left in prose: **wall 1 takes NO row lock** (its arm (c) is a bare `EXISTS` — F148's correction, now falsifiable: adding a `FOR` clause reds G1 and one cell in 052), and **all three league-writing RPCs lock `leagues` before `scoring_systems`**, one global order.
> **[AMENDED 2026-08-26, review R644 — "one direction" was true of PL/pgSQL and was stated as true of the system.** `leagues_scoring_system_id_fkey` is `ON DELETE NO ACTION`, so a DELETE of a referenced `scoring_systems` row locks the scoring row **first** and then takes `FOR KEY SHARE` on the referencing `leagues` row: the reverse direction, run by RI machinery that appears in no `prosrc` — the only place §G's cells can look. **SE.5 is what makes it reachable**, because §2 is the first thing in the chain to put an owner-owned, hence owner-DELETABLE, row in front of a live league; before 105 the reference was always an ownerless template `authenticated` cannot delete. Reviewers reproduced it deterministically and at concurrency (14/120 and 22/120 legitimate saves aborted with 40P01). **Deliberately NOT defended against, and that is a ruling rather than an omission:** the DELETE that opens it is refused by the FK itself 100% of the time (23503) — the only shape that deadlocks had **zero successes in 120 rounds**, so it fails on its first single-threaded test rather than flaking in production — 40P01 is a transient retryable abort with no partial write, no DELETE route exists, and §12.25's own hygiene case (deleting an ORPHANED fork) takes no RI lock at all. An `ON DELETE RESTRICT`-shaped guard would be new surface on a security wall to defend against a statement that already fails: CLAUDE.md's *"no defending against personal problems"*. **The transferable half: a catalog pin over `prosrc` cannot see the RI lock graph and must not claim to.**]**
> **The first run of that sweep reported 50 errors per 10 rounds and zero deadlocks, and the zero was worthless:** a shell variable holding the scoring-system id was empty, so the harness had been running `invalid input syntax for type uuid: ""` instead of the statements it described. It is recorded because "0 deadlocks" and "0 statements executed" look identical in the output — CLAUDE.md's rule, in the measuring instrument rather than in the product.

> **(3) SE.5(3) — THE REACHABILITY ASSUMPTION, RE-DERIVED INSTEAD OF INHERITED.** Every "not reachable today" in 104, D272 and F142/F151 rested on `leagues` being SELECT-only to clients AND both attach RPCs restricting `p_scoring_system_id` to `is_template = TRUE AND owner_id IS NULL`. **D169's arm removes exactly the second half.** The re-derivation is a pin, not a paragraph (053 §G4/§G5): a fork row is in wall 1's profile by **two arms at once** — it carries a `format` member (arm b) AND it is live-league-referenced (arm c) — and the commissioner's own raw 001:623 `FOR ALL` write to it, the route this task newly makes reachable against a league-referenced row, is **REFUSED at the table**. Two arms matter because arm (c) alone lapses on detach and arm (b) alone would lapse if a future fork ever wrote a flat document. **What SE.5 opens is "a user-writable row in front of a league", not "a corruptible one".**

> **(4) THE IDEMPOTENCY KEY IS WIDER THAN IT LOOKS, DELIBERATELY.** §12.25 forbids a new column, so `scoring_fork_template` has no `action_id` and dedupes on STATE: the league already references a non-template row whose `rules` deep-equal the document this call would build, **owned by a commissioner of this league** — not `owner_id = auth.uid()`. `is_league_commish` admits co_commissioners, so under the narrower-looking predicate a co-commissioner's RETRY misses the test and mints a duplicate row. The tighter predicate is the one with the retry-safety hole. Pinned at 053 §C14, and the same predicate is used by `scoring_update_rules` so both RPCs agree on what "the league's own fork row" means. **[AMENDED 2026-08-26, review R639 — this sentence ASSERTED the save side while only the fork side was pinned, a direct violation of the standing rule this same PR adopted at §(20).** Narrowing the SAVE's predicate alone to `= auth.uid()` red **nothing**, while the capability demonstrably regressed: a co-commissioner could no longer save the league's own fork, and the refusal told them the row "is not this league's own forked custom row" — false and unactionable. The `lives_ok` now exists at **053 §C15** and reds under exactly that mutant. **The transferable half: a predicate SHARED between two functions needs a `lives_ok` on BOTH sides — sharing it is precisely what makes a single pin look sufficient.**]**

> **(5) THE SAVE REFUSES UN-NORMALIZED DOCUMENTS RATHER THAN NORMALIZING THEM**, and the reason is not tidiness: §7.3.3.1 makes the All-Positions switch state **derived from the document**, so a server-side strip would change what the editor renders on the next load with no error and no diff — CLAUDE.md's "nothing happened" class, in the one place a commissioner would never think to check. Guardrail 4 already lives inside `scoring_rules_validate`, so the RPC does not need a clause; it needs to not swallow the one that exists. §D8 is the control that keeps §D7 honest: the same override with a DIFFERENT value is accepted by the same call on the same row.

The validation arm is the **only** check in `update_league_settings` on a same-row re-attach, because step 6's re-freeze does not fire when the reference is unchanged. §F6 proves it works independently of wall 3 by refusing **with wall 3 still disabled**, and the verdict carries where the exception was raised so "the attach arm refused" is measured rather than inferred.

> **(7) FOUR DEFECTS IN MY OWN SUITE, ALL FOUND BY RUNNING THE PROBES BEFORE CLAIMING GREEN.** Two are new shapes worth carrying forward. **(a) `count(*)` ELIDES THE CALL:** §B4–§B6 refused documents through `select count(*) from (select f(x)) q` and every cell reported `1 rows` — the planner drops an unreferenced subquery output column, so the function was never invoked and three refusal pins were vacuous against a function that raises. > **(11) THE FIX ROUND (review R638–R650: 21 claims tested, 17 survived, 4 killed; MERGE-WITH-FOLLOWUPS, no blockers). THE GENERALISATION IS THE NEXT RUNG ABOVE D272(20), AND IT IS SHARPER THAN EITHER PREVIOUS ONE.**
>
> > **In a defence-in-depth design where every layer raises the same error family, an assertion on the OUTCOME cannot localize.** SE.4b round 1: vacuity sits on permissive branches. Round 2 (D272(20)): the suite pins what the guards *do*, not what determines *whether* they run. **SE.5: the suite pins THAT the system refused, not WHICH layer refused — and six cells had an observable alphabet coarser than the distinction their own text claimed to make.**
>
> The count, because the shape is only visible in aggregate: **R638** — the alphabet was `left(sqlerrm, 44)` and the discriminator lives at character **66**, so three `scoring_update_rules` refusals were one byte-identical string and two guards had zero mutation coverage. **R646** — the alphabet was `(SQLSTATE, HINT)` and two arms of the *same function* emit the same pair (delete the no-PA-keys guard and `'{}' <@ anything` is TRUE for both families, so the *ambiguity* arm raises with the identical hint). **R641** — same alphabet, and the RPC's own `PERFORM` and wall 1 behind it emit the same SQLSTATE, HINT **and MESSAGE**, because they call the same validator. **R640** — the alphabet was "outsider reads 0 rows", and three independent tables' RLS all produce 0. **R639** — no assertion at all on the permissive arm, so the alphabet was empty. **And §D2, which this task had already found and fixed in its own probe sweep, was the same thing.**
>
> **Why it is systematic rather than sloppy, which is the part worth carrying:** the architecture that makes SE.5 safe is exactly the architecture that makes it untestable by outcome. Front-door RPC, wall 1, wall 3, RLS and CHECK constraints deliberately converge on the same P0001 families with the same messages — that convergence is a **feature** (one user-facing error however you arrive at it, which is why TS↔SQL guardrail parity is pinned byte-for-byte) and the suite inherited it without inheriting a way to see through it. **Any future task adding a guard behind an existing wall reproduces this defect unless the helper discriminates by construction.**
>
> **The fix was three lines and it was already in the file.** `pg_temp.attach` read `pg_exception_context` and reported a `raised_in:` token; it was applied to one helper of three. Swept to all of them (plus a shared uuid-stripping message widener, because 36 identical characters were eating the whole 44-char budget), every previously-vacuous cell now kills its mutant: **D4 · D5 · C15 · E3b · D7+D10 · B5**, control 71 ok / 0 red. Two of those cells are new (**C15** for R639, **E3b** for R640) and both were written the hard way: R640's *obvious* fixture — "give the outsider membership in a different live league" — is measured **non-killing** (053 already had it, as u5), so the working cell instead makes `leagues` and `league_members` temporarily world-readable so that §12.25's own identity clause is the only thing left standing.
>
> **(12) PATTERN 2, which the reviewers named and this task's banner had missed as a CATEGORY.** *105 is the first migration to put a user-owned, user-writable, user-DELETABLE `scoring_systems` row in front of a live league.* Three findings fall out of that one fact: user-**owned** → it enters an `owner_id` namespace two shipped readers treat as a one-row-per-user store (**F156**); user-**writable** → the §7.3 lifecycle window stops being structural and becomes an RPC-level check (**R645**); user-**deletable** → the FK's NO-ACTION RI check becomes reachable, closing a lock cycle (**R644**). §4's banner *did* re-derive the confinement's consequences and got two of five — the lesson is not carelessness but that **"this row is now client-writable" has a CHECKLIST attached** (who else reads this namespace? what invariants were enforced by unreachability? what RI edges become reachable?) and it was enumerated from memory. The checklist is now written into 105 §4 so the next task does not have to remember it.
>
> **(13) TWO THINGS THE REVIEW DECLINED TO LET ME FIX, AND BOTH REFUSALS ARE CORRECT.** R644's FK direction gets **prose only** — an `ON DELETE RESTRICT`-shaped guard is new surface on a security wall against a statement the FK already refuses 100% of the time (CLAUDE.md's "personal problems"). R648's banner claim that the refusal "names `normalizeScoringDoc`" is **trimmed, not made true** — 103's two `v_msg` literals are byte-identical mirrors of `validate-rules-doc.ts`, and `scoring-parity-db.test.ts` compares only `REJECT|hint|path` under a family regex that would still match an appended function name, so editing them would split TS↔SQL message parity **unpinned**. Trimming a banner is free; editing a mirrored literal is not.
>
> **(14) A22 MOVED TWICE IN ONE PR, AND THE SECOND MOVE IS THE PIN BEHAVING CORRECTLY.** `7a5a0273…` → `a1c16d02…` (the lock change) → `fe392869…` (R644/R647 correcting two claims *inside* wall 3's body). The second is a **comment-only** edit — and a golden on `prosrc` cannot distinguish a comment from code and should not try, because the migration-073 failure it exists to catch is exactly an edit that looks harmless. Both re-derivations followed the same discipline: apply the FILE body in a rolled-back transaction and hash the result, after first proving the deployed body carries a marker only that version has; and re-measure the other three literals in the same breath to make "the diff is wall 3's prosrc alone" a measurement.

This task takes **D272** and files **F142**. Chain heads measured at task time, never inherited: `ls supabase/migrations/ | tail -1` → **`103_scoring_rules_validate.sql`**, `ls supabase/tests/ | tail -1` → **`051_scoring_rules_validate.sql`** ⇒ **104 / 052**. **D137 head provenance:** both function names are NEW — `git grep -c "scoring_systems_rules_guard\|leagues_scoring_rules_valid" 8133431 -- supabase/migrations/` → **0 files** (the commit is pinned so the command survives this migration existing) — and 059's `leagues_snapshot_guard` is defined **once and never replaced** (`grep -rn "leagues_snapshot_guard" supabase/migrations/*.sql` → 059 only, at `:24`/`:126`/`:147`/`:150`), so it is stood beside, not authored over. > **(1) WALL 1 IS `SECURITY DEFINER` BECAUSE `leagues` HAS RLS — and the argument is a measurement, not a preference.** D175(2) writes the reference arm as a SYSTEM fact: `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM leagues WHERE scoring_system_id = NEW.id AND deleted_at IS NULL)`, with **no membership join** (unlike §12.25's member SELECT policy, which has one). `leagues` carries exactly one policy and it is a SELECT policy — `select polname, polcmd from pg_policy where polrelid='public.leagues'::regclass` → **one row, `polcmd = 'r'`, `is_league_member(id) OR owner_id = auth.uid()`** (001's `"League owners can manage" FOR ALL` is gone; 052 replaced the read policy). A plain INVOKER trigger's `EXISTS` is therefore RLS-filtered, and the arm evaluates **FALSE — silently, not loudly —** for a writer who owns the scoring row but is not a member or owner of the league referencing it. That is not a hypothetical writer: it is a commissioner who forked and then left, and it is exactly the writer the arm exists to stop. The house precedent for a DEFINER guard trigger already exists (018/025/026/028), and the newer strict form is used: `search_path = ''` with every reference schema-qualified. **§4.1's third requirement — in-body authorization — is DISCHARGED rather than waived, and the discharge is pinned:** a `RETURNS TRIGGER` function has no callable surface at all (`select public.scoring_systems_rules_guard()` → **`0A000`**, *"trigger functions can only be called as triggers"* — measured, and asserted in pgTAP 052 §A8/§A9), so there is no subject to authorize. **Wall 2 is deliberately NOT DEFINER** (059's shape): it reads no table, so it borrows nothing — and being INVOKER it calls the validator **as the writing role**, which is what makes 103's REVOKE stopping at PUBLIC/anon load-bearing. `service_role` is `rolbypassrls = t, rolsuper = f` and, with only a SELECT policy on `leagues`, is the one client role that can write a league row at all; pgTAP 052 §F8 pins that its refusal is **`P0001` with the field path, not `42501`**, so a REVOKE from service_role reds rather than silently degrades the contract SE.5/SE.6 consume.
>
> **(2) THE TRIGGER FIRES ON "IN THE PROFILE", NOT ON "RULES CHANGED" — the union of D175(1) and SE.4b(1), and the difference is reachable.** D175(1) says the guard runs *"whenever the row is in the league profile"*; tasks-SE §5 SE.4b(1) adds *"and `rules` is new or changed"*. Implemented as: **skip only an UPDATE that was ALREADY in the profile carrying the IDENTICAL document** (that document passed this wall on the write that put it there — D175(4)'s never-retroactively-invalidate guarantee). Under the narrow reading alone, `UPDATE scoring_systems SET is_template = TRUE, owner_id = NULL` on a research row **mints a world-readable, league-attachable template carrying a legacy flat document, without `rules` ever being touched**. `authenticated` cannot reach it (058's `scoring_systems_template_ownerless` CHECK forces `owner_id = NULL`, which 001:623's `FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = owner_id)` re-uses as its WITH CHECK and refuses) — but `service_role` can, and D175's whole point is that the wall binds every role. Pinned at pgTAP 052 §E6 with §E7 as its control, and probe 2 reds **exactly E6 and nothing else**.
>
> **(3) THE PROFILE IS COMPUTED FROM `NEW`, WHICH IS WHY THE REFERENCE ARM CARRIES MORE THAN ITS OWN CELL.** Probe 1 (the DoD probe — drop arm (c), leaving template+format) was expected to red one cell and red **five** (C3m, D3, E3, E4c, G1) plus **three vitest tests**. The reason is worth recording: a format-2 fork row **downgraded to a flat map** has no `format` member in `NEW`, so arms (a) and (b) are both dark on that write and only the reference arm can catch it. D175(2) describes this case in one clause — *"a fork row REWRITTEN as an invalid flat map while attached"* — and the probe measures that it is the arm's dominant job, not an edge of it.
>
> **(4) THE FIFTH DECORATION PIN WAS THIS TASK'S OWN, AND IT IS RECORDED IN PLACE.** The brief said *"a pin whose fixture makes the guarded line unreachable is decoration — this lane found that four times in one task; assume a fifth."* The fifth was §B4: the D175(4) census originally re-wrote each profile row's own `rules` back onto itself and asserted the write landed — which is **precisely the write the identity short-circuit in (2) skips**, so the validator was never reached. Measured rather than reasoned (probe 7): with 103's `|coef|` bound tightened to 3 so a shipped template document genuinely fails, the original form reported **`ok 19`**. It now INSERTs a template copy of each profile document under a fresh name — an INSERT through arm (a), which no short-circuit can skip — and probe 6 shows it **RED** under the same condition. The vacuous form and the reason are kept in the file rather than quietly replaced.

> **(5) AND THE SIXTH WAS THE `SECURITY DEFINER` DECISION ITSELF.** Before §E4b/§E4c existed, demoting wall 1 to INVOKER red exactly **one catalog assertion** (§A3) and **nothing that exercised the wall** — because every other writer in the file is either `postgres` or the league's own owner, both of whom can see the league either way. §E4b/§E4c add a writer who owns the scoring row and **cannot see** the referencing league (their own `select count(*) from leagues where scoring_system_id = s6` returns **0**), and probe 3 now reds **A3 + E4c**. A structural pin on `prosecdef` is worth having; on its own it certifies the keyword, not the consequence.

> **(6) THE FORGE IN `scoring-walls-db.test.ts` ACT 3 IS NOT THE ONE SE.4b(5) PRESCRIBES, AND THE SUBSTITUTION IS A FINDING.** The breakdown says to forge the corrupt-while-attached state with `ALTER TABLE scoring_systems DISABLE TRIGGER` as superuser, calling that *"the only way the state can exist"*. > **(22) R626 — THE TOCTOU SEAM, FIXED WITH A LOCK AND MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Wall 1's arm (c) reads `public.leagues` and wall 3 reads `public.scoring_systems`; each held the row in front of it and neither held still the PREMISE it read from the other's table. Reproduced here as a two-session race on the shipped chain: session A opens a transaction and writes the F21 document to an unreferenced row (legal — outside the profile); session B repoints a league at it. **Without the lock: B reports `UPDATE 1`, `COMMIT`, and the check reads `live_league_referencing_invalid_doc = 1`. It creates a two-direction lock pattern and therefore a **deadlock surface** — named rather than hidden; a deadlock is a clean `40P01` rollback, which is what this seam is being traded up TO. **`UNREPRESENTABLE` and "for every role, every path" are now scoped to sequential** in the banner: the sentence was broader than the code, which is the thing this lane does not do.

The claim that (a) leaves F70 red was wrong and is withdrawn; the shape decision never rested on it — reasons (ii) and (iii) are independent and each was verified at review. One shape, three rows, no global blast radius.
  **(2) F70 IS EXPLAINED, NOT PAPERED OVER — AND THE "TWO-POSITION JUMP" WAS A RANDOM DRAFT SLOT.** The row demanded that `rb03 → rb05` be explained or left open with the observation sharpened. It is explained, and the explanation accounts for **every** value ever recorded against `:389`. `draft-board-autopick-db` configures `draft_order_mode: 'random'`, so the commissioner's slot is redrawn every run; its 5 board fixtures carry `adp: NULL` and its 7 placeholder seats always walk source 4, `ORDER BY pl.adp NULLS LAST, pl.id` (095:3440). On an EMPTY pool those seats therefore eat the board from the top, in id order, and the commissioner's own board read returns **`BOARD_ORDER[slot − 1]`**. Hence: `rb02`/`rb03`/`rb04`/`rb05` = slots 2–5; **`vitest-lpd-p2`** = slot ≥ 6, board exhausted, fall-through to source 4 over F127's residue; **`undefined`** = the reset-with-no-restore case where only the 5 fixtures existed and the pool ran out before the commissioner's turn. A per-run counter cannot produce two different assertions from one commit; a redrawn slot can. **So "+1 per run" is not merely unestablished, it is refuted** — and the row's own "different worktree" note is a coincidence, not a variable.

It is a **source** question, governed by **D229(5)/§4 rule 12**, which is why MP.6c's item 2 makes the room's non-draft context an OBJECT with a pluggable source: the deferred league-attached mock then becomes a **third source rather than a rewrite**. (8) **The transferable finding, and it is D231(3a) one level DOWN.** D231(3a) said *a release-independence claim is a claim about ROUTES as well as components*. This says: **the fix for that route guard was itself scoped as a route matter, and the component layer and the action layer each carry their own copy of the coupling the route layer's fix cannot see.** **Independence is a property of every layer a request passes through, and has to be measured at each one rather than argued from the topmost.** Folded into `tasks-MP` §5's MP.6 banner and §1.7.

- **D236 — A mock's roster shape is a SNAPSHOT; a real draft's stays LIVE; and the second half is a decision, not an omission.**

1. **What was wrong, restated at the level that explains why it survived three milestones.** D95's *"a mock never re-hydrates"* was implemented as *"copy `leagues.settings->'draft'` into `drafts.config`"* — and `roster_settings` is a **separate COLUMN**, so the copy never contained it. The launch snapshot looked complete because the thing it was missing was not in the block it copied. 038's config pin asserted that block and passed. **The lesson is the one D231(3a) keeps producing: a check that covers the shape you thought about cannot fail on the shape you did not.**
2. **The fix is a deletion, not a guard.** `draft_mock_cpu_need`'s `JOIN public.leagues` is **gone** (every caller is a mock arm — `089:2322`, superseded by `091:516`), and `draft_autopick_resolve`'s `SELECT l.* INTO v_league` moved **inside** its `is_mock = FALSE` arm. **No league fallback is written on the mock path**, deliberately: a fallback would re-open exactly the re-hydration D95 forbids and would leave the read MP.2 exists to remove. Legacy rows are handled by a **backfill** instead (094 §2), which is what makes the no-fallback position affordable.
3. **The storage key is `config->'roster'`, holding the WHOLE roster object rather than just `starting_slots`.** Two readers need the slots today; the whole object costs nothing, makes the draft row self-describing beside the `total_rounds` already derived from it, and gives MP.4's settings OBJECT (§4 rule 12) a place to land that is a **new source, not a rewrite**. The §7.3.8 draft block is flat scalars, so the key cannot collide.
4. **REAL DRAFTS KEEP THE LIVE READ, AND THIS IS THE DECISION THE TASK WAS ASKED TO STATE.** §7.3.3's scoring-snapshot doctrine and D95 both point at snapshot-at-start as the house position — but a real draft's settings edits go through **§8.7/D141's pause-first commissioner controls**, which is a different argument with a different blast radius (a live twelve-human draft, mid-flight, whose commissioner is entitled to change the board). **MP.2 had no mandate to settle it and did not.** It is folded into the LAW as spec **v2.16.1** rather than left in a PR body, so the next lane inherits the decision instead of re-deciding it silently, and **042 §D pins it** by showing the same mid-flight edit MOVING a real draft's autopick while the mock's stands still. No `config->'roster'` is written for a real draft either — an unread stored field is a claim nobody checks (042 §A pins the negative).
5. **THE COLLAPSE IS NOW A MEASUREMENT, NOT A PARAGRAPH (probe 2).** §1.2 predicted that a league-less mock would leave `v_slots`/`v_total` NULL and collapse every bot's need term. Probed in a rolled-back transaction (`league_id` NOT NULL and its FK dropped, a standalone mock inserted, the shipped body installed under a probe name): the pre-094 body returns **0.5 for a starter and 0.5 for a bench player** — not an error, not a stall, **every position priced identically** — while the 094 body returns **1.0 / 0.5**. That is the failure mode MP.3 would otherwise have met as "the bots seem to bid oddly", and the transaction rolled back with `attnotnull` and `drafts_league_id_fkey` re-verified present.
6. **The break probe, at exact counts.** Restoring both shipped reader bodies turns **11 of 042's 24** RED — tests 11/12/13 (§C, the D95 pin), 15 (§D's disagreement line), 16/17/18 (§E's structural sweep), 21/22/23/24 (§F's boundary). **§B stays GREEN, and that is the point of §B:** on an unedited league the snapshot and the live league are the same object, so the no-change pin cannot discriminate — which is what makes §C a pin on re-hydration rather than on the new code path. Restore verified **md5-identical** on all three bodies (`pg_get_functiondef`), and no probe text is committed.
7. **Two existing pgTAP fixtures had to change, and both changes are the migration being real rather than accommodation.** `038:503` subtracted `- 'mock' - 'draft_order'` from the config snapshot and asserted the rest; it now also subtracts `- 'roster'`, so it keeps testing exactly the §7.3.8 block it was written to test (the VALUE is asserted in 042 §A). `039`'s §G fixture builds its mock by direct INSERT and fed `draft_mock_cpu_need` a hand-built config; it now carries the roster snapshot `create_mock_draft` would have written — **the same value as that league's own `roster_settings` (`039:332-334`), so every stored literal in that section is unchanged.** Both were RED before the fixture edit and green after, with the suite total unchanged at 2923 before 042 was added.
8. **The backfill is proved, not assumed (probe 3), because this dev machine holds ZERO drafts** — `select count(*) filter (where is_mock) from drafts` = 0, so "the migration ran clean" would have measured nothing. In a rolled-back transaction: a legacy-shaped mock (draft block + `mock` key, no `roster`) and a real draft under a league with a `{TE:3, bench:2}` roster; the migration's UPDATE **verbatim** stamps `UPDATE 1`, the mock gains `roster.starting_slots[0].key = 'te'` with its `mock` key and draft block intact, **the real draft is untouched**, and a second run reports `UPDATE 0` (idempotent).
9. **NO `db reset` WAS RUN.** The chain-order rule calls for reset-first only when a reset is otherwise required; `npx supabase migration up` replays the new file against the deployed chain, and the rehearsal recorded in 094's banner is that plus the full pgTAP suite. Destroying Chris's dev login and data to rehearse what `migration up` already exercises is a cost with no evidence attached (F110's own lesson, one turn later).
10. **Scope held — and the residue claim is narrowed to what is true (R492).** F109(a)'s `leagues`-EXISTENCE GUARD class is untouched and stays **MP.3's** (D234(4)). Two consequences recorded so MP.3 does not re-derive them. **(a)** `draft_mock_cpu_need`'s single `public.leagues` reference **was** this settings JOIN, so that body drops off F109(a)'s list entirely; `draft_autopick_resolve`'s two are the DECLARE (`v_league public.leagues`) and the SELECT, and the SELECT is now unreachable on a mock. **(b) THE CLAIM STOPS THERE, AND THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS ITEM DID NOT.** *"No `public.leagues` reference remains reachable on a mock's path"* is true and is what the sweep pins. *"The league coupling is exhausted"* would be **false**: `draft_autopick_resolve` still carries **two `v_draft.league_id` predicates ON the mock path** — the queue source's `t.league_id = v_draft.league_id` (the R120 join) and the primary-board source's `ll.league_id = v_draft.league_id`. They read `drafts.league_id`, not the `leagues` TABLE, so they sit outside both MP.2's charter and F109(a)'s `EXISTS(leagues …)` class — but with a NULL `league_id` **both silently yield nothing, and the launcher's own queue and board are ignored while best-ADP quietly wins.** Added to F109(a)'s inventory. **The general form is the one worth keeping: an inventory written as "what I removed" reads as "what remains", and the second sentence is the one MP.3 would have paid for.**
11. **R491 — AND THE SNAPSHOT'S ABSENCE IS NOW A LOUD FAILURE, WHICH THE FIRST CUT LEFT SILENT.** `COALESCE(config->'roster'->'starting_slots', '[]')` cannot distinguish *"never snapshotted"* from *"legitimately no starting slots"* (an all-bench roster is legal), and the first of those **is this migration's own defect arriving quietly**: measured with the guards removed, an unsnapshotted mock's autopick still returns a player and QB/RB/WR all price at **0.5 / 0.5 / 0.5**. Both readers now `RAISE` P0001 on a mock whose config lacks the `roster` **KEY** (key absence, never an empty array — the all-bench case must still price, and is pinned doing so), and **§2's backfill ends by PROVING no unsnapshotted mock remains** instead of trusting an UPDATE's row count. **Unreachable today** — `league_id` is NOT NULL with a live FK, so the backfill's join covers every mock — **but MP.3 drops that NOT NULL and MP.4 adds a settings writer, and a guard has to exist before the reachability does.** CLAUDE.md verbatim: *assert the reason for emptiness*. Probe: guards removed ⇒ **exactly 2 of 042's 29 RED** (tests 27, 28), the all-bench test 29 staying green; restored **md5-identical**.
12. **R496 — what the backfill FIRES, named rather than rediscovered.** `public.drafts` carries `tr_broadcast_drafts` with **no WHEN clause** (measured: `pg_get_triggerdef(...) ~ 'WHEN'` → false), so §2 emits one broadcast per stamped mock. Zero impact on this deploy (F12: prod's history ends pre-league-schema, so there are no mock rows to stamp) and the audience elsewhere is a room whose draft did not change. **Named, not fixed** — narrowing a shipped trigger is not MP.2's to do.
13. **R497 — `draft_mock_cpu_need` is EXECUTE-able by `anon` AND `authenticated`, and always has been.** 089 shipped it with no REVOKE; 094 preserves that **exactly**, because changing a grant is not a settings-reader fix. It is a STABLE read-only pricing helper, so the exposure is a value rather than a write. **Recorded as a measured fact in 042 §E** — so a future REVOKE reddens there and gets read — and **handed to MP.3 as F112**.

**2026-08-24 — Builder (F110 closure, the fixture-pool fix; branch `fix/F110-fixture-adp-scale`; TEST FILES ONLY — zero migrations, zero function bodies, zero app code)**

- **D235 — A pgTAP fixture may never state its premise about the WHOLE `players` table. Two premises were doing exactly that, and they are two different bugs, not one.**

1. **The band (9 of the 10 failures) — the R286 lesson, applied where F60's sweep had not reached.** `022`, `025` and `026` seeded fixture players on an INTEGER ADP scale (`022` RB `1…17` / WR `31…40` / QB `51…57` / K `151…153` / DST `161…162`; `025` QB `1…20`, RB `101…112`; `026` QB `1…20`, RB `101…120`) and never cleared `players`. A seeded dev pool holds **1,075 rows / 530 with an ADP**, and its **global minimum is 1.8** (RB) — measured, not assumed — so the two scales **interleave** and `draft_autopick_resolve`'s source-4 walk drafted real players. **Fix: every fixture value divided by 1000**, landing the whole band in `(0, 1)`. This is the band `035` has carried and documented since M3 (`035:19–23`) and the exact repair F60 made to `draft-realtime-db.test.ts`; these three files are F60's un-swept remainder.
2. **Why divide rather than re-number, and why it is green in BOTH worlds.** A single positive divisor preserves the order among fixtures **exactly** — every within-file discriminator survives untouched, including `025`'s load-bearing "the 20 best ADPs are ALL QBs" and `026`'s `lr-p003` pin. `draft_autopick_resolve` reads adp **only as an ordering key** (`ORDER BY pl.adp NULLS LAST, pl.id` at `086:692` and `086:742`; the `row_number()` at `086:692` is consumed as an ordinal by `ORDER BY c.src, c.ord` and compared against no threshold), so scale itself carries no meaning and only *relative position* can change. Every fixture moves **strictly below** the real pool's minimum, so the only orderings that can change are the ones where a real player previously preceded a fixture — precisely the failures. **On an EMPTY pool there are no real players, so the fixture-only order is bit-for-bit what it was**: the suites are green after a fresh reset and on a seeded machine alike, and **this was established by reasoning from the fix, not by running a destructive `db reset`** (`players.adp` is unconstrained `numeric`, so the fractions store at full precision — checked).
3. **The 10th failure is a DIFFERENT species and no ADP band could have fixed it — `022`'s FLOOR world (test 38).** Its premise was *"a forced TE need with **ZERO TEs in the pool**"*, which is a claim about the whole table; a seeded pool holds **231 TEs (94 with an ADP, min 22.1)**, one of them fits the need, greedy step h is never reached and the pin went red. **Fix: `022`'s LD roster_settings slot changes from `{"key":"te","eligible":["TE"]}` to `{"key":"floor","eligible":["NOPOS"]}`** — a token no player pool can carry. `draft_autopick_resolve` builds `v_need` straight from that array and tests it with a plain `v_row.pos = ANY(v_need)` (`086:631`/`086:706`): **no slot vocabulary is validated, no other branch keys off `'TE'`**, and `TE` was never load-bearing here — so step h is reached by the identical path, now **true by construction** instead of true by luck. Nothing else in `022` referenced that slot (checked: `starting_slots` appears twice, `"te"` once).
4. **Neither fix loosens anything, and both were probed (§4.3, D146).** The test count is **2923 before and after** — no assertion was dropped, renamed away or widened; the only assertion text that changed is test 38's *description*, from "a forced TE need with ZERO TEs in the pool" to "a forced need NO player in the pool can fill", which is what it now literally does. **Probe A (the semantic change):** plant one player at `position 'NOPOS', adp 0.999` — far WORSE than `tk-rb01`'s `0.001` — and test 38 goes **RED with `have: tk-probe-nopos`**, proving the need gate is live and step h is reached *only* because nothing fits; if the gate were dead the floor pin would have been satisfied anyway and the test would have proved nothing. **Probe B (the band):** restore `025`'s integer scale and tests **48 and 81 go RED again** (`have: 3` / `want: 8`). Both reverted, full suite re-run green.
5. **The standing rule this leaves.** *A fixture that asserts on an ADP-resolved pick must win by VALUE (a fractional band below the real minimum), and a fixture whose premise is an ABSENCE must make that absence true within its own fixture — never by betting on what the shared `players` table happens to contain.* The second half is new; F60/R286 only ever covered the first, which is why the sweep criterion R315 corrected still missed test 38.
6. **`F94` was checked while in the file and deliberately NOT touched (its own row owns it).** `src/lib/leagues/api/draft-board-autopick-db.test.ts` **does not carry F110's exposure** — it is already immune by the R286 redesign, seeding its fixtures at `adp: NULL` ("the one placement no walk can reach", `:83`), so a seeded pool can never steal a fixture from it. **Its exposure is the exact inverse and it is F94's:** `:424` asserts the ADP-resolved pick is **NOT** a fixture and `:436` asserts `picked?.adp` is **not null**, both of which require a **non-empty** real pool with ADPs — they fail on the empty pool a fresh reset leaves. Reported, not fixed.

**2026-08-24 — Builder (MP.1, the storage investigation; branch `feat/MP-MP.1-storage-investigation`; docs only, migration count ZERO):**

- **D234 — The storage shape is DECIDED: a standalone mock lives in the SAME tables, with `league_id` nullable and the ownership arm scoped by `league_id IS NULL`. Mock-owned tables are REFUSED, and D233(3)'s guardrail is the finding, stated plainly.**

*Every figure below was measured against the **deployed local schema** (`supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` tops at **093** = repo HEAD `8fc5852`), never by grepping the migration tree — that method difference is how D228's 4× error happened, and it is how two of the figures this entry corrects went wrong too. Each claim names its command (tasks-DR §4 rule 9).*

1. **THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS D233(1) STATES IT: no. The engine cannot operate on mock-owned storage without duplicating the auction rules, and it is not close.** `SELECT count(*), sum(array_length(string_to_array(prosrc,E'\n'),1)) FROM pg_proc … WHERE proname ~ '^(draft|create_mock|delete_mock|mock_draft)'` → **58 live functions / 6,310 lines**. *(§1.3's "6,252" is the same measurement by a newline count: 6,310 − 58 = 6,252. No discrepancy — recorded so the next session does not re-derive it as a conflict.)* Of those, **37 functions / 5,901 lines** name one of the six draft tables, across **206 individual table-naming lines**, spread over **17 migration files** (`grep -lE '^CREATE (OR REPLACE )?FUNCTION +(public\.)?(draft_|create_mock|delete_mock|mock_draft)' supabase/migrations/*.sql | wc -l`). **The auction subset alone is 25 functions / 3,604 lines** (`proname ~ '(bid|nominat|auction|solven|budget)' OR prosrc ~ 'public\.draft_bids'` — `draft_tick` 1015, `draft_nominate` 295, `draft_force_pick` 280, `draft_award_nomination_internal` 232, `draft_undo` 204, `draft_place_bid` 178 …). **Dynamic SQL is absent: exactly one function in the family contains `EXECUTE`, and it is `draft_actor_name`** — re-confirmed, not recalled.
2. **And the price of (b) is LARGER than D233(3) priced it, in three places nobody had measured.** **(i) The FK fan-in.** `drafts` has **five** FK children (`pg_constraint … confrelid='public.drafts'::regclass`): `draft_picks`, `draft_queues`, `draft_liveness`, `draft_bids`, **and `draft_dnd_marks`** — the sixth table §1.3 never enumerated. Mock-owned storage duplicates the whole family, not four tables. **(ii) The realtime layer.** Five broadcast triggers fire on the draft path (`tr_broadcast_drafts`, `_draft_picks`, `_draft_bids`, `_draft_bids_void`, `tr_broadcast_league_chat`); each needs a twin. **(iii) The app layer, which §1.3 never measured at all.** `grep -rn "from('<t>')" src --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx'` → **148 call sites across 24 TypeScript files** (`drafts` 81 · `draft_picks` 33 · `draft_bids` 19 · `league_chat` 8 · `draft_queues` 7 · `draft_liveness` 0). Mock-owned tables mean a table-selecting or a parallel service layer on top of the two copies of the auction rules. **(iv) The suites.** **19 of 42 pgTAP files** name one of the six (836 `drafts` mentions, 284 `draft_bids`, 259 `draft_picks`, 117 `league_chat`, 65 `draft_queues`, 56 `draft_liveness`), and every one asserts against a body that names what it touches — D233(3)'s second argument, now with the count.
3. **Rewriting to table-agnostic dynamic SQL is refused for the reason D233(3) names, and the measurement makes it concrete: 23 of the 58 functions are `SECURITY DEFINER`** (`prosecdef`), every one of them built on `search_path=''` (tasks-M* §4.1). Turning 206 literal table references into `EXECUTE format(...)` is 206 opportunities to reintroduce the search-path hazard that discipline exists to close. **Refused.**
4. **THE SAME-TABLES PATH, RE-PRICED — and TWO of D233(4)'s three figures are wrong, in D228's own error species.**
   - **`NOT NULL` drops: FOUR, confirmed exactly.** `information_schema.columns WHERE column_name='league_id'` → 11 rows: `teams` already nullable, **10 `NOT NULL`**, of which **four are on the draft path** — `drafts`, `draft_picks`, `draft_bids`, `league_chat`. The other six are league-only tables a mock never touches. **D233(4) is right on this one.**
   - **In-body auth sites: EIGHT executable on a mock's path, not eleven — and SEVEN bodies actually change.** §1.3's `length/replace` count returns 13, but **four of those 13 are COMMENT lines**, not calls (`draft_make_pick`, `draft_nominate`, `draft_touch`, `set_team_autodraft` each carry an `-- … is_league_member(NULL) is FALSE` note). Filtering `trim(line) !~ '^--'` gives **9 executable sites across 9 functions**, one per function: `create_mock_draft` · `delete_mock_draft` · `draft_make_pick` · `draft_nominate` · `draft_pause` · `draft_place_bid` · `draft_resume` · `draft_touch` · `set_team_autodraft`. **`set_team_autodraft` is a league verb and out of scope → eight on a mock's path**; **`create_mock_draft` is superseded by MP.3's new standalone launch RPC → seven bodies amended.** **This is exactly D228(3)'s failure repeated one level down: a counting method that cannot tell live code from dead text.** D228 counted superseded bodies; §1.3 counted comments. **The rule the two together establish: count what EXECUTES, not what MATCHES.**
   - **RLS: FOUR SELECT arms required, not five — and the fifth is optional for a reason worth writing down.** `pg_policies` shows **14 policies in `public` naming `is_league_member`** (§1.3's figure — correct once you notice it excludes `realtime`), of which **five sit on four draft-path tables**: SELECT on `drafts`/`draft_picks`/`draft_bids`/`league_chat`, plus **`league_chat`'s INSERT**. **The INSERT arm is not required — but NOT for the reason this entry first gave, and the correction is this session's own rule failing on itself (R485).** The original reason was *"every engine write bypasses RLS"*, resting on `postgres` being `rolbypassrls`. **That establishes a bypass for `SECURITY DEFINER` bodies only, and 35 of the 58 engine functions are `SECURITY INVOKER`** (`prosecdef` → **35 `f` / 23 `t`**) — `draft_queue_replace` is an **invoker, client-callable engine writer** (`has_function_privilege('authenticated', …, 'EXECUTE')` → true) which runs as the caller, and `authenticated` is **not** `rolbypassrls`. **A blanket claim measured on the wrong population — exactly the species tasks-DR §4 rule 9 exists for.** The conclusion survives on the narrower ground that actually holds, re-measured: **every client-reachable `league_chat` writer is `SECURITY DEFINER`** — all thirteen engine-family chat writers except `draft_pause_internal` are definer and granted to `authenticated`, and **`draft_pause_internal` is granted to neither `authenticated` nor `anon`**, being reached only from `draft_pause` and `draft_tick` — and `relforcerowsecurity` is **false** on all seven tables — measured. The INSERT arm is needed only if a human types into a mock room, and D226(2) says there is nobody to type to. **So: four SELECT arms, and a fifth that MP.3 may decline with a reason.**
   - **`draft_queues`, `draft_liveness` and `draft_dnd_marks` cost ZERO** — none carries `league_id`; `draft_liveness` has RLS on with **zero policies** (deny-all to clients, RPC-only); **`draft_queues`' two policies ALREADY carry the exact predicate this decision recommends** — `d.is_mock AND d.config->'mock'->>'launched_by' = auth.uid()::text` — shipped, in production, in `pg_policies` today. **The ownership predicate is not new work and not a new idiom:** `launched_by` appears in **11 live functions** (`create_mock_draft` 6 · `draft_tick` 5 · `draft_make_pick`/`draft_nominate`/`draft_place_bid` 3 each · `draft_autopick_resolve`/`mock_draft_expire` 2 each · `delete_mock_draft`/`draft_pause`/`draft_queue_replace`/`draft_resume` 1 each). **MS.2's gate is reused verbatim, per the lane constraint — nothing is reinvented.**
   - **Indexes and constraints: ZERO work.** **Eight** unique indexes name `league_id` schema-wide (`pg_indexes WHERE indexdef ~ 'UNIQUE' AND indexdef ~ 'league_id'`), but **exactly one is on the draft path** — `drafts.one_active_real_draft_per_league`, already filtered `WHERE is_mock = false`. The other seven are on `league_lists`, `league_members`, `league_rosters` and `league_weeks`, which a mock never touches. *(R487 — the sentence as first written said "the only unique index on `league_id`", which is false schema-wide.)*
5. **THREE ITEMS THE SAME-TABLES PRICE WAS MISSING — and the first one, added at review (R484), is the most severe thing in this entry.**
   - **THE `leagues`-EXISTENCE GUARD CLASS: UNDER THIS SHAPE THE ENGINE NEVER CLAIMS A STANDALONE MOCK AT ALL, AND IT FAILS SILENTLY.** This session's "breaks on a NULL `league_id`" sweep stopped at `is_league_member` and missed a **third, larger class** — the `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.leagues l WHERE l.id = … AND l.deleted_at IS NULL)` soft-delete guards. Re-swept with `LATERAL regexp_matches(prosrc,'([^\n]*public\.leagues\M[^\n]*)','g')`, comment lines filtered: **`draft_tick` 14 · `draft_start_internal` 3 · `create_mock_draft` / `draft_autopick_resolve` / `draft_create_internal` / `draft_reset` / `draft_set_order` 2 each · `draft_complete_internal` / `draft_end` / `draft_make_pick` / `draft_mock_cpu_need` / `draft_nominate` / `draft_place_bid` 1 each.** **SIX of `draft_tick`'s sit INSIDE its `AND d.is_mock` scans** — body lines **268/291** (ARM 1.6), **531/559** (ARM 2.5), **680/722** (ARM 2.6(c)), each an `AND EXISTS (… l.id = d.league_id AND l.deleted_at IS NULL)` on the scan that decides which mock to advance. **Probed live in a rolled-back transaction over three `live` rows: `tick_leagues_guard` is `t` for the REAL draft, `t` for the MOCK-in-league, and `f` for the MOCK-standalone.** **So the tick never picks a standalone mock up — no CPU picks, no nominations, no bids — and it says nothing.** That is strictly worse than the `league_chat` failure below, which this entry credited itself with catching: **that one raises 23502 loudly; this one produces a mock that runs and never bids.** **And the same class is loud in the other direction:** `draft_make_pick`, `draft_nominate` and `draft_place_bid` each carry a **second, uncounted** `IF NOT EXISTS (… leagues …) RAISE … USING ERRCODE = 'P0002'` **immediately after** the `is_league_member` site item 4 counted, and `draft_end` / `draft_reset` carry the `PERFORM … FOR UPDATE; IF NOT FOUND` variant — probed the same way, **`raises_P0002` is `f` / `f` / `t`**, so the human's own pick, nomination and bid would all 404 on their own practice. **CONSEQUENCE FOR THE PRICE: item 4's "seven bodies amended" is WRONG. It is seven bodies PLUS the leagues-existence guard class**, which touches `draft_tick` (six mock-scan arms), `draft_make_pick`, `draft_nominate`, `draft_place_bid`, `draft_end` and `draft_reset`. **It does not change the DECISION** — these are predicate edits inside bodies that stay where they are, and mock-owned tables would inherit every one of the same guards — **but MP.3 is materially larger than item 4 implied, and that must not be discovered during the build.** **OWNERSHIP: MP.3, not MP.2.** MP.2's charter is the two live **settings readers** (`roster_settings->'starting_slots'`); these are **candidate-set and existence predicates**, a different class in different bodies, and they belong beside the `NOT NULL` drops in the same migration. **Filed as F109(a).**
   - **`league_chat`'s `NOT NULL` drop is LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic.** `draft_pause_internal` and `draft_resume` each `INSERT INTO public.league_chat (league_id, …) VALUES (v_draft.league_id, …)` **with no `is_mock` guard** — **fourteen** functions in the schema `INSERT INTO public.league_chat`; thirteen are in the engine family and the fourteenth is `set_team_autodraft`, **excluded as a league verb (R489)**. Of the thirteen, **twelve mention `is_mock` at all** (`draft_pause_internal` does not) — and **these two execute the chat INSERT on a mock's path with `v_draft.league_id` unguarded**, both on a standalone mock's path (`draft_pause_internal` is called by `draft_pause` **and `draft_tick`**). With `league_id` NULL and the column still `NOT NULL`, **pausing or resuming a standalone mock raises 23502 and the practice is stuck.** This is §1.2's finding on the storage axis rather than the settings axis, and it is **MP.3's** to close — either by the drop or by an `is_mock` guard, its call. **Not fixed here (MP.1 changes nothing).**
   - **THE REALTIME POLICIES, WHICH NO PRICING HAD COUNTED UNDER EITHER SHAPE.** `realtime.messages` carries **two policies on `draft:%` topics** — `members read draft topics` (SELECT) and `members track presence on draft topics` (INSERT) — and **both gate on `is_league_member(d.league_id)` via a subquery on `drafts`.** Without an arm, **the launcher cannot subscribe to their own mock's channel and the room is dead**, and the room is realtime-driven (tasks-M2 §4 rule 5). **The cost is identical under either shape, so it does not move the decision** — but it must be in MP.3's work list. **And the chat pane's READ is league-keyed too (R490), which this entry's D226(2) appeal covered only for the SEND:** `useDraftChat` (`src/hooks/use-draft-chat.ts:44–50`) is `enabled: Boolean(leagueId && draftId)` and filters `.eq('league_id', leagueId!)`, so with no league **the query never runs, and a standalone launcher cannot read the engine's own SYSTEM posts** — the pause/resume/clock notices the room depends on. "Nobody to chat with" does not mean "nothing to read". **Added to F109(c), and MP.6 is the alternative owner if the room's data hooks land there first.** **The good news is measured:** the four draft broadcast trigger functions (`broadcast_draft_update`, `broadcast_draft_pick_change`, `broadcast_draft_bid_insert`, `broadcast_draft_bid_void`) **do not reference `league_id` at all** — only `broadcast_league_chat_insert` and `broadcast_league_roster_change` do — so the topic and payload layers are **already league-free** and only the two read policies need the arm. **Filed as F109.**
6. **D233(5) ANSWERED, and the answer is stronger than "no weakening" — it is "provably identical".** The recommended predicate is
   `is_league_member(league_id) OR (league_id IS NULL AND is_mock AND config->'mock'->>'launched_by' = auth.uid()::text)`.
   **The truth table is one line:** for any row where `league_id IS NOT NULL`, the second disjunct's **first conjunct is FALSE by construction**, so the whole predicate **reduces to the shipped one, term for term**. There is no real-league row for which the new arm can contribute a TRUE. Separately measured: **`is_league_member(NULL)` returns FALSE, not NULL** — it is a `SELECT EXISTS(…)`, which is never NULL — so **a nullable `league_id` fails CLOSED**. There is no NULL-permissiveness hole to defend against; the column's nullability, on its own, grants nobody anything.
7. **AND IT WAS PROBED, INCLUDING THE DELIBERATE BREAK (§4.3 falsifiability floor).** One rolled-back transaction, three users — `u1` league member and standalone launcher, `u2` outsider, **`u3` an EX-member who launched a league-attached mock and then left the league** — over three `drafts` rows (a REAL draft, a MOCK-in-league, a MOCK-standalone inserted after an in-txn `DROP NOT NULL`), read as `authenticated` under each user's JWT:
   - **A · shipped policy:** u1 → `REAL, MOCK-in-league` · u2 → `(nothing)` · u3 → `(nothing)`.
   - **B · the recommended arm:** u1 → `REAL, MOCK-in-league, MOCK-standalone` · u2 → `(nothing)` · **u3 → `(nothing)`. Every league-owning row is visible to exactly the same people as in A.**
   - **C · THE DELIBERATE BREAK — the identical arm with the `league_id IS NULL` conjunct removed:** **u3 → `MOCK-in-league`.** An ex-member keeps read on a league-attached mock after leaving the league — **strictly more permissive on a row that HAS a league**, which is precisely what D233(5) forbids. **Shown RED, then reverted** (the whole probe is inside `ROLLBACK`; afterwards `pg_policies` shows the shipped `is_league_member(league_id)` qual restored, `drafts.league_id` back to `is_nullable = NO`, and zero probe users left in `auth.users` — all three verified).
   **So the `league_id IS NULL` conjunct is load-bearing, not defensive decoration**, and MP.3 must not "simplify" it away. Probe script: `docs/specs/` carries no fixture; the exact SQL is reproduced in the PR body.
8. **What this decision does NOT do, stated so MP.3 does not over-read it.** It does not touch a real league or an `is_mock = FALSE` draft (§4 rule 11): the four `NOT NULL` drops are **widenings**, which no existing row can violate, and the four RLS arms are **provably inert** on every league-owning row (item 6). It does not choose the launch RPC's signature, the bot-seat shape (D227) or the settings source (D229) — those are MP.3/MP.4. It does not fix the two live `JOIN leagues` readers; **`draft_mock_cpu_need` (`089:394`) and `draft_autopick_resolve` are MP.2's**, and the sequencing is now a hard prerequisite rather than a preference: **under this shape a NULL `league_id` makes that JOIN match nothing and every bot's need term collapse (§1.2), and no storage decision can defend against it — MP.2 must land before MP.3.**
9. **The spec fold this decision OWES, and it is not MP.1's to make.** Spec **§12.4/§12.5/§12.6-adjacent** print `CREATE POLICY … USING (is_league_member(league_id))` for `drafts` (`spec:912`), `draft_picks` (`:938`) and `draft_bids` (`:990`), and §12's DDL prints `league_id` as `NOT NULL`. **v2.16 §8.8 already rules the standalone mock into v1** (`spec:570`), so §12's listings are stale rather than contradictory — but they are LAW as printed, and **the task that changes a policy owes the erratum, not the task that recommends it.** **Filed as F109 with MP.3 named.** *(No halt: D233 explicitly charters MP.1 to price the change to those arms, and the breakdown — merged LAW — already prices "five RLS policy arms on four tables" as in-scope. Recommending a change the lane document sanctions is not improvising around the spec.)*
10. **Recorded because it cost this session an hour and will cost the next one the same: `npm run test:db` is RED on a seeded dev machine, and it is an ENVIRONMENT artifact, not a regression.** 10 failures across `022_draft_tick_autopick` (6), `025_mock_draft_mode` (2), `026_draft_completion_rosters` (2) — every one in the autopick/roster family. **Cause, measured rather than guessed:** those suites seed fixture players on an integer ADP scale (025:213–217 — `mk-qb01…20` at ADP `1…20`, `mk-rb01…12` at `101…112`) and **never clear `players`**; this machine's `players` holds **1,075 rows, 530 with ADP**, topping out at **Jahmyr Gibbs 1.8, Bijan Robinson 2.7, Ja'Marr Chase 3.2** — which **interleave with the fixture scale**, so autopick drafts real players and the fixture assertions fail. **It is F94's mirror image**: F94 says the pool is EMPTY after a reset; here the seeds ran afterwards and the pool is FULL. **Drift was ruled out before concluding this**, per CLAUDE.md's reconciliation rule: `pg_get_functiondef(draft_autopick_resolve)` diffed **byte-identical** against its chain HEAD (`086_auction_tick_completion.sql:552`), and the migration table tops at 093. **No destructive `db reset` was run to "fix" it** — that would have cost Chris his dev login and data for a red this session did not cause. **Filed as F110.**
