(7) **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE:** no named `AUCTION_BID_INCREMENT` constant (D199(1) reserves the named increment for **AP.2**, whose uncontestable predicate needs `high_bid + increment`); no change to `draft_place_bid` (089's head delegates and inherits); no touch to 091/AP.3's reactive-CPU arms, which sit outside every hunk; and no fix to the `draft-board-autopick-db` red, which is `main`'s and is **F94**.
- **D215 — The uncontestable instant award: the order Chris corrected mid-build, why the extraction had to be proved first, the third path nobody listed, and what is deliberately absent.** (1) **THE ORDER WAS RULED MID-TASK AND THE BUILD FOLLOWS THE RULING, NOT THE BRIEF.** This session was briefed with the message running BEFORE the award — a 3-second beat at the end of which the award lands. Chris corrected it in the middle of the build: *"No you've misunderstood. It awards the player immediately and then displays that message for 3 seconds until the next nomination."* So the server finds the nomination uncontestable and awards it **immediately, atomically, in that same determination**, and the 3 seconds is a display/pacing beat over an already-painted board, living in the gap before the next nomination opens. **What had been built for the pre-award version, and was removed:** two migration-banner sections (item 3's "announcement then board, in order" framing and an item 4 titled "THE RACE, ANSWERED"), one comment on the extracted award's phase guard claiming it "makes a double award structurally impossible", and the client's render ordering (the beat had been designed to replace the board for its 3 seconds; it now runs over it). **No pending-award state, no re-check-at-expiry, no cancellation path and no double-fire guard was ever coded** — the design was atomic from the first line of SQL because D199(4) already specified one transaction — so the correction cost prose and one component decision, not machinery. Spec **v2.13.4** folds it, because §8.6.9 and §16.5.4 both printed the wrong order and E67 repeated it.
- **D215 (cont.) — the general principle, which reaches past this task.** (2) Chris, same session: *"but a commish can pause a draft and change anything or someone can disconnect at any time. TBH in drafts that's known as a 'personal problem'"*. **Pause → change → resume is the sanctioned mechanism** (§8.7); a live window owes no defence against edits that belong inside a pause, and a mid-auction disconnect is what §8.6.2's system nomination exists for. Prefer decide-and-commit-in-one-step, then display the outcome. This does **not** relax genuine server-side races: two writers on one row, double submission of one RPC and §8.1/E2 idempotency stand exactly as before. The distinction — *defend against two writers, not against a person changing their mind* — is now spec text at §8.6.9, so the absence of those paths reads as a ruling instead of an oversight the next session "fixes".
- **D215 (cont.) — the build mechanics.** (3) **THE EXTRACTION'S LOSSLESSNESS WAS PROVED BEFORE THE SECOND CALLER EXISTED (the 087/R367 discipline, run as an actual build step).** ARM 2.6(b)'s 191 lines (092:3471–3661) became `draft_award_nomination_internal`, de-indented by exactly 8 spaces — `diff` of before and after under `sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//'` is EMPTY, so the move changed no non-whitespace character — with **one** substantive line changed (`v_auc_completed := … + 1` → `v_completed := TRUE`, because the counter belongs to the sweep and the answer belongs to the award). A variant of 093 carrying the extraction and the predicate but **not** the wiring was built and run: 41 files / **2855** assertions with 034, 035's behavioural half, 036, 037, 038 and 039 fully green, and exactly **three** failures — every one a `prosrc` / `pg_get_functiondef` SOURCE pin naming `draft_tick`'s body (035 §8's completion-writer delegation, 038 §135's R408 award-lookup scope, 040 §8's twelve-reserve-readers count). All three were RE-POINTED, none relaxed, and 035 and 040 each gained a **second** assertion so the delegation is pinned at both links rather than moved from one to the other. (4) **THE HEAD SET IS 092 FOR ALL FOUR, AND THE BREAKDOWN'S CITATIONS ARE STALE.** tasks-AP §AP.2 cites `089:2480–2671` and `089:658`; 091 and then 092 replaced those bodies. Re-derived at task time with `grep -lE '^CREATE (OR REPLACE )?FUNCTION +(public\.)?<name>\(' supabase/migrations/*.sql`, every claimed range re-checked to start on its own `CREATE OR REPLACE` line: `draft_tick` 092:2542–3749 · `draft_nominate` 092:2273–2529 · `draft_system_nominate_internal` 092:2155–2260 · `draft_force_pick` 092:858–1117. Per-function hunks: **3 (+17/−195) · 2 (+51/−9) · 2 (+33/−10) · 3 (+29/−2)**. (5) **THERE ARE THREE NOMINATION PATHS AND THE BREAKDOWN NAMED TWO.** `draft_force_pick`'s auction arm IS a nomination (087/R301 — a commissioner "pick for a manager" on an auction opens one at the floor, with its own `draft_bids` row and its own phase flip), and §8.6.9 is written about nominations with no qualifier on who opened one. Wiring it follows LAW rather than widening scope — tasks-AP's own preamble says the spec wins where the two disagree — and the precedent for this exact function being missed by this exact lane is **D214(1)**, where AP.1 found it absent from §1.3's read-site table. Pinned in 041 §F.
- **D215 (cont.) — the wire and the client.** (6) The uncontestable path performs two `drafts` UPDATEs in one transaction: the ordinary phase flip carrying an additive `"uncontested": true` and a **NULL** `current_deadline` (E67's "no bid clock is ever opened", made true on the wire and not only in the row), then the award. Both fire 070's row trigger, so the room learns of it with **no new column, event name or topic**. Two consequences worth writing down: **(a) the key never comes to rest** — both statements commit together, so by the time any SELECT can run `current_nomination` is already NULL, which is what makes §16.5.4's "a reconnect cannot lose the award", "a late joiner sees the completed award" and "never show it twice" structural rather than a matter of client discipline; **(b) `realtime.messages` exposes NO ordering key for two rows written in one commit** — measured: identical `inserted_at` (the transaction timestamp) and a random-uuid `id` — so 041 §H asserts SET MEMBERSHIP rather than a sequence. Under the corrected order that is exactly right: the award is committed either way, so a client processing the two payloads in either order paints the same board and shows the same message. (7) **THE CLIENT LATCHES AT THE PAYLOAD, NOT AT A RENDER, and it is the one non-obvious client decision.** Both events land in one commit, so React can coalesce them into a single render and a `useEffect` watching `current_nomination` would then never observe the marker at all; `useDraftRoom`'s broadcast handler sees every payload exactly once whatever React does with the renders. The 3 000 ms is ONE exported constant, the sentence is composed in ONE function (so Q18's ruling is a one-line change), the instant is read through `systemTime` — D3's one sanctioned wall-clock seam — and a PURE decision function decides while the timers only wake the component. **THAT SENTENCE WAS FALSE AS FIRST SHIPPED, AND REVIEW CAUGHT IT (R464) — recorded because the species matters more than the instance.** The first revision computed the decision against a `nowMs` held in component STATE whose only writers were the initialiser and a `setTimeout` callback, which made the timeout **the sole writer that could retire the message**: measured, it was still visible at t+4000 and t+9000, and background tabs clamp `setTimeout`, so that is ordinary rather than exotic. The docblock claimed the opposite in the proved register — **§4 rule 9 again, and the third time this lane has caught a claim about a post-change world written from the INTENT of the change rather than observed** (D214(5), R463, this). §16.5.4 is LAW that the beat is *"exactly 3 seconds … on every client"*, so **the code moved, not the claim** — withdrawing it would have left shipped behaviour violating the spec, which is the move AP.1's blocker punished. **As fixed:** the whole decision is `uncontestedBeatSentence`, a pure function of the latched beat and a sampled instant, and the component samples **at render** through `systemTime`, so every render re-decides and no timer can gate the answer; an exact-boundary `setTimeout` keeps "exactly 3 seconds" exact and a 500 ms `UNCONTESTED_BEAT_SAMPLE_MS` interval, cleared at the boundary, covers the clamped-tab case a timeout cannot. Every clock read on this path is `systemTime` — **the fix does not depend on F97's unfixed `Date.now()` and does not deepen it**, and the two hooks are deliberately not merged (they live in different components, so sharing one sampler would mean rehoming shipped L.C3.1 code and dragging F97 in). (8) **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE:** no server-side `pg_sleep`, scheduled action, `pg_net` or second cron (tasks-AP §4 rule 11 / D199(5)); **no client-side copy of the §8.6.9 predicate** — the server decides, and a TS mirror here would have been the third copy of the max-bid family that **F95** exists to prevent; no touch to `draft_place_bid` / `draft_place_bid_internal` (a bid can never meet an uncontestable nomination — pinned); no re-issue of `cron.schedule` (§22.3); no §7.3.8 knob (Chris ruled the rule, not a setting); and no fix to `draft-board-autopick-db`, which is `main`'s **F94** and was re-baselined this session on a `main` worktree against a `main`-chain database (`draft_nomination_uncontestable` present 0 times) failing identically.


**2026-08-17 — Architect (the draft-room redesign breakdown, PR #155 — merged 2026-08-17; transcribed verbatim from `tasks-DR-draft-room-redesign.md` §3 per the tasks-M2 D86–D101 / tasks-M3 D126–D143 precedent.** *Folded late, by the **DR.1** Builder on 2026-08-18: PR #155's own §6 owed this transcription "at merge" and the merge landed without it, so §4 ran D146 → D157 with the ten numbers D157 had just been renumbered around. Discharged here rather than left for DR.2 to trip over — the same PR also files the §6 row #155 owed, as **F63**.)*

- **D147 — The room escapes the shell by moving the guard up, not by duplicating it.** `src/app/app/layout.tsx` today does auth + username gate + `<AppShell>` in one component (:12–40). It splits: the **layout keeps the guards and becomes a pass-through**, and `<AppShell>` moves down into a route group `src/app/app/(shell)/layout.tsx` that holds every existing route, with the room in a sibling group `src/app/app/(room)/leagues/[leagueId]/draft/`. **Route groups do not affect URLs**, so `/app/leagues/[id]/draft` is unchanged — no redirect, no link rewrite, no broken deep link, and the `DraftBar`'s own-room path check keeps working. Chosen over the alternatives deliberately: a `usePathname()` conditional inside `AppShell` would make every app route pay for the room's special case and would still mount the shell's providers; a separate top-level `/draft/…` URL would break every shipped link and the spec's §16.1 route table. **The guard is not duplicated into two layouts** — one copy, above both groups, is what keeps cold-load auth honest (D148).
- **D148 — Cold-load correctness is an acceptance criterion with a named adversary.** A new browser tab is a server-rendered cold start with no client history, and so is a refresh mid-draft; the new-tab ruling makes this the *primary* path rather than an edge case. **Observation recorded 2026-08-17 (Chris, in two browsers):** loading the live draft URL directly bounced to `/app?redirect=%2Fapp%2Fleagues%2F…%2Fdraft` while in-app click-through worked. Two mechanisms exist and the Builder must distinguish them by evidence rather than assume:
  **(a) the dev-auth artifact (likely, and benign in production).** `devAutoLogin` (`src/lib/supabase/dev-auth.ts:26–45`) is a **client-side** `signInWithPassword`. On the very first cold load of a fresh browser there is no session cookie yet, so the server sees an anonymous request and `middleware.ts:36–42` redirects; the browser then signs in, and every later request has a cookie. That produces exactly the observed two-hop shape (`/app/leagues/…/draft` → `/login?redirect=…` → middleware's :45–50 branch sees a user, rewrites the pathname to `/app` and **keeps the search params** because it clones `nextUrl`, landing on `/app?redirect=…`).
  **(b) a real, production-plausible defect found while diagnosing (a).** `src/middleware.ts` writes refreshed auth cookies onto `supabaseResponse` via `setAll` (:18–27) but **both redirect branches return a brand-new `NextResponse.redirect(...)` (:41 and :49), which does not carry those cookies.** This is the documented `@supabase/ssr` footgun: a cold load holding an expired-but-refreshable token can be bounced *and* lose the refresh. It is not reachable through in-app client-side navigation, which is exactly why the redesign — whose primary entry is a cold tab — is what would surface it.
  **The task's obligation is to prove which one it is, on a real (non-dev-auth) session, and to leave a test rather than a memory** (DR.1, DR.8). Filed as ledger row **F63** so the routing is findable. *(Transcription correction, DR.1 2026-08-18: this sentence read **F61** when the breakdown was authored, and the entry's own §6 marked the number provisional per R312 first-filed-keeps. PR #156 filed F61/F62 first, so this row is **F63** — the number D158(4) reserved for exactly this re-point. Nothing else in this decision changed.)* *(Recorded but out of scope to celebrate: `login/page.tsx:24/:51` does honor `?redirect=`, so once a user logs in they do land in the room — the destination is preserved through the login page and lost only by middleware's `/login → /app` rewrite.)*
- **D149 — Three zones, two bands of chrome, and the on-the-clock line resolves INTO the status strip rather than becoming a third band.** The brief flagged three candidates competing for the top (the 54px bar, the Live/Round/order strip, and the on-the-clock line). They resolve to **two**: the command bar (54px, ink, pinned) and the status strip (`h-header` = 58px, the existing token). Chris's "move it to the left side of **the div**" is read as the div it already lives in — the status strip's flex row (`snake-draft-room.tsx:719–765`), where it currently sits **right-aligned next to the clock** (:743–759). Moving it left makes one band whose two ends read *whose turn* and *how long*, which is a better answer than a dedicated band and costs 112px of vertical chrome instead of ~170px. **A third band is out of scope and a Builder proposing one has left it.**
- **D150 — The dock is a NON-MODAL drawer, and that single choice settles most of its behavior.** The panels overlay the board; the board, the clock, the command bar and the presence strip stay visible and operable behind them. Therefore: **no focus trap, nothing `inert`, no scroll lock, no backdrop that swallows clicks** — a user must be able to watch the clock while browsing the pool, which is the entire draft-night workflow. Escape closes; clicking the active tab toggles it closed; **exactly one panel is open at a time** (two open panels is a rail again). Focus moves to the panel on open and **returns to the tab button** on close. Default state is **closed**. **This is deliberately NOT the shipped `Sheet`/Radix Dialog primitive**, which traps focus and marks the rest of the page inert by design — using it here would make the board unreadable while the pool is open. The dock is a plain positioned region with `role="tabpanel"`/`aria-expanded` wiring, not a modal.
- **D151 — Open height is fixed, and the board never resizes.** The open panel occupies a fixed fraction of the viewport (`min(60vh, …)` desktop / ~75vh mobile — the Builder pins the exact token) and is **absolutely positioned over** the board. The board's own geometry — the grid's `minmax(96px, 1fr)` columns and its horizontal scroll (`draft-board-grid.tsx:53–105`) — **must not change when a panel opens or closes**: a board that re-lays-out on every tab press is the thing a full-width board was asked for to avoid. No drag-to-resize in v1 (a resize handle on a drawer that overlays a horizontally-scrolling grid is a pointer-conflict problem worth its own task, not a freebie).
- **D152 — Elevation: the dock panels and the command bar are BOTH sanctioned resting shadows, and each says why in a comment.** CLAUDE.md's ruling is that nothing in normal flow rests elevated and shadows appear only behind an interaction prefix — **with an explicit exception for true overlays and for bars pinned over scrolling content**. The dock panels are true overlays (they float above the board); the 54px command bar is pinned chrome over scrolling content. Both therefore keep a resting `shadow-hard-*` **with a comment naming the exception**, exactly as `src/components/ui/elevation-rule.test.ts:38`'s `OVERLAY_FILES` allowlist requires of shared primitives — and any new file the test's sweep covers is added to that allowlist with its reason, never silenced. **Everything else the redesign touches obeys the ordinary rule:** the status strip does not rest elevated, and selected/on-the-clock/active states stay carried by fill (`bg-accent-soft`) or border (`border-accent`), never by a shadow.
- **D153 — `Draft Options` is a menu over the SHIPPED panel body, not a reimplementation of it.** CLAUDE.md forbids near-duplicate components, and `commish-draft-panel.tsx` is 956 lines of working, reviewed, refusal-aware controls. The menu lists the control groups; choosing one opens the existing panel at that section. **What actually changes in that file is its trigger** — the blue `Commish panel` button (:120–123) is deleted and the panel becomes trigger-less, opened by the bar. The eight sections keep their bodies, their gates, their confirm dialogs and their system-post semantics. **Nothing about §8.7's control semantics changes in this lane** — no new refusal, no relaxed one, no altered audit or chat behavior.
- **D154 — On a mock, the command bar is the launcher's bar, because a mock has no commissioner.** `isCommish` is already `false` on every mock (`snake-draft-room.tsx:443`, D110(1)). The bar's three variants are therefore: **commissioner** (Pause/Resume + Draft Options + status + Exit), **member** (status + Exit), **mock** (MOCK identity + status + Exit, plus — for `config.mock.launched_by` only — Pause/Resume practice and a reduced *Practice options* menu carrying delete-and-exit). The `MockBanner` at `:712` is **absorbed into the bar** rather than stacked beneath it (§16.5.4's v2.12 note): a permanent bar plus a permanent banner saying the same thing is the duplication §16.3's say-a-thing-once rule exists to stop. **No commissioner control becomes reachable on a mock** — the reduced menu carries only what D110(1) already permits the launcher.
- **D155 — The pause overlay stops narrating and starts illustrating.** With the bar announcing "Draft paused by @commish" for everyone, `DraftPauseOverlay`'s duplicate copy is retired; the board keeps a *visual* paused treatment (dimmed, non-interactive) and the clock keeps its shipped paused rendering (`pick-clock.tsx`'s paused mode). **The Resume affordance moves to where the actor is** — the bar's Resume button for a commissioner, the same for a mock's launcher — so `canResume`/`onResume` (`pause-overlay.tsx:38`, wired at `snake-draft-room.tsx:604`) lose their button rather than their meaning. One state, one voice, one place to act.
- **D156 — The two-tabs guard is a courtesy over a correctness boundary, and is scoped to say so.** *(**RULED by Chris 2026-08-17** — "The most recent one takes over and the others disconnect"; PROGRESS §3 **Q14** Resolved. This decision is now built, not proposed.)* The server is authoritative (§8.1), so two tabs can never corrupt a draft — a stale tab's action is refused by the same validators as anyone else's. What two tabs *do* cost is real but bounded: two sockets and two `draft:<id>` subscriptions against §9.3's ≤3-channel budget, two `draft_touch` heartbeats, and a presence list that shows one manager twice (presence is keyed by team id — `use-draft.ts:244`). The guard is therefore **client-local leader election** (`BroadcastChannel` keyed by draft id, `localStorage` fallback): newest tab holds the room, older tabs unsubscribe, stop the heartbeat, and render a takeover state. **Per browser profile, not per user** — a laptop and a phone are two legitimate clients and are left alone. **It adds no channel, no route, no server state.**

- **D188 — L.C2.2 build mechanics (the auction commissioner routes; no schema change).** **Number note (D161's grep-together rule):** `main` @ 6d5b1f6 is at R411 / D187 / F76 with ZERO open PRs; the parallel L.C2.1 Builder (the orchestrator warned it would file D188+) had pushed NO branch and no PR at the time of writing (`git branch -r` / `gh pr list` both checked, twice — at branch-cut and at PROGRESS-write), so this session takes **D188** and files **no F number** (it adds no hand-off: the one thing it leaves for a later task — the D141 disabled-with-copy UI — is already F72's remaining half, owned by L.C3.2); the re-grep is owed at merge, first-filed-keeps. (1) **THE BANNER'S ROUTE NAMES WIN OVER THE PROMPT'S PARAPHRASE.** The task banner (tasks-M3 L.C2.2 item 1) and the C40 row both print `POST …/draft/reverse-bid` + `POST …/draft/budget`; the orchestrator's prompt rendered them `reverse-won-bid` / `adjust-budget` while declaring the banner authoritative. The banner is LAW (approved PR #150) and the C40 disposition, the PROGRESS §2 row and the §15.2 erratum all cite its names, so the routes are `reverse-bid` and `budget`; the HOOKS carry the RPC verbs' names (`useReverseWonBid` / `useAdjustBudget`) because hook names are not in the banner and the verb name is the better handle in a panel. Recorded so a reviewer reading the prompt does not flag the route names as drift. (2) **`reason` IS REQUIRED ON THE FOUR — THE D114(1) CARVE-OUT, NOT A REVERSAL OF IT.** D114(1) made `reason` optional on the M2 verbs and REQUIRED "exactly where the task text mandates it" (then: the post-start order dispatch). The L.C2.2 task text mandates it for the four auction verbs — they are the money-moving (reverse = a refund, budget = a correction of other people's money), bid-voiding (cancel) and terminal (end — §8.7 prints "fully audited; cannot be silent") controls — so the four schemas carry `reason: z.string().trim().min(1).max(500)` non-optional, the builders take it structurally (the `orderRequest` shape: an empty reason is SENT as `""` so the route 400s rather than silently dropping the requirement), and probe B is what the requirement buys: with reason optional, a body-less `POST …/draft/end` ENDS THE DRAFT. The priced reassign/move keep their shipped optional reason (no contract change to a shipped verb inside this task). Stored nowhere still (F32/F40; `commissioner_actions` does not exist — the wire suite pins its absence by name). (3) **ZERO BUSINESS LOGIC IN THE ROUTE, AND WHAT THAT MEANT CONCRETELY.** Three temptations declined: a Zod `delta !== 0` refine (087 refuses 0 with its own 22023 copy — the route passes it through; the ops pin sends 0 rather than dropping it), a route-side "is the draft paused?" check for the gated verbs (D141 lives in ONE helper in 087/090 — re-implementing it would let the two drift; the route maps the P0001 to a 400 and surfaces the ruling's own sentence, which the wire suite byte-compares), and a confirm phrase on `end` (C41's hard confirm is the UI's — the strict body makes a smuggled `confirm` key a 400, pinned). The only shape fences added are the int4-safe `delta` bound (±1,000,000) and `price >= 0` (a $0 league is legal — 084; "below this league's minimum bid" is the RPC's). (4) **`action_id`: NONE, BY SIGNATURE.** 087's four auction verbs and 090's priced reassign/move take no `p_action_id` (checked against the CURRENT `pg_proc` identity arguments on the 001–090 stack, not assumed from the sketch), so none is minted or accepted — no invented parameter, no stamping contract to pin. Force-pick keeps its D114(4) REQUIRED action_id untouched. (5) **BANNER ITEM 2 ("existing control routes pass the auction args through") — THREE ARMS, NOT ONE.** `reassign`/`move-player` gain `price` (the orchestrator's contract); `clock` gains the three auction timers with `pick_timer_seconds` going optional and a "name at least one timer" refine (the same first check 087 makes — which clock a body may name for which draft type stays the RPC's ruling, and the wire suite pins the auction's pick-clock refusal passing through); the PATCH's order dispatch ALREADY edits `nomination_order` on an auction (087's set_order arm) — pinned over the wire, not changed. The clock HOOK was extended additively (`pickTimerSeconds: number | null` + an optional `auction` timers object — the panel's shipped `{pickTimerSeconds, extendCurrent: false}` call is byte-identical and DR.3's source pin stands) so the route has a client when L.C3.2 builds the auction clock section; its banner already carries "auction clock edits (pause-gated)", so this is a shipped hook arm, not a hand-off. (1) **F56's TWO RULES DO NOT CONFLICT — THE REMEDY WAS OVER-BROAD, AND THE SPEC SETTLES IT (R429).** Rule 1's first cut gave every no-draft branch one remedy: degraded or failed ⇒ the error-with-retry card. `degraded` means, by construction, *we hold last-good data* — which is exactly the state rule 2 (and §16.5.4's required-states line, which is LAW: *"degraded (banner + last-good data, never wrong numbers)"*) says must keep rendering. So the rule keeps its content — **an absence claim must be backed by a READ, never by a failure** — and the remedy now scales with what the surface can DISCLOSE with: a no-draft branch that can carry the room's ONE banner surface (§16.5.4 v2.12's 54px command bar) renders `degraded` as the spec's degraded state; one that cannot has nowhere honest to put a banner, and §16.5.4 forbids inventing a one-off treatment, so it renders error-with-retry. In this room exactly one no-draft branch mounts the bar — the **D94 scheduled lobby** (DR.7(4)) — so its `stale` prop, which R429 proved was a constant `false`, is now LIVE, and the other three (recap pointer, "no draft yet", "Draft not found") keep the gate. **Shape matters as much as the decision:** the scheduled branch was moved AHEAD of the gate rather than the gate's condition being weakened, because `!absentDraftIsHonest(health) && somethingElse` is an INERT GATE that a count pin cannot see (R430) — `auction-room.test.ts` now pins `if (!absentDraftIsHonest(health)) {` as a whole-condition literal ×2, and probe B2 shows the inert shape RED. **Not escalated to §3:** the stop condition is for a spec that is ambiguous or wrong, and §16.5.4 is neither; D191(3) is this same PR's own build-mechanics entry, and a fix cycle is where an over-broad remedy in it gets corrected. (2) **THE ANTI-SNIPE RE-ARM NEEDED A SIZE TEST, NOT A BETTER KEY (R428).** D191(2) scoped the detector to an unchanged `nominationKey`, which closes the NOMINATING→BIDDING false positive and (verified by the reviewer) the commissioner-clock and cancel-renominate attacks. It does not close **resume**: `draft_pause` writes `current_deadline = NULL` (069:353-357) and `draft_resume` writes `now() + deadline_remaining_ms` (069:485-492) — same key, strictly later deadline — and the only thing separating the two was the client having SEEN the null frame, which a missed frame removes. The separator that does not depend on frame delivery is SIZE: 085's `GREATEST(current_deadline, now() + anti)` (085:780-791) either leaves the deadline alone or lands the remaining at exactly `anti_snipe`, never more; a resume lands the pre-pause remainder. `ANTI_SNIPE_REARM_SLACK_MS = 1_500` covers §9.3 offset error and is deliberately small — slack is the width of the hole. Pinned in BOTH directions as stored literals, including the reviewer's own `T+18s → T+30s` numbers, D128's after-zero full window, a 400ms-late sample, and the exact 11,500 / 11,501 boundary. Residual, stated: a pause taken while the clock was ALREADY inside the floor window, whose null frame is also missed, still passes the size test — the announcement then names a clock the visible countdown agrees with, and a tighter lower bound would risk false-negating a real re-arm under load, which is the worse failure. (3) **THE COERCION'S COMMENT WAS THE BUG REPORT (R427).** D191(1) said the `draft_type === 'linear' ? 'linear' : 'snake'` coercion is "simply unused" on the auction path. It had two consumers: `boardInput` (grid-only, genuinely unreached) and `myNextPick`, which fed the SHARED status strip. `nextPickNumberForTeam` walks pure board geometry; the auction rotation skips filled rosters (§8.6.7(c)/E27), so the walk coincides with the nomination order in lap 1 and diverges permanently after. §16.4 zone 2 enumerates the strip's contents and "your next pick" is not among them. Suppressed at the source (`isAuction ? null : …`) rather than at the strip, so the claim the comment makes is now true. The cause was structural: the handler body lived inside a `useEffect` in `use-draft.ts`, and this repo has no jsdom and no testing-library, so no node test could reach it — the behavioural pins drove sinks they built themselves. The body is now `applyChatBroadcast` in `use-draft-feed-sink.ts` (whose own banner already promises "no React, no Supabase client … drivable from a node test"): same code, same two rules, and **no QueryClient** — the R271 league-detail refresh arrives as a callback, so the module keeps the import graph it documents and no cycle is created. - **D184 — L.C1.6 build mechanics: the void-event decision (F69), the bulk rule, the cross-run answer, the D134 client half, and a measured harness race.** **Number note (D161's grep-together rule + D176's merge-time lesson):** R, D and F swept together across `main` @ b2b1927 (#161 merged 2026-08-19 — no open PRs at filing) — tops at R400/D183/F73 (the `F97` hits are `spec-tier-view.md`'s hex, `D700` is not a decision id), so this session takes **D184** and files **F74**; re-grep owed at merge. (1) **A VOID EMITS AN EVENT — ONE PER VOID STATEMENT, NEVER PER ROW — and the two rejected options are recorded with their reasons.** The task banner's three candidates: (a) an `UPDATE OF voided_at` arm is right in KIND and wrong in GRANULARITY if per-row — D162 situation (c) stamps a whole run in one statement and R379 forbade "one event per row"; the shape taken is a **STATEMENT-level AFTER UPDATE trigger with OLD/NEW transition tables**, emitting ONE event per draft per statement naming the DISTINCT (seq, player) pairs voided. Postgres refuses a column list on a trigger with transition tables (0A000, measured live), so `UPDATE OF voided_at` is replaced by in-body discrimination `OLD.voided_at IS NULL AND NEW.voided_at IS NOT NULL` — pinned from three sides (zero-row stamp / non-void column / re-stamp each emit nothing). (b) "the drafts payload carries the voided seq" is REJECTED as the vehicle: every void site does update the drafts row in the same txn (the 'drafts' event always ACCOMPANIES a void, and 037 pins that accompaniment), but a client would have to INFER the void from side effects and still could not tell WHICH rows to strike — a fact about bid rows belongs on the bid event, stated. (c) "re-read on the next INSERT" is REJECTED: sufficient for cancel by accident (the same nominator renominates on resume), wrong for reset (the next INSERT is the NEXT run's opening at seq 1 — a held cache merges runs until it notices), silent for `draft_end` (no INSERT follows). The record `{voided_at, voided_count, nominations}` is bounded by nominations, not bids (a 180-nomination reset lists ≤ 180 pairs in ONE event) and carries no per-row data — amounts/teams per row would be the per-row payload by another name. Event name stays `'draft_bids'` with the operation as discriminator (D109(1)); the record shape differs by operation and that is stated at both ends. (2) **The consequence for the three writers is stated, and the undo's TWO events are pinned as a feature, not a wart:** `draft_undo` on an auction runs the helper's live void and then the rewind sweep — two statements, two events, naming DIFFERENT nominations (037 §F: seq 3 then seq 2, seq 1 untouched, seq 3's already-stamped rows not re-announced by the sweep). Emission ORDER is 087's statement order and cannot be read back from stored rows inside one pgTAP transaction (every row shares one `now()`), so 037 keys the pair by seq rather than claiming an order it cannot observe — the same reason every "latest drafts event" pin in 037 is an EXISTS/COUNT over records only the named step could have produced. (3) **NO RUN KEY RIDES THE WIRE (R379(b) answered):** the only reader that must SEE voided rows — 087's undo on-clock recovery — is server-side and scopes by `started_at` itself; a client feed holds LIVE rows only (`voided_at IS NULL`), and that SELECT is run-pure at its snapshot (situation (c) stamps the whole previous run before the next writes a row); §9.3's fetch-first on (re)join reads the new run alone. ~~and the reset's ONE void event empties a held cache anyway~~ — **WITHDRAWN as stated (R401, M3 batch 7, 2026-08-19):** the cache claim held only when the event was applied AFTER the data it post-dates. Mechanism: React Query REPLACES a query's cache with the fetch result when a fetch resolves, discarding every `setQueryData` made while it was in flight; the handler as first shipped applied events straight onto `getQueryData`, and the `SUBSCRIBED` join refetch opened exactly that window — a bid landing in it was lost, a void (cancel/undo/reset) landing in it was undone by the pre-void snapshot (zombie rows), and after a reset the run-1 zombies merged with run-2 rows at seq 1 until the next rejoin; the first fetch dropped events outright (`if (!rows) return`); no gap detector repaired it. The closure is D185's feed sink — the wire contract and the no-run-key answer are unchanged. Putting `started_at` on the wire would carry a column no client renders (§9.2) to solve a problem the event stream already closes — recorded so it is not re-derived as a payload gap; a future struck-through-history UX reads voided rows by REST scoped by the fetched row's `started_at`, the engine's own key. (4) **D134 on the client is KEY-PRESENCE-GATED, and tasks-M3 §2's compat claim is corrected, not repeated.** §2 called `DraftsBroadcastRecord`/`PickBroadcastRecord` "non-strict Zod parses"; they are plain interfaces with structural guards. The property that matters is pinned in BOTH directions: additive wire keys never leak into the cache because the reducers copy NAMED fields (forward compat — old client, new server), and a record MISSING the D134 keys (a post-088 client against a pre-088 database — the F12 push order is not the client's to assume) patches the 070 eight and leaves the cached `current_nomination`/`budget_adjustments`/`price` untouched (backward compat). `price` joins the pick-UPDATE identity for the R260 reason: D142's priced move may change ONLY the price, and a reducer blind to it would drop exactly that event (pinned: price-only UPDATE applied; reflected-including-price inert). (5) **The bid FEED is its own cache + pure reducer (the L.B3.3 chat precedent), not room state.** `use-draft-bids.ts` reads live history over the RLS member SELECT **paged past PostgREST's 1000-row cap** (the CLAUDE.md "exactly 1000 rows looked like the whole table" lesson — a bidding-heavy 12-team auction can exceed it), and `use-draft-bids-ops.ts` appends INSERTs tuple-deduped (no `id` rides the wire — D109(2); `(seq, player, team, amount, created_at)` is unique in practice and a D143 renomination at the same seq/player/amount differs by `created_at`) and strikes void summaries by (seq, player) — at any instant at most ONE nomination's rows are live at a seq (the D162 invariant), so the pair names an unambiguous set; a void naming rows we never held is inert (they are gone regardless; the join refetch reconciles). `use-draft.ts` folds `'draft_bids'` into that cache on the ONE channel and invalidates it on every confirmed (re)join; the DR.6 budget pin is extended with the positive half (`ch.on(… 'draft_bids' …)` present, the feed hook opens no channel). FIFO is load-bearing (pinned): an event arriving between the settle and the async cache notification must not overtake a held one (a held VOID of (seq, P) applied AFTER a fresh INSERT of the D143 renomination of the same P would strike the live row). (3) **Anti-snipe is implemented as `deadline := GREATEST(deadline, now() + anti_snipe)`, with the zero case as its own branch.** GREATEST states D128 as "the clock may only be EXTENDED": above the threshold the standing deadline wins (the countdown continues — Chris's own clarification), at the threshold the two are equal, below it the floor wins. The `auction_anti_snipe_seconds = 0` case is a separate branch on purpose — **and the reason was recorded WRONG at first landing; corrected in the batch-3 fix cycle (R329).** It is NOT that GREATEST would hand an expired clock "a fresh now()-based clock": at anti_snipe 0, `now() + make_interval(secs => 0)` IS now(), so the two forms agree on every LIVE deadline and `GREATEST(expired, now())` is merely now() — still due, not fresh. The branch is observable in exactly two states, both of which are the disabled extension declining to touch a clock: an ALREADY-EXPIRED deadline, which an unconditional GREATEST would REWRITE forward to now() (pinned, 034 pin 61, and it is the ONLY pin the probe reddens), and a NULL one, which GREATEST — ignoring NULLs — would INVENT (unreachable today: nominate always writes a deadline and the one NULL-deadline state is `paused`, which both verbs refuse first). **The counterpart is now recorded rather than silent:** with anti_snipe > 0 a bid landing after the clock already read zero receives a FULL FRESH WINDOW (`now() + anti_snipe`) — D128's letter, and consistent with snake's posture that the TICK is the enforcer of expiry, not the deadline column; pinned at 034 pin 62. **The exact-threshold instant is observationally a no-op** (flooring to 10s when 10s remain changes nothing), so the discriminating pins are threshold − 1s (floors) and threshold + 1s (does not), both pinned to the second against the transaction instant. (4) **The max-bid clause IS §8.6.8 at the bid layer, and it is pinned by its CONSEQUENCE, not only by its refusal.** Bids move no money (D131(2)), so no bid can break solvency; an AWARD of an over-large bid can. `max_bid = remaining − (open_slots − 1) × min_bid` is precisely the largest amount whose award leaves the winner exactly on the floor — so 034 simulates the award AT max_bid (solvent, at equality) and ONE DOLLAR ABOVE it (insolvent), and carries the cross-cutting property "no bid above its bidder's max bid exists in history", bracketed by a population count so the NOT EXISTS cannot pass over an empty table (R307). (5) **Validation ORDER is a UX decision, recorded: capacity is checked BEFORE the bid bounds.** A complete roster reads `max_bid` 0 (084's E27 branch), so bounds-first would refuse a full team with "over your max bid of $0" instead of "your roster is complete" — the message would be true and useless. (6) **MOCK AUCTIONS ARE REFUSED BY BOTH VERBS — a deliberate seam, not an omission (F61).** No auction mock can exist today (071's `create_mock_draft` refuses auction configs and a mock's `draft_type` is snapshotted at creation), so the refusal is unreachable; the alternative was silence, and silence becomes a hole the moment L.C1.7 lifts the 071 refusal — every league member could bid inside another member's solo practice until the D103(2) launcher gate is retrofitted. Bidder-team resolution for mock seats is genuinely L.C1.7's design (CPU seats bid through the tick, D132), so the seam refuses now and lifts there, with the two 034 pins flipping in that PR. Its sibling obligation is **F62**: 086's system nomination must keep the invariant 085 establishes — every nomination opens with a `draft_bids` row (`action_id` NULL for the system path, which is why C39 made the column NULLable). (7) **PROBE-ORDERING DISCIPLINE — learned by running the DoD probe twice.** The first shape of 034 put the E5 over-max refusal in the MIDDLE of a bid ladder; under the probe the refused bid landed, the next pin's bid became a self-raise, and that raised an ERROR outside `throws_ok` which **aborted the file at 42 of the then-84 asserts with a single RED** — the probe destroyed the evidence it was supposed to produce. Reordering so that each ladder's over-max refusal is its LAST act and comes from a seat that is NOT the standing high bidder gives the honest signature: **6 of 91 RED and the file runs to the end** (the count re-captured against the batch-3 plan; §F's new R330 identity block obeys the same discipline — its ACCEPTED arm first, both refusals from seats that are not the standing high bidder — which is why its own probe leaves 5 RED instead of aborting), including the property pin and the two population counts that show the refused bids landed. *Rule to carry forward: a break probe that aborts the suite proves less than one that leaves its wreckage on the floor to be counted — order the pins so the mutation's damage stays observable.* (8) **Recorded residual (no bespoke message):** a RETIRED seat's manager reaching a bid path would get 084's loud P0002 from `draft_team_budget` (R321) rather than a bespoke refusal. Deliberate — retirement is M4's, a retired seat is outside both the rotation and the invariant's team set, and a loud honest raise beats inventing UX copy for a state this milestone cannot produce. (9) **Break-probe results AS RUN (the R306 lesson), all three re-captured against the batch-3 plan of 91:** (a) the DoD probe — dropping `IF p_amount > v_max_bid` — turned **6 of 034's 91** pins RED: 48 (LA's $187 vs a $186 max), 81 (E25's $2 vs a $1-max seat), 87 (the same at min_bid 0), 66 and 88 (the two population counts: the refused bids landed), and **89**, the property pin — plus **2 of 3** cases in the wire suite. The NOMINATION-side max-bid pins (29, 79) stayed GREEN by construction — they are `draft_nominate`'s own §8.6.7(a) clause, a different arm in a different function — as did §G's solvency-consequence pair, which are privileged award simulations that never route through the probed function. (b) the R330 probe — removing the nomination-identity guard — turned **5 of 91** RED (44, 45 the two refusal arms; 46 the per-nomination row count; 66 and 88 the population counts), with pin 43 (the matching-identity ACCEPTANCE) GREEN by construction. (c) the R329 probe — replacing the zero branch with an unconditional GREATEST — turned **exactly 1 of 91** RED (pin 61), with pin 60 GREEN, which is the finding it was written for. All reverted; 91/91 and 3/3 re-verified. (10) **NOMINATION IDENTITY ON THE BID PATH (R330 — landed in the batch-3 fix cycle, before 085 ever merged).** `draft_place_bid` gained two OPTIONAL trailing arguments, `p_nomination_seq` and `p_player_id`, refusing on mismatch with §16.3's "just went off the board" copy; omitted ⇒ shipped behavior, so no caller broke. **Why the RPC and not the route:** the RPC is the server-authoritative boundary (spec §4/§8.1 — clients never compute, and every caller must be safe, not only HTTP ones); a route guard would leave the sim, the pgTAP suite and every future caller exposed, and L.C1.4's completion path awards on exactly this data. **Why BOTH arguments:** neither subsumes the other — `player_id` catches the ordinary moved-on case, and `nomination_seq` catches the two cases where the same player is live under a different nomination (D143's cancel-and-renominate does NOT consume the sequence number; an undone award returns a player to the pool at a later sequence). The route obligation is **F64**. (11) **RECORDED RESIDUAL — the E2 replay lookup is VERB-BLIND (R331, ledger row F65).** Both verbs replay on `(draft_id, action_id)` with no verb discrimination, so an action_id used by one verb returns a false success through the other (proven live). The contract is therefore per-verb and enforced at the MINT SITE (L.C2.1), and the three in-body shapes were each rejected with a stated reason: **narrowing** the lookup is forbidden because the UNQUALIFIED lookup under the draft lock is exactly what makes a duplicate action_id un-insertable (it is the recorded reason no `EXCEPTION WHEN unique_violation` wrapper is owed, and narrowing re-opens a raw 23505 on the PARTIAL `uniq_draft_bid_action`); **argument-consistency** discrimination contradicts R125 and the two shipped 034 E2 pins, which deliberately replay with DIFFERENT arguments and assert the original row comes back; and **position-based verb inference** ("an opening row is the earliest row of its nomination_seq") breaks under D143's cancel-and-renominate, which writes a second opening under an existing seq and would make the rule FALSE-REFUSE a legitimate reconnect retry in L.C1.5's world — a worse bug than the one it closes. A verb column on `draft_bids` would settle it exactly and is recorded as the option rather than taken (085 ships no DDL, and the table is L.C1.1's).

Its roster INSERT reads **`p.price`** — D111(3)/§12.7 for auction rows, and the identical NULL for snake rows because `draft_picks.price` is NULL there, so 066's literal `NULL` and this expression are the same value on every snake board (pinned from the snake side in 035 §I, with 026 owning the full chain). It also clears `current_nomination` (a no-op for snake, hygiene for an auction). (2) **E26 IS STRUCTURAL, AND THAT CHANGES THE DoD PROBE — disclosed rather than quietly substituted.** The task prints a probe of the form "drop the E26 branch". (3) **ATTRIBUTION IS READ OFF THE WINNING BID ROW, not inferred from the actor at the clock.** `is_auto := (the winning draft_bids row's action_id IS NULL)`, `made_via` follows — so a system nomination nobody raised is `autopick`, a human nomination nobody raised is `manager`, and a system nomination a human RAISED is `manager` at the raise price (all three pinned, 035 §D/§E). This is also what makes **F62 load-bearing**: with no backing row the award has no honest attribution and REFUSES by name, so the invariant is enforced rather than merely asserted (035 §H pins the refusal). (4) **`picked_by` is NULL on every tick-written award, deliberately.** §12.5's `draft_bids` carries no user column, so the only way to name a user would be `league_members` — which misattributes the moment a seat changes hands (§7.2.1: franchises outlive managers). ARM 2 takes the same posture for autopicks. The attribution that IS true — `team_id` plus the bid history — is the one recorded. (5) **A LIVE DEFECT WAS FOUND AND CLOSED, and it was MEASURED before any code was written.** 068's ARM 2 has no `draft_type` awareness at all (tasks-M3 §2 recorded the grep; 084 then made auctions startable). A privileged probe on `main` @ 9c81f7c — an 8-team $200/min-1 auction started through `draft_start_internal`, deadline rewound to now() − 60s, one `draft_tick()` — wrote `draft_picks(pick_number=1, round=1, price=NULL, is_auto=t, made_via='autopick')`, advanced `current_pick_number` and moved `on_clock_team_id` by `draft_team_for_pick`, with **zero `draft_bids` rows** and `current_nomination` still NULL: a free player, no nomination, no bidding. At deadline + 1s the same probe returned `held_for_grace: 1` and wrote nothing — the D102 grace hold was the only thing between a live auction and a silently snake-drafted board. ARM 2's claim and its under-lock re-verify now both exclude auctions; 035 §C pins it behaviourally. (6) **THE AUCTION'S K/DST DEFERRAL IS THE FORCED-ONLY ARM (D129(2), finalized).** `draft_autopick_resolve`'s OPEN-mode escape `current_round > total_rounds − 3` is snake/linear's: an auction has no rounds, and D126 makes `current_round` there the display-only ROTATION LAP, so inheriting the window would let a lap counter unlock kickers. One hunk, `draft_type <> 'auction'`, gated so snake is the same expression (022's E30 pins stay green). The boundary is pinned one unit short both ways against a SNAKE CONTROL IN THE IDENTICAL STATE (035 §G): same league shape, same pool, same picks — the snake seat takes the kicker, the auction seat does not. Item (6) also removes the resolve chain's dependence on `current_round`, which is what makes D126's "display only" true rather than aspirational. (7) **THE ROTATION SCAN AND THE COMPLETION DETECTOR ARE ONE COMPUTATION.** The next nominator is the first team after the NOMINATOR (not the winner — D157(2)) with `open_slots >= 1`, found by a single `CROSS JOIN LATERAL draft_team_budget` (the shape `draft_auction_solvent` itself uses, so rule 7 holds without n round trips inside the lock); the scan finding NOBODY *is* the completion condition. Two separate predicates could disagree — one cannot. (8) **§8.6.8 IS RE-VALIDATED AT THE AWARD, NOT TRUSTED FROM THE BID.** Bids move no money (D131(2)); the award does. `price <= max_bid` is exactly the condition whose award leaves `remaining' >= open_slots' × min_bid`, so re-reading the winner through the ONE family under the held lock is what makes the award solvency-preserving BY CONSTRUCTION. A violation is engine corruption (D131(4) makes budget edits refuse it) and is LOUD — no pick written, recorded in `auction_failures`. **Recorded residual — NO REMEDY EXISTS TODAY (corrected by R364, and DRIVEN rather than assumed).** The state was forged (an over-max `high_bid` with a backing bid row, so F62 passes and the solvency clause is what refuses) and put through the real verbs: tick 1 refuses loudly with `auction_failures[0]` naming §8.6.8, 0 picks, nomination standing; `draft_pause` → `draft_resume` leaves `status live, time_left −00:00:01, still_nominated`; tick 2 reproduces the IDENTICAL failure. **Pause contains the retry loop; it does not clear the nomination**, and `draft_cancel_nomination` is L.C1.5's and has not shipped — so the only recovery in this migration's world is `draft_reset` + `draft_start_internal`, which WIPES THE BOARD. Reachability, recorded and not filed: `draft_move_player` (069:946) has no `draft_type` guard and can shrink a live high bidder's `max_bid`, so a commissioner mis-click reaches the state before L.C1.5's priced validation lands — that arm is already an explicit L.C1.5 deliverable. The deliberate trade still holds: an insolvent award breaks a never-weaken invariant permanently, and a loud stall is recoverable — at the cost of the board, which is now stated at its real size. Loosening the clause by ONE DOLLAR turns **13 of 105** RED — including `draft_auction_solvent` going FALSE on the finished board, which is the D146 doctrine paying for itself. (9) **MOCK AUCTIONS ARE OUT OF ARM 2.6's CLAIM, and the consequence is recorded rather than guessed at.** They are unreachable (071 refuses auction configs; 085's verbs refuse mocks — F61), and L.C1.7 owns the CPU sub-arm (D132/D138). Until then a hand-built live auction mock is claimed by NO arm. **That sentence was FALSE when first written and is true now only because of R362** (see M3 batch 4): ARM 2.5 — the mock CPU think-time arm — had no `draft_type` predicate in its claim OR its under-lock re-verify, and its pick path is `draft_autopick_resolve` → `draft_apply_pick_internal`, the SNAKE writer. A privileged fixture (live auction mock, CPU seat on the clock, `cpu_speed: fast` so the think-time was due while the deadline was still 30s out, `started_at` fresh so ARM 1.6 could not pause it first) returned **`"mock_cpu_picked": 1`** and wrote `draft_picks(pick_number=1, round=1, price=NULL, is_auto=t, made_via='autopick')` with `current_pick_number` → 2, ZERO `draft_bids` and `current_nomination` NULL — the exact shape ARM 2's exclusion had just closed, through a second door. Pinned in 035 §J, including the fixture-is-DUE pin and the no-contained-exception pin, so the zeroes cannot pass for the wrong reason. **The general lesson, which is why this is item (9) and not a footnote: the claim "X is claimed by no arm" was inferred from the two arms the task was thinking about rather than measured across all of them** — the sixth consecutive defect of that species in this lane. - **D163 — ROSTER CONSTRUCTION IS NOT ENFORCED FROM THE DRAFT (Chris, ruled in session 2026-08-18; recorded in the L.C1.5 batch-5 fix cycle, R374).** Recorded because **nothing in `docs/specs/` carried it**: §3 Open said "None currently", there was no §4 entry, and `grep` for "roster construction" / "positional legality" across `docs/` returned nothing. **The ruling, in Chris's framing:** *"A user may draft 16 WRs — that is their problem to solve in free agency. The draft never consults positional legality: capacity is a pure count, and positional slots are a weekly lineup concern. It can be a legitimate strategy to draft only RB/WR and pick up a QB, K, DST and TE once the season starts. **But whenever AUTODRAFT is doing the picking or nominating**, it should first attempt to fill the remaining **holes** with the final picks rather than add positional depth — 'this roster's only open slot is a Kicker, so draft a kicker with the final pick.' A user can do whatever they want; autodraft should not leave them without a QB/K/DST."* **(1) THIS CONFIRMS SHIPPED BEHAVIOR — it is recorded with the evidence rather than as a new requirement, and every clause was verified before it was written down.** **Capacity is a pure count**: 084's `draft_team_budget` derives `open_slots = total_rounds − non-undone picks` (084:67) with no positional term anywhere in the family, and the v2.8.11 manual-pick rule ("slot validation at pick time = capacity only") is what the priced Manual Edit paths and `draft_nominate` both enforce (D129(1): "humans may buy a 3rd QB"). **The autodraft half is the forced arm**: the auction inherits the snake resolver unchanged at `086:648` — `v_forced := v_remaining <= v_unfilled` — so while a roster has more picks left than holes the chain adds the best available player, and once picks-remaining equals holes it fills the holes. **(2) D129(2)'s OBLIGATION IS THEREFORE DISCHARGED, AND IT WAS DISCHARGED IN L.C1.4 — NOT LEFT OPEN.** D129(2) closed with "(no rounds in auction; deferral holds until open slots force them — Builder finalizes the documented rule, pins the boundary)". The rule was finalized in the **C32 erratum (spec v2.12.1)** — §8.4's K/D-ST deferral maps to its FORCED-only arm because an auction has no rounds for the "final 3 rounds" escape to refer to — and **the boundary is pinned one unit either side in 035 §G**: "ONE UNIT SHORT of FORCED (remaining 2 vs unfilled 1): the auction seat still declines the kicker and takes an RB" (035:955) and "FORCED (remaining 1 = unfilled 1, a K seat among them): the deferral lifts and the kicker is resolved" (035:964), against a SNAKE control in the identical state (035:945). The parenthetical in D129(2) is marked discharged in place. **(3) THE C33 ERRATUM'S *FIX* STANDS BUT ITS *REASONING* DOES NOT, and the spec is corrected (v2.12.3).** C33 argued that §8.6.7(e) "can select a player the NOMINATOR cannot roster" and that (b) would then award an **illegal** pick. Under this ruling that is not a legality problem at all: capacity is a count, and §8.6.7(c)'s rotation-skip already guarantees the nominator has an open slot, so ANY player is rosterable by them. The system nomination still runs the nominator's own §8.4 chain — **no behavior changes** — but the reason is now **"so an absent manager gets a player their own board would have picked"**, which is a quality-of-outcome argument, not **"so the award is legal"**. A wrong reason attached to a right fix is how the next session justifies the wrong change. **(4) WHAT IS NOT RULED, and is deliberately left alone:** whether the autodraft hole-filling should look further ahead than the forced arm does (e.g. a soft preference for holes before the boundary), and anything about weekly lineup legality, which is M4's. No spec section moves for either.
- **D164 — M3 batch-5 fix-cycle mechanics (L.C1.5, PR #159; R367–R374).** **Number note (R, D and F checked TOGETHER per D161, across every open branch):** `main` @ 4930bd8 is at **R366 / D161 / F67**; the only other open PR is #152 (docs), which claims R≤311 / D≤144 / F≤59 — above nothing. This branch already holds **D162**, so the ruling takes **D163** and these mechanics **D164**, and the two new ledger rows take **F68** and **F69**. **(1) A PRE-WRITE CHECK AND A POST-WRITE CHECK ARE NOT THE SAME CHECK, AND CALLING BOTH "the E28 algebra" IS WHAT HID THE BUG.** R367: the priced Manual Edit paths asked `price <= max_bid` **before** the write. That question is about the world in which the pick has NOT landed. The stuck clock is created **by** the pick landing — the receiving team's `open_slots` and `remaining` both fall, its `max_bid` falls with them, and if it is the live high bidder its own standing bid becomes unaffordable. `draft_auction_solvent` cannot see it either, because a bid holds no money (D131(2)) so no derivation reads it: the team passes `remaining >= open_slots × min_bid` and the award is still refused forever. **Rule this cycle adopts: when a guard's subject is changed by the write it guards, the guard must be re-asked after the write.** The two questions now have two implementations at three call sites and ONE helper behind them. **(2) A SECTION THAT CANNOT FAIL FOR THE CASE IT CLAIMS TO COVER IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE MISSING PIN.** 036 §I is titled "the priced Manual Edit Mode paths" and its fixture (LG) is paused **with no live nomination**, so no priced-path pin could ever run against a high bidder. This is the same shape as R362 (an arm nothing swept) and R329 (a pin that could not detect its own mutation). **Rule: when a section's title names a surface, its fixture must be able to reach every state that surface has** — and "is there a state this fixture cannot be in?" is now a question to ask of a fixture before writing pins against it. §I(b) adds the world (LH) rather than editing LG, so §I's own boundary story stays readable. **(3) TWO MORE COVERAGE SENTENCES OUTRAN THEIR PINS — SEVEN TASKS RUNNING.** R369: the banner said §B swept member/commissioner/outsider/anon × INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (it swept member × 4 and commissioner × 2) and that "§H sweeps all eleven" mocks (§H is the reverse-won-bid section; §M swept four). R371: the banner said §G's decoy was "built through the REAL verbs … renominate the same player at the same amount" when §G's own comments say the renomination is the TICK's and the collision is forged privileged. **In all three the substance held** — the reviewer probed outsider/anon directly, and rebuilt the D162 collision through real verbs only (three rows at seq 1, two tying; pre-D162 lookup returns 2, shipped lookup returns 1). **Disposition: EXTEND THE PINS where the claim is the coverage you would want (R369, both halves), CORRECT THE PROSE where the claim was about provenance (R371).** A banner sentence being accidentally true is not a defence. **(4) A HAND-OFF IN A SESSION-LOG CELL IS NOT A HAND-OFF (R51, again — R372).** `voided_at`'s broadcast/payload treatment was deferred to L.C1.6 in a migration comment and a free-text session-log cell, with no ledger row and no amendment to `tasks-M3-auction.md`'s L.C1.6 banner (a file this PR never touched, written before D162 existed). It is now **F69** plus a read-list line. **(5) A DIVERGENCE YOU CHOOSE TO KEEP MUST BE PINNED AND SAID (R373).** `draft_set_order` refuses a pre-start order edit on an auction and accepts one on snake. **Disposition: PIN, do not align** — aligning would be a behavior change to a shipped verb inside a fix cycle, the auction's message points at a real editor (League settings / `nomination_order_mode`, §7.3.8) so it is a UX asymmetry rather than a hole, and which way it should align is the same standing product question F57 already carries. Pinned at 036 §K (auction half) against 023:1248 (snake half). **(6) "RED ON MAIN TOO" IS ANCHORED TO A COMMIT, AND THE MERGE TARGET IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS (R370).** F56's extension recorded the E2E failure against `main` @ 5a1bf1c; on the merge target 4930bd8 the failure set is **larger and different in kind** — `draft-live.spec.ts:162`'s `getByText('Draft lobby')` reproduces **in isolation on a clean stack** and is **DR.1 test debt**, not F56: DR.1 moved the room out of the app shell, so `PageHeader` writes a store `AppHeader` reads and `AppHeader` is shell chrome (the comment at `draft-lobby.tsx:188` on `main` says so outright). Filed as **F68**, owned by the DR lane, deliberately not fixed here. **(7) RECORDED COUNTS RE-RUN, AGAIN (D161(5) applied without being asked).** 036 grew 150 → 181, so all five original probes were re-run against the enlarged file; every original RED SET reproduced exactly (3 / 2 / 10 / 2 / 1), which is the evidence that the first record was honest. Probe 6 is R367's own: **10 of 181** — and its tenth RED is **§A's new no-drift source pin**, added in this cycle because "one helper so the three cannot drift apart" was otherwise unpinned prose, which is the same species of claim R369/R371 were filed for. - **D161 — M3 batch-4 fix-cycle mechanics (L.C1.4, PR #158; R362–R366).** **Number note (R312 first-filed-keeps, the FOURTH time this rule has been needed — and the fourth instance was created by this very entry):** this cycle renumbered R339–R343 → **R362–R366** against the open branches, wrote the rule down, **and then filed its own ledger row as `F66` without applying it** — `F66` was already taken by the held DR.1 PR #157 (the unmatched `/app/*` root-404 row). Corrected to **F67** by the orchestrator at review time. The lesson is narrower and more useful than "check the open branches": **check every counter, not the one that just bit you.** R and D were checked here; F was not, because the collision that prompted the check had been an R collision. Until #157 lands, `git show <open-branch>:docs/specs/PROGRESS-leagues.md` must be grepped for **R, D and F together** before any of the three is assigned.  D157–D158 are #156's, D159 belongs to the OPEN Chris-held DR.1 PR #157, D160 is this PR's original entry — so the fix cycle takes **D161**. The reviewer's own R-numbers collided the same way (R339–R343 against #157's R339–R361) and renumbered to R362–R366. **(1) A SECOND DOOR TO THE SAME WRITER IS STILL THE SAME DEFECT, AND "NO ARM CLAIMS IT" IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A READING.** 086 closed ARM 2's auction door with a probe it ran, then asserted in three places that a live auction mock is claimed by no arm — without running that one. ARM 2.5 claimed it and snake-autopicked it (R362). The general rule this cycle adopts: **a sentence of the form "X is claimed/handled by no Y" must name the observation that establishes it, and the observation must sweep every Y, not the two the task was thinking about.** The pin that makes it stick is not the zero — it is the pin BEFORE the zero asserting the fixture was genuinely claimable, and the pin BESIDE it asserting nothing merely failed (`mock_cpu_failures = '[]'`); a zero with neither is the CLAUDE.md "nothing happened means it worked" trap wearing a test's clothes. **(2) A COMMENT THAT JUSTIFIES A `LIMIT 1` IS A CLAIM, AND D143 ALREADY REFUTED THIS ONE.** "Unique by construction" was written about a triple that a ruled-but-unbuilt verb makes non-unique (`draft_cancel_nomination` does not consume the sequence number). The lookup was correct only by an ordering, and the tiebreak behind that ordering is `gen_random_uuid()`. **Rule: when the discriminator is a column you already have, put it in the WHERE — do not let an ORDER BY carry a correctness argument.** `player_id` is now in the WHERE and 035 §K pins the disambiguation with a decoy the ordering deterministically prefers. **(3) D143'S "OPEN BIDS ARE VOIDED" HAS NO SCHEMA REPRESENTATION, and 086 is its first consumer.** `draft_bids` is append-only with no UPDATE/DELETE policy for anyone (083, D131(2)), so a voided nomination's rows stay and merge under one sequence number for every reader keyed on `nomination_seq` alone. 086's award survives it; the room's bid feed, L.C1.6's broadcast and the recap have not met it yet. Routed into **L.C1.5's read-list in tasks-M3 §6** with the three options and the instruction to record the decision or raise a spec question — not left as a comment for someone to find. **(4) A REFUSED AWARD HAS NO REMEDY UNTIL L.C1.5, and pause is not one.** Driven, not reasoned: pause → resume leaves the nomination standing and the next tick reproduces the identical refusal (D160(8), corrected). **Rule: "Z can be recovered by W" is the same species of claim as (1) — drive W before recording it.** **(5) RECORDED COUNTS MUST BE RE-RUN WHEN THE FILE THEY COUNT CHANGES.** Adding 11 pins made "35 of 105" unreproducible, so all three original probes were re-run (D160(10)); the 1–105 sets reproduced exactly, which is the evidence that the original record was honest. **(6) A PIN THAT READS A WHOLE-TICK ARRAY REPORTS A NEIGHBOUR'S FAILURE AS ITS OWN.** §K's first draft asserted `auction_failures = '[]'` and went red under probes that break other worlds; scoped by `draft_id`, it is deterministic. The existing pins 79/87 read `auction_failures->0` and have the same shape — left alone (no drive-by) and filed as **F67**, with the mechanism named: `now()` is transaction-stable inside a pgTAP file, so every forced `now() - interval '1 second'` deadline ties and ARM 2.6's `ORDER BY current_deadline` breaks the tie arbitrarily.


**2026-08-14/15/16 — Architect (the M3 breakdown, PR #150 — merged 2026-08-16; transcribed verbatim from tasks-M3-auction.md §3 per the tasks-M2 D86–D101 precedent; D139–D143 fold Chris's 2026-08-15/16 auction-UI rulings, spec v2.10/v2.10.1):**
- **D126 — Auction state lives on the drafts row; phase is `current_nomination`'s NULLity.** No new state columns: `current_nomination` NULL ⇒ **nominating** (`on_clock_team_id` = the nominator per `nomination_order` rotation, `current_deadline` = nomination clock); non-NULL ⇒ **bidding** (`current_nomination = { player_id, high_bid, high_bidder_team_id }` per 065:121's printed shape, `current_deadline` = bid clock). `current_pick_number` doubles as the 1-based **nomination sequence** (§12.4's "sequence # (auction)"); `draft_picks.round` is NULL for auction rows; `current_round` tracks the rotation lap (display only). `total_rounds` keeps its D91 meaning (draftable slots = starters + bench) — it is the auction's per-team roster capacity, not a rounds count.
- **D127 — Budgets are always DERIVED, never stored counters.** `remaining_budget(team) = auction_budget + adjustment(team) − Σ price(non-undone picks)`; `open_slots(team) = total_rounds − count(non-undone picks)`; `max_bid(team) = remaining − (open_slots − 1) × min_bid` (§8.6.1). One SQL derivation fn family (§5), used by every validator — a stored counter could drift from truth; a derivation cannot. Commissioner budget edits need storage: **additive column `drafts.budget_adjustments JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`** (team_id → integer delta; spec-absent schema recorded here + erratum, the D102 precedent) — validated per E28 at edit time, room-visible (D134), history via the D97 system chat post until M6's audit rows. *Recorded nuance:* the settings-layer floor (league-settings.ts:541) uses roster_size incl. IR — deliberately conservative vs the engine's D91 open-slots; both stand.
- **D128 — Bid-clock semantics: a fixed window with an anti-snipe floor (the E6-consistent reading).** The bid clock starts at `auction_bid_seconds` when bidding opens (at nomination) and is **not** reset by bids; a bid landing with remaining < `auction_anti_snipe_seconds` resets remaining **to** `auction_anti_snipe_seconds` (§7.3.8's own words: "resets clock **to it**"; Appendix C L.C1: "reset bid clock to auction_anti_snipe_seconds"; E6: 3s left, threshold 10 → clock reads 10s). `auction_anti_snipe_seconds = 0` disables extension (pure fixed window). §8.6.3's looser "each bid resets the bid clock per anti-snipe" is read as "each bid applies the anti-snipe rule". **C34 flags this for Chris's read before build** — pacing is product feel; the alternative (Sleeper-style reset-to-full-per-bid) contradicts E6 as printed and would need a spec change. **RULED 2026-08-15 (Chris, in-session): CONFIRMED** — his own scenario language: 30s total clock; bids above the threshold neither reset nor pause it — the countdown continues uninterrupted (Chris's explicit clarification); a higher bid landing inside the final 10 seconds resets the clock to 10 seconds (his "bid with 3 seconds left → clock resets to 10"), repeatable. D128 as written is the LAW reading; no spec change.
- **D129 — Nomination discipline.** (1) Human nomination validates: nominator's turn, player undrafted, opening bid ≥ `auction_min_bid` AND ≤ nominator's max bid (§8.6.7(a)), **capacity-only fit** (open_slots ≥ 1 — the v2.8.11 manual-pick rule extended: need-fit is a system-path rule, humans may buy a 3rd QB). Rotation-skip (§8.6.7(c)) guarantees the nominator has an open slot, so the §8.6.7(b) nominator-award is always legal. (2) **System nomination (timeout) = the M2 autopick resolution chain run for the on-clock team** (queue → primary board → Big Board → ADP with need-fit; 068's `draft_autopick_resolve`) at an opening bid of `min_bid` ($0 legal when `min_bid = 0` — C38; R305) — this satisfies §8.6.7(e)'s "fits *some* team's open slot" (it fits the nominator's) and makes (b) safe; one implementation, snake and auction (C33 records the reading). K/D-ST deferral maps to the forced-only arm (no rounds in auction; deferral holds until open slots force them — ~~Builder finalizes the documented rule, pins the boundary~~ **DISCHARGED in L.C1.4, migration 086 — marked 2026-08-18 (R374/D163(2)), not left open:** the rule is finalized in the **C32 erratum, spec v2.12.1** (§8.4's deferral maps to its FORCED-only arm because an auction has no rounds), and the boundary is pinned ONE UNIT EITHER SIDE in **035 §G** — 035:955 "ONE UNIT SHORT of FORCED (remaining 2 vs unfilled 1) … declines the kicker" and 035:964 "FORCED (remaining 1 = unfilled 1) … the deferral lifts" — against a snake control in the identical state at 035:945. The forced arm itself is `086:648`, `v_forced := v_remaining <= v_unfilled`). (3) The **D102 grace contract carries to the nomination clock**: autodraft/no-user/FRESH seats system-nominate AT deadline; a STALE seat's nomination is held to deadline + grace, manual nomination allowed during the hold. (4) **No auto-bidding for absent seats** (§8.6.5/OQ 10) — grace applies to nominations only; you cannot be timed *into* a bid.
- **D130 — Award path.** Bid-clock expiry under the draft-row lock: winner = `current_nomination.high_bidder_team_id` (or the nominator at the opening bid when no raises — §8.6.7(b)/E26); write `draft_picks` (pick_number = nomination seq, round NULL, `price`, `made_via`/`is_auto` per actor: system-nominated no-raise awards are `is_auto = TRUE, made_via = 'autopick'`); clear `current_nomination`; advance rotation to the next team with open_slots ≥ 1 (E27 skip); next nomination deadline. **Completion = no team has open slots** → the 072 completion txn extended to write `acquisition_cost = price` (D111(3)); "budgets exhausted" (§8.6.6) is unreachable — solvency guarantees every open slot is affordable at min_bid, pinned as a property.
- **D131 — Auction reversals.** (1) **`draft_reverse_won_bid`** (§8.7's "undo a won bid"): targeted soft-undo of a specific auction pick (`is_undone = TRUE`) — player to pool, budget restored by derivation (free), the team re-enters the rotation if it was complete; live/paused drafts only (post-completion reversal is F44's M6 class). (2) **Undo/cascade (E29):** when a nomination has live bids, `draft_undo` FIRST voids the nomination (clear `current_nomination`; `draft_bids` rows stand as append-only history — "bids returned" costs nothing because **bids never hold budget, only won picks do**), then reverts picks; on_clock rewinds to the target nomination's nominator with a fresh nomination clock. (3) Undo is provably solvency-preserving (remaining' = remaining + price ≥ (open+1) × min_bid whenever price ≥ min_bid — pinned as a property). (4) **E28 extends to the live nomination:** a budget edit that would make the CURRENT high bid insolvent for its bidder is refused (friendly: void the nomination or reverse won bids first) — otherwise the close could award an unaffordable player.
- **D132 — CPU bidders: tick-driven, value-based, same validators (one implementation, two consumers).** Mock auction CPUs nominate via D129(2) (their own resolve chain) at humanized think-time (the D93 PRNG pattern) and **bid** via a seeded value model: dollar value = f(ADP rank, budget scale, roster needs) × (1 + seeded noise), deterministic per (draft_id, nomination_seq, team_id, pass) — a CPU raises only while `high_bid + 1 ≤ min(its value, its max_bid)`, at most one raise per tick pass per nomination (bids land ~5s apart — humanized pacing for free), with the near-buzzer tail falling out of the think-fraction distribution (anti-snipe becomes visible, §8.8). E62 by construction: CPUs pass the same server-side max-bid/solvency validator as humans. The sim's auction personas (L.C4.1) drive the same decision spine through real RPCs (D100).
- **D133 — Client Broadcast STAYS CLOSED (the D109(5) decision, made).** M3 adds no `extension = 'broadcast'` INSERT policy: the "bid-button pulse" IS the authoritative `draft_bids` INSERT broadcast (sub-second, already fan-out-cheap), and v1 auction needs no typing indicators. A member who could client-broadcast could forge a server-shaped bid event to the room — the same spoof D109(5) refused. Recorded as deliberate; revisit only with a named consumer + a forgery-safe event namespace (v1.1 at earliest).
- **D134 — Payload extensions (the §9.2 "columns clients render" rule, extended additively).** `draft_broadcast_payload` += `current_nomination` + `budget_adjustments` (neither is blind: the high bid is the room's centerpiece and §8.7 transparency wants budget edits visible); `draft_pick_broadcast_payload` += `price` (the board renders spend; 070's exclusion note is superseded by an auction that renders it — banner updated in place… NO: the exclusion note's migration is released — the NEW payload fn versions in 088 carry the updated banner, D137). New **`draft_bid_broadcast_payload`** (nomination_seq, player_id, team_id, amount, created_at — never `action_id`) + INSERT trigger on `draft_bids`, event name `'draft_bids'` — the exact name the M2 client's inert-default pin already proves safe (use-draft-ops.test.ts:351). Old clients strip additive keys (non-strict Zod, §2) and ignore the new event: no forced-upgrade window.
