**2026-08-07 — Builder (drop `profiles.display_name` — not a milestone task):**
- **D116** Dropping the retired name column (migration **077**; spec v2.9.1; closes the "separate, later change" D115(1) deferred). (1) **Why now.** D115 kept the column as an inert NULL because production ran the old schema and any DDL broke the site in one merge order or the other. The hosted-migration reconciliation removed that: production and the repo are in sync at 076, 69 rows, history clean (001-040, 048-076; the 041-047 gap is intentional per D50). The column is now dead weight with zero readers left after this PR. (2) **077 must be LAST, and stays last.** Thirteen earlier migrations read or write the column (001 creates it; 006, 019, 038, 048, 049, 050, 051, 060, 062, 069, 073, 075), so a fresh `db reset` only replays cleanly while the drop is the highest number. Those earlier files are deliberately NOT edited — they run before 077. Nothing numbered after it may touch the column. (3) **D115(4) is REVERSED, and this is the whole risk of the PR.** "The other five readers are left alone" was right while the column existed and was permanently NULL. Once it is gone the same five — `notify_list_followers`, `create_league`, `seat_league_member_internal`, `get_join_preview`, `draft_actor_name` — break at RUNTIME on the next call, because Postgres records no dependency from a function BODY to a column: the drop does not block, nothing fails at apply time, and the first symptom is a live error. `notify_list_followers` is the dangerous one — it runs on every list update and Lists is one of three launch surfaces. All five are re-pointed FIRST, in the same transaction as the drop, so no instant exists in which a live function references a missing column. (4) **The bodies are production's, not the repo's.** Each was dumped with `pg_get_functiondef` from the live database and edited by removing exactly the `display_name` term from its `COALESCE`; signature, volatility, SECURITY DEFINER/INVOKER, `search_path` pin, grants and surrounding logic are untouched. (Repo and production agreed for all five this time — verified — but authoring against the repo is precisely what caused the reconciliation, so the rule stands regardless of the result.) `CREATE OR REPLACE` updates the `pg_proc` row in place, so ACLs and any dependent trigger survive: 038's `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM PUBLIC, anon` on `notify_list_followers` is preserved by being left alone, not re-issued. For the record `notify_list_followers` is NOT trigger-bound — it is a two-arg `RETURNS void` RPC called from `src/lib/lists/helpers.ts`, and production has zero triggers whose body mentions the column. (5) **No observable behaviour change.** Every row's `display_name` was already NULL, so every chain already fell through to the handle. `get_join_preview` and `draft_actor_name` still render the BARE handle; `notify_list_followers` still renders `@handle` — D115(4)'s corollary stands. (6) **The drop is guarded.** A `DO` block counts non-NULL values first and raises rather than destroying one; the whole migration is one implicit transaction, so the function replacements roll back with it. `DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS` + an existence-gated, dynamically-executed check make a re-run a no-op. Verified before authoring: 6 profiles, 0 with a value. (7) **`ai_personas.display_name` and `expert_profiles.display_name` are untouched** — public parody brand copy and a dead legacy table, neither a person's name; pinned PRESENT so an over-broad sweep fails. (8) **pgTAP 023 fixtures move to handles.** It planted display names on three users for deterministic actor strings; those `UPDATE`s would no longer parse, so the pins read the usernames `draft_actor_name()` now returns (`cc_user_01/02/05`). 005's R31 slot becomes `hasnt_column`. New pgTAP **027** pins the outcome universally over `pg_proc.prosrc`, so a future function — or a `CREATE OR REPLACE` hotfix authored against a stale body, the exact failure the runbook warns about — fails loudly. (9) **`src/types/database.ts` was hand-edited, not regenerated**: typegen clobbers the hand-written alias block. Three lines removed, alias block md5-identical, diff is 3 deletions and nothing else.

**2026-08-05 — Builder (identity ruling — not a milestone task):**
- **D115** Identity-ruling build mechanics (Chris's ruling 2026-08-05; spec v2.9; migration 075). (1) **No schema change, on purpose.** The earlier attempt (PR #96) renamed `profiles.display_name` → `full_name`; three reviewers rejected it, and the deploy-order argument is the one that generalizes: production runs the current schema, so any rename breaks the site in one merge order or the other. Storing nothing needs no DDL — the column is NULLABLE with no default, so the old app reads NULL and falls back to `@username` (the post-ruling render anyway) and the new app never reads it. Dropping the column is a separate, later change once no deployed code references it. (2) **The stored names are cleared, not just stopped.** Accounts created before the ruling already carry OAuth real names, and `profiles` is world-readable, so stopping the write alone would leave the leak alive for exactly the users who hit it. `UPDATE profiles SET display_name = NULL` is DML, idempotent, and invisible to both app versions. (3) **The function body is production's, and the 049/050/051 guards are NOT re-imported.** The replacement is `pg_get_functiondef`'s live output minus the name write. That live body has no `*-ai` namespace rejection, no reserved-placeholder shape check, no R31 fallback: 049/050/051 were never applied to production (its ledger is 001-036, 073, 074), and 073's search_path hotfix was rebuilt from a pre-049 body, so a fresh local reset loses them too. Restoring them is a real bug worth its own PR — smuggling a handle-namespace behaviour change into a privacy fix is how the 051 regression happened in the first place. **Flagged for a follow-up, deliberately not fixed here.** (4) **The other five readers are left alone.** `notify_list_followers` / `create_league` / `seat_league_member_internal` / `get_join_preview` / `draft_actor_name` each read the column through `COALESCE(..., username)`. With it permanently NULL they resolve to the handle with no edit — and `CREATE OR REPLACE`-ing league functions that do not exist in production would plant orphans there. The corollary: `get_join_preview` and `draft_actor_name` render the BARE handle, not `@handle`; PR #96's cosmetic `'@' ||` prefix on those two is dropped along with its migration, and pgTAP 016/023/026 are back to `origin/main`'s strings. (5) **Personas keep their name, under their existing column.** The privacy rationale does not apply to a fictional analyst with no human behind it, and the "(AI)" suffix is a transparency device (spec-ai-expert-personas §4.6). Rendering `@bathew-merry-ai` instead of "Bathew Merry (AI)" would be an unrelated product regression. PR #96's `ai_personas.display_name` → `persona_name` rename is DROPPED: no schema churn in this PR. `expert_profiles.display_name` is likewise left alone — dead legacy, no reader anywhere in the app. (6) **Two-line identities collapse to one.** Surfaces that rendered "name" over "@handle" (account menu, profile header, follower rows, command palette) now render the handle once — keeping both lines would print the same string twice. `PublicListCard` and the explore feed gained an OPTIONAL `name`, set only for personas, rather than forking a second card component. (PR #96's render sweep, kept — reviewers passed it.) (7) **Account settings has no name field at all**, so there is no "private" copy to be wrong about. PR #96 shipped helper text promising privacy the database did not provide; the fix is not better copy, it is having nothing to describe. (8) **The one red vitest is the local stack, not the branch.** `invites-api-db`'s F2 `inviter_name` pin fails because the local Supabase DB has PR #96's abandoned 075 applied out-of-band (`profiles.full_name`; `get_join_preview` returning `'@'||username`). (3) **`draft_start` is create-if-absent** by composing the idempotent `draft_create` (D94's no-dead-end principle applied to the MANUAL path — a league scheduled purely through the settings surface has no drafts row and the Start button must still work); re-start of a live draft is a D63-class idempotent no-op (`started:false`, board untouched — pinned), and a live-draft-under-a-scheduled-league inconsistency refuses loudly rather than silently resetting a board. (4) **Seams as explicit refusals:** auction start AND auction pick refuse with friendly P0001s naming M3 (the 059 "lands in M2" precedent — M2 implements none of §8.6); `is_mock` picks refuse naming L.B1.6/071 so the human-turn path can never silently apply to mocks before the D103(2) branch is amended in (cross-referenced in the 066 banner and tasks-M2 L.B1.6). (5) **Lock order (CORRECTED by R122, batch 2 — the original "no cycle exists" clause missed the FK row lock):** `draft_create`/`draft_start` take leagues → drafts; `draft_make_pick` locks the drafts row explicitly and reads leagues/league_members/teams unlocked — BUT its draft_picks INSERT takes an implicit RI FOR KEY SHARE on the leagues row (the `league_id` FK, 065:152), so the pick's true order is drafts → leagues(KEY SHARE) and a drafts-row FOR UPDATE taken under the league lock while a pick is in flight DOES deadlock (live-proven 40P01 — the batch-2 probe; the victim can be the manager's pick). The discipline that prevents it (the R122 fix): draft_start's idempotent no-op arm reads the drafts row WITHOUT locking it, and the drafts-row FOR UPDATE is taken only BELOW the `scheduled` league gate, where no pick's INSERT can be in flight (picks require 'live'; start moves draft + league in one txn under the league lock) — structural prosrc pin in pgTAP 020. The league row stays explicitly unlocked in the pick path (heartbeats must not contend, D102; a removal racing a pick = at most one in-flight pick lands, identical to §7.2.1's removal-on-the-same-pick-clock semantics — recorded, not "fixed"). No commissioner bypass exists in `draft_make_pick` (pinned): the force path is L.B1.4's. (6) **E2 replay semantics:** the replay short-circuit runs BEFORE status/turn checks and returns `{draft, pick}` — the ORIGINAL pick row + the CURRENT authoritative draft state, with no outcome discriminator — so an immediate replay is byte-identical (pinned via GUC-captured text and wire deep-equal). **Completion counts live (non-undone) picks** rather than inferring from `current_pick_number` (robust against 069's undo rewinds) and is mock-sufficient per the task banner: `drafts.complete`/`completed_at` only, the league deliberately STAYS `drafting` — pgTAP pins that, and 072 flips the pin when the transition + `league_rosters` land. (7) **Slot-fit reading recorded:** need-fit/K-D/ST deferral are AUTOPICK-only rules (§8.4 frames them under "Autopick strategy"); a manual snake pick needs no per-position validation because the advance math guarantees each team exactly `total_rounds` picks and rounds = draftable spots (D91) — recorded so 068 doesn't "fix" manual picks by mistake. (8) The §7.3.8 defaults mirrored in SQL COALESCEs (`snake`/`random`/90/false) restate the spec's printed D column as defense against a bare `'{}'` blob — the settings catalog remains the source of truth on every sanctioned write path. (9) **Held-lock proof form (§4.6):** the stack vitest asserts `min(pick RTTs) < 50ms` — the client RTT upper-bounds the in-RPC lock window, a systematically held lock inflates EVERY sample, and a one-off load spike cannot flake the suite; timing via `process.hrtime.bigint()` (monotonic, outside the D3/D17 wall-clock ban — harness measurement, not league logic).

- **D26** Synthetic-tier design points. (1) **PRNG streams are keyed by (seed, playerId) only — never scenario id** (FNV-1a + mulberry32, `synthetic/prng.ts`): same-seed scenarios share stat lines, which is what makes the `provider_outage` back-fill proof an *equality against a same-seed `happy_path` world* instead of a self-referential recomputation. (2) **Skeleton/values split:** the timing/event skeleton (slate, kickoffs, event instants, player pool, inactives) is a fixed function of scenario id; only stat values draw from the seed — asserted by the "different seed → different lines, same skeleton" transcript test. (3) Stat lines are `floor(finalLine × progress)` — in-game deltas monotone by construction, outage recovery is cumulative back-fill for free (§23.2). (4) The synthetic tier supplies **real `kickoffAt` timestamps** (plus `gameDate` derived from them) — it's the tier that *can* (§23.6); flex/postponement reveal their new kickoff only from `announceAt`. D6's format ("one line per provider call") gains a line-1 metadata header `{format: 'fieldscout-fixture', version: 1, provider, season, week}` — additive, versioned, and parse-rejected loudly on mismatch. Rationale: the D24 self-review note — fixtures carry source semantics downstream branching doesn't know; the recorded provider's identity must live IN the artifact, not be guessed from its path. `RecordingStatsProvider` stays a transparent wrapper (exposes the inner provider's `name`/`capabilities`; the header is written by the harness/CLI that owns the file).

PG17's MAINTAIN; "7" was a miscount, per R2) to the three API roles, and the default ACLs are exactly as D18 recorded. **ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES chosen over per-table grants** because production *is* a default-ACL model: with per-table grants only, any future migration that omitted a grant (by oversight or on purpose) would silently diverge from prod, which auto-grants regardless; the versioned default ACLs replay to prod's exact model in every environment — fresh local reset, and a future re-provisioned hosted project on the new no-auto-grant default. **[Corrected 2026-07-19 per R1 — the original entry claimed the migration was "pushed to prod itself"; it was not.]** What actually happened: 037 was applied locally only; the local grant/default-ACL state after a fresh reset was verified byte-identical to prod's (grants + `pg_default_acl` comparison). **037 has NOT been pushed to prod** — prod's migration history still ends at 036. Deliberate narrowing (e.g. an internal service-role-only function) must be an explicit REVOKE in that migration.** *Carve-out (R5, 2026-07-19): "RLS is the only effective gate" holds for tables only — SECURITY DEFINER routines bypass RLS, so every one needs in-body auth (plan §8.3, spec §12.0) plus explicit REVOKE discipline; first instance `038_notify_list_followers_auth.sql`.* pgTAP `001_api_grants.sql` pins the surface (witness-table grants, default-ACL canary table + function, RLS-still-gates behavioral check) so a CLI behavior change fails loudly there. *Process note (R6, 2026-07-19): plan §8.1's staging-clone rehearsal line was skipped for 037 without a recorded waiver — recorded now: no staging clone exists (environments are local + prod only); the fresh local `db reset` replay plus the byte-identical grants/`pg_default_acl` comparison against prod served as the rehearsal evidence. **2026-07-21 — Builder (M1 batch-5 findings remediation, R57–R61):**
- **D58** Scoring-module failure semantics for corrupt inputs (the two R58/R59 rulings, both pinned by test). **(1) R58 — an unmappable tier source value is UNREPORTED (family absent → pending), never an all-zero delivered family.** The decision hinged on whether the published bucket tables are real-contiguous (which would justify clamping/flooring a fractional value into a bucket) or integer-gapped: they are **integer-gapped** — ESPN's Scoring-Formats article prints PA `1–6 / 7–13 / 14–17 / …` and YA `100–199 / 200–299 / …` (re-verified value-for-value by the batch-4 review), leaving real-valued gaps between adjacent buckets (13.5, 99.5), so the tables' domain is the integers and there is no defensible bucket to clamp into. Consequence: `familyMaps` requires an INTEGER inside ≥1 bucket; a fractional value is out-of-domain even when it happens to sit inside an interval (14.5 pends the family, same as 13.5 — no partial acceptance of corrupt data), and a negative PA (below `def_pa_0`'s pinned floor) pends. Pinned at the exact review-probed gap values (PA=13.5, YA=99.5, negative PA, plus in-interval-fractional PA=14.5); the one-hot property extended beyond integers (fractional/negative/non-finite sweep) asserting *delivered ⇔ integer-in-a-bucket, and delivered ⇒ exactly one hot per platform set*; a named counter-pin proves the all-zero-family state (and partial-family emission) is unconstructible. **(2) R59 — a corrupt rules coefficient THROWS (TypeError naming every offending key), the loud option:** a non-finite-number coefficient in `scoring_rules_snapshot` is corrupt config, not missing data — marking it pending would misbadge corrupt config as "waiting on stats" (the reviewer's own analysis), and letting it through NaN-poisons a total `NUMERIC(8,2)` will store (Postgres numeric has NaN — live-verified in the review). Validation runs up-front over all rules keys (including keys with no delivered stat — corrupt config is never quietly parked as pending); string-numerics (`"0.5"`) throw too, since silent coercion masks the corruption the L.A1.11 freeze should have caught. Pinned: NaN can never reach the return value — every adversarial coefficient shape either throws TypeError or yields a finite total, plus a finite-total assertion inside the 250-run property. The M4 worker (L.D1) decides catch-and-quarantine vs fail-the-run at the call site (F23's composition row is where that lands); the module's contract is simply *never emit a poisoned or silently-wrong breakdown*. **(3) R61 taken:** the round(full sum)≠Σ(rounded perKey) rule now has a stored-literal discriminating pin (`{a:0.111,b:0.111}×{a:3,b:3} → 0.67`; Σ-of-rounded yields 0.66) beside the statistical property. **(4) R57's spec fold-back is v2.8.4** (§7.3.3 parenthetical + changelog; header Version field corrected 2.8.1 → 2.8.4 in passing — it had been stale since v2.8.2).

No typegen re-run: no signature changed). **(1) R90 — the one real invariant hole, and the fixture blindness that hid it.** `leave_league`/`remove_manager` moved `teams.owner_id` only on the departing member's OWN franchise, so every placeholder seat they had minted as commissioner stayed owned by a proven non-member on `teams.owner_id REFERENCES profiles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` (001:495) — that account's deletion would destroy those franchises AND, via `league_members.team_id ON DELETE SET NULL` (052:67), leave cache rows with `team_id` NULL: a seat with no franchise, invisible to every capacity count, i.e. **the exact shape the S2 policy drop / erratum v2.8.8 / D74(3) exists to make unrepresentable**. 063's own banner named the hazard as the reason it moves `owner_id` at all, then covered one franchise out of N. Fixed as ONE league-wide sweep per departure path (`WHERE league_id = … AND owner_id = <departing> AND id <> v_team.id` → the acting commissioner; `leave_league` guards on a non-NULL commissioner). **Why 142 asserts missed it:** every L2 seat in the fixture was later claimed or assigned, which moves `owner_id` as a side effect — so the residual could only appear on a seat that is minted and then NEVER filled, a shape no fixture had. Both new fixtures ('Ledger Seat', 'Creator Seat') exist purely to be un-filled. Lesson for the ledger's sake: *a fixture that always exercises the happy path of a side effect cannot detect a missing sweep.* **(2) R93 — authorization re-read UNDER the lock, all five RPCs.** Four of them evaluated `is_league_commish` BEFORE `leagues … FOR UPDATE` and never again, so an actor demoted while blocked on that lock still completed one privileged write; `leave_league` alone had it right and its comment said why. Each of the four now re-reads the actor's role after the lock and gates on it (`NOT IN ('commissioner','co_commissioner')` → 42501). Two deliberate choices: the pre-lock `is_league_commish` call is **kept**, because dropping it would make a nonexistent league answer P0002/404 instead of 42501 — an existence leak the SQLSTATE convention explicitly forbids — so it is a fast-fail, not the gate; and `set_member_role`/`remove_manager` fold their existing exact-role read INTO the re-gate rather than reading twice (that read is what the creator anti-coup guards key on, which is the aggravating half: a stale actor reading `'manager'` was strictly MORE powerful than a legitimate co-commissioner, since every anti-coup guard keys on `'co_commissioner'`). **(3) R93's pin is STRUCTURAL, and that is a considered exception.** The guard fires only when a demotion commits while a call waits on the league row; both reads hit the same table in the same transaction, so no single-session pgTAP fixture can reach it and a two-session race test would be nondeterministic (the house does not ship flaky pins). §R therefore asserts, per RPC, that the actor-role re-read appears AFTER the first `FOR UPDATE` in `pg_proc.prosrc`. It is falsifiable in exactly the claimed way — deleting OR hoisting a re-gate fails exactly one assert, which names its RPC (probe 2 shown). **(4) R94 — replaying a completed transfer.** 063's banner promised D63 idempotency for `set_member_role`, but the headless-league guard was unconditional in `p_role` and sat ahead of the idempotent arm, so the natural retry — the transferor's own client, now a co_commissioner, resending the same PATCH — died on P0001/400 with copy asserting the target is not commissioner. - **D71** PATCH settings partial semantics — **merge-over-current** (the R79 ruling; supersedes D70(1)'s full-object wire contract on the partial-body point). (1) **The hole:** the declared "settings = the FULL L.A1.6 contract object" contract was unenforced — every `leagueSettingsSchema` field default-fills, so a one-key body (`{settings:{median_game:true}}`) parsed clean and silently reset the ENTIRE settings surface to catalog defaults (review live-proof: team_count 14→12, faab_budget 777→100 with the §12.2 re-seed amplifying it to every seat's balance, and `draft.draft_scheduled_at` NULLED while status stayed `scheduled` — exactly the state the gate-item-3 enforcement point exists to prevent). (2) **The choice, merge over reject-partial:** merge is the REST-correct PATCH reading, matches what L.A2.4's settings panel will send (per-group saves — the panel can send just its group), and a FULL object merges to itself so the sanctioned GET-detail → edit → PATCH-back round-trip is byte-identical to before; reject-partial would have forced every client to always send full objects and still needed a deep-required schema variant to close the NESTED variant of the same hole (a partial `draft` block default-filling `draft_scheduled_at` to null). (3) **Mechanics:** the settings path ALWAYS reads the CURRENT stored settings first (RLS-scoped client, same service call) and deep-merges the raw partial over them — plain objects merge recursively; arrays, scalars, and null REPLACE wholesale (null is a VALUE for the nullable fields — deliberately NOT RFC-7386 key-deletion); `undefined` skipped (unrepresentable in JSON). The MERGED WHOLE then re-enters the ONE canonical strict schema (unknown keys at ANY level reject; no default can ever fill — the current row supplies every key) and `validateLeagueSettings` (cross-field rules run against the merged whole). The partial input is validated POST-merge through the single catalog schema — no hand-maintained deep-partial schema, so the D60(10) anti-pattern stays dead; the wire schema's `settings` is now `z.looseObject({})` (any JSON object; shape enforced post-merge). (4) **Deliberate consequences:** (a) read-first means an RLS-invisible league uniformly **404s** on the settings path (was 403 via the RPC's 42501) — matching the status path and GET detail and fixing the pre-D71 inconsistency where a scoring-only PATCH already 404'd on invisible leagues while a settings PATCH 403'd; no existence leak either way (non-member and nonexistent stay indistinguishable), and a MEMBER non-commish still 403s from the RPC — pinned with a privileged-seat fixture (service-role `league_members` insert; real-user membership is RPC-only until L.A1.14). (b) The read-merge-write is NOT held under the RPC's row lock — D70's last-write-wins-wholesale concurrency caveat extends to interleaved read-merge-write (single-commissioner M1 reality; revisit if co-commissioner concurrent edits become real). (5) **Pins (round-trip suite 68 → 74):** the EXACT R79 probe is the regression trap (a scheduled 14-team faab-777 league with a draft instant: `{settings:{median_game:true}}` → 200 changing ONLY `median_game` — whole-object equality with one delta, plus by-name pins on team_count/max_teams 14, budget 777, seat balance 777 NOT re-seeded, draft instant + `scheduled` status intact), nested one-key merge inside `draft` (instant survives), merged-whole cross-field reject (`{regular_season_weeks:15}` alone breaks the Q10 seam post-merge → per-field 400 + no-write), unknown-key rejects top-level AND nested, and full-object identity. Deliberate-break probe: reverting the merge to the pre-D71 parse fails 4/5 trap tests on exactly the team_count 14→12 reset (shown, reverted). (6) **Companions:** R80 → spec erratum **v2.8.7** (§12.2 re-seed folded in, one sentence + changelog — D70(4) is the recorded rationale); R81 → ledger **F28** (shrink-below-occupancy); R82 → the top-level unknown-key PATCH pin in the wire-shape test (the R77-class discriminating pin: sent alongside a valid key, a plain z.object would strip-and-200). No migration/pgTAP/typegen change — 061, 015, and the generated Functions surface are untouched.

So the payload builder became a pure op, `auctionTimerPayload`, which clamps each box into `AUCTION_TIMER_RANGES` (§7.3.8's literals) and includes a key only when the CLAMPED value differs from what is stored; an empty or unreadable box means *unchanged*, never a guess. **The label and the clamp now read the same literals** — `TimerInput` takes a `range` and renders `` `${min}–${max}s` `` from it — so the two cannot drift apart again, which is the actual defect this finding names. **Route and RPC deliberately unchanged**, and pinned as unchanged: they are the backstop, not the enforcement, and server-authoritative is untouched — the UI simply stops proposing a number its own label calls illegal. | F218 | **THE INGEST WRITE PAIR (queue → stats) IS TWO POSTGREST CALLS, NOT ONE TRANSACTION — AT-LEAST-ONCE TODAY, ATOMIC LATER; UNTIL THEN THE WORKER MUST HONOUR THE READINESS PREDICATE.** L.D2.1's fix round (R706, D303(2)) writes `score_fanout` BEFORE `player_stats` so a crash between the two calls is recoverable (the stored row stays stale → the next poll re-detects and re-enqueues; pinned). What that leaves: **(a)** a delta can be queued whose stats have not landed yet — briefly on every poll (the gap between the two calls), indefinitely after a crash until the next poll. Both stamps are the ONE injected instant, so **`player_stats.updated_at >= score_fanout.enqueued_at` is the readiness predicate** (pinned equal on a clean poll; pinned older-than after a simulated crash): **L.D2.2's drain must leave a queued player whose stat row is older than its queue row — or absent — in the queue and score it on a later drain, never from the stale row** (pin it with the same crash fixture: drain during the gap → 0 scored / row still queued; the next poll lands the stats → scored on the next drain). **(b)** The permanent fix is one transaction for both writes — an `ingest_write_batch(p_rows jsonb, p_now timestamptz)` SECURITY DEFINER RPC (rules 9/§4.1: in-body service-role check, `search_path=''`, REVOKE) or the L.D1.9 `score_write_week_batch` family extended to the ingest side — owned by L.D2.3 (which rebinds the cron, F216) or L.D1.9 (which opens the write door), whichever lands second; when it lands, the predicate becomes a defence-in-depth pin rather than a correctness requirement, and D303(2) gets the note. Not a STOP: §23.2 asks for idempotent, diff-aware upserts and "no league state advanced on partial data", both of which hold — the queue is not league state, and a duplicate enqueue is a no-op by PK. **[amended at merge, 2026-09-02 — R714]:** the predicate alone has a liveness hole: a crash between the two calls followed by a poll whose line for that player EQUALS the stored (stale) row writes nothing, so `updated_at` never reaches `enqueued_at` and the queue row is orphaned — invisible to §23.2 because the stored row is by then correct. **L.D2.2's readiness rule must carry an orphan escape: ready if `player_stats.updated_at >= score_fanout.enqueued_at` OR a later poll for `(season, week)` completed after `enqueued_at`** (the persisted last-poll-completed surface is F217's vehicle); pin the orphan fixture (crash, then an identical re-poll) beside the crash fixture. | D303(2)/(11), R706 | L.D2.2 (the predicate at the drain) · L.D2.3 / L.D1.9 (the single-transaction door) | ⬜ Open |

### Should-fix

- **R22 · should-fix · .eslintrc.json:50 — refs: D3/R15 ("mechanical, not convention"); D26 item 5.** The new `Math.random` guard did not inherit the R15 widening the Date guard got. Empirically probed via ESLint stdin against `src/lib/leagues/**`: `globalThis.Math.random()` and `const M = Math; M.random()` are both **lint-clean** — the exact two escape shapes (globalThis routing, constructor/object aliasing) R15 closed for `Date`. `crypto.getRandomValues(...)` is also unbanned (a common "random" reach). D26 records "two new D3-style lint selectors," but the shipped guard is strictly narrower than the D3 guard it cites. Add `MemberExpression[object.name='globalThis'][property.name='Math']`, Math-aliasing selectors, and (optionally) a crypto.getRandomValues ban.
- **R23 · should-fix · synthetic-stats-provider.test.ts:128 + scenarios.ts:21 — refs: §23.6 ("versioned, deterministic, re-runnable"); D26 (library versioning).** No test pins any concrete PRNG-derived stat value against a stored golden constant. Both determinism tests compare two in-process runs of the same code (`fullWeekTranscript` twice; outage vs happy_path), so an *unintended* behavior change — a draw-order refactor in `finalLine`, a range tweak, a `mulberry32` edit — changes every scenario's "deterministic" world while the entire suite stays green. That defeats the versioning contract the schema declares ("bump `version` on ANY behavior change"): nothing can detect an unversioned behavior change, and any future fixture/simulator run pinned against library v1 silently diverges. One golden test (e.g. the full DEFAULT_SEED stat line for one player per position, as literals) makes version bumps mechanical instead of honor-system.
- **R24 · should-fix · live-stats.test.ts:40 — refs: the falsifiability standard this batch claims throughout; §23.2.** The seam's game-window boundary is the one instant-sensitive edge in this diff with **no** boundary pin: tests run mid-window (18:00Z on game day) and 3 days out, never at `kickoffDay` exactly or `kickoffDay + 36h` exactly (live-stats.ts:163 — both edges inclusive). An off-by-one in either comparison (`>=`→`>`, `<=`→`<`) passes the suite. Two exact-instant cases close it; the window semantics are load-bearing for the finalization pass (`weeksToFinalize` gets `inWindow` from this check).

### Nit

- **R25 · nit · synthetic-stats-provider.ts:249 — refs: D25 ("provider-reported calendar day").** Synthetic derives `gameDate` from the kickoff's **UTC** day, so the SNF game (Sun 8:20pm ET) reports Monday `2026-09-21`, while the sleeper tier reports the ET day (checked-in 2025 fixture: Sunday games carry the Sunday date). Literally D25-compliant but a cross-tier semantic drift in the same field: composed with the seam's UTC-day-start+36h window it shifts a late game's window by a day vs. real data. Harmless on the current slate (earlier games open the window); worth aligning to the ET day before L.A0.6 composes synthetic with the seam.
- **R26 · nit · scenario-beats.test.ts:290 (D26 back-fill proof) — refs: §23.2 (back-fill on recovery).** Answering the brief directly: the outage-vs-happy_path equality is genuinely cross-scenario (it would catch PRNG streams keyed by scenario id, or outage state leaking into values — the two ways this provider *could* regress), but it is **not an independent computation**: both sides run the identical pure `finalLine`/`progress` code on identical inputs, and since the provider is stateless the equality is near-tautological. What §23.2 actually cares about — writer-side cumulative back-fill after a degraded window (upserts catching up in `player_stats`) — is untested anywhere in this batch and lands on L.A0.6. Fine for M0 provider scope; recorded so the gate task doesn't inherit "back-fill is proven" as a premise.
- **R27 · nit · scripts/record-fixtures.ts:90,99 — refs: D27 (identity lives IN the artifact).** The CLI hardcodes `provider: 'sleeper'` in the header and `sleeper.jsonl.gz` in the path instead of reading `provider.name` — re-introducing at write time exactly the guessing D27 exists to prevent. Equal today; a silent lie the day the CLI wraps any other provider.
- **R28 · nit · fixture-format.ts:68 — refs: D27 ("parse-rejected loudly on mismatch").** Loud rejection covers `format`/`version` only; a header missing `provider`/`season`/`week` parses fine and yields `name = 'fixture:undefined'` downstream. A three-field presence check would make the identity guarantee total.
- **R29 · nit · fixture-replay-provider.ts:104 — refs: D6 (failures replay as failures).** Recorded failures replay as a generic `Error` carrying the message only — the recorded `status` (e.g. 429 vs 500) is dropped, so a future consumer branching on status sees a different shape live vs replay. No consumer branches today.
- **R30 · nit · D24/D28 seam composition (live-stats.ts:94 + fixture-replay-provider.ts:58).** D24's "record/replay reproduces today's writes" is true for every column *except* `source`: the writer stamps `provider.name`, and replay's name is `'fixture:sleeper'`, so a replayed ingestion writes `source: 'fixture:sleeper'`. That is D28's intended honest default — but the documented opt-in (`recordedProviderName`) has **no supported mechanism** reaching the writer; L.A0.6 will have to hand-roll a delegating wrapper that overrides `name` to get byte-identical rows. Deliberate-by-design per D28; recorded so the gate builder budgets for it (and so the wrapper, when written, is recognized as the sanctioned deliberate-impersonation path, not a smell).

| R48 | **Ledger entry F6, NOT a migration — Builder judgment call as delegated.** Why not DB CHECKs now: **(a)** the mutual-exclusivity CHECK (`NOT (revoked_at AND claimed_at)`) would encode claim semantics L.A1.14 hasn't defined — the review's own probe B shape (claimed_at set AND later revoked_at set) is plausibly *legitimate* for a multi-use invite: some uses claimed, then the commissioner revokes further use; a CHECK baked in now risks a revert migration the day the claim RPC defines this. **(b)** `CHECK (use_count <= max_uses)` alone is safer but settles a clamp-vs-block question that belongs to the RPC (055's own comment says commissioners "may raise" `max_uses` — whether one may ever *lower* it below `use_count` is undefined), and shipping half the backstop invites false confidence. **(c)** Cost: a CHECK-only migration would take 057 and shift the schema lane a third time in one week (057 def_ya → 058, cascading the §7 table + PROGRESS §2 again) for two backstops on a table with **zero writers of any kind** — failing the D53 proportionality test 056's status CHECK passed (that one was free, in-table, at creation). ### Should-fix

- **R57 · should-fix · calculator.ts:36-49 (`roundHalfUp` doc) + spec §7.3.3 precision rule — "half-up" is ecosystem-ambiguous and the spec never pins which meaning; the implementation's choice is right but lives only in the decisions log; refs: E38 (determinism), D57(2), the §3 fold-back discipline.** The two authorities the rounding question names genuinely diverge at negative half-cent boundaries: strict "round half up" (the Wikipedia/IEEE toward-+∞ convention) gives `−0.005 → −0.00`, while Postgres `NUMERIC(8,2)` assignment — **tested live this session, both numeric-literal and float8 paths** — gives `−0.005 → −0.01` (half away from zero; Java's `RoundingMode.HALF_UP` also means away-from-zero, so the bare term supports both readings). The implementation sides with the DB, which is the only coherent choice under E38's determinism rule (JS result ≡ stored result), and pins it at `−0.005 → −0.01`. But the spec text still says bare "half-up": a future implementer (or the L.D1 writer's author) reading §7.3.3 alone can pick the toward-+∞ reading and diverge from both this module and the column type on negative totals (all-miss K weeks, INT-heavy QB weeks). The divergence window is narrow — with 2-decimal template coefficients × integer stats every sum is exact at 2 decimals, so a negative half-cent boundary needs ≥3-decimal coefficients — but the determinism rule is absolute and the fix is one line. Fold a spec erratum (changelog + §7.3.3 parenthetical): *"half-up = round half away from zero, matching NUMERIC(8,2) assignment; −0.005 → −0.01"* — per the repo's own rule that resolved ambiguities get folded back into the spec, not left in D-rows.
- **R58 · should-fix · derive-stats.ts:83-91 (`emitFamily`) — a delivered source value that lands in no bucket emits an all-zero family: delivered-zero everywhere, nothing hot, nothing pending — the silent-wrong-total class E61/F20 exist to prevent; refs: §23.5, E61, F20, D57(1).** Probed live: `def_points_allowed: 13.5` → all 11 PA keys delivered as 0 (13.5 falls between `def_pa_7_13` and `def_pa_14_20`; both platform sums = 0, violating the one-hot invariant the property test asserts — but that property only scans **integers**, so the state is invisible to it); `def_yards_allowed: 99.5` → same for YA; a (bogus) negative PA → same, since `def_pa_0` pins lo=0. Downstream, every tier rules key scores a delivered 0 with an empty `pending` — for ESPN templates that silently erases the D/ST tier component (up to ±5 points/side) with no badge, which is a *worse* state than the pre-F20 all-pending bug (that one was at least honest). Reachability today is low — `player_stats` sources are INTEGER columns (057), and nothing calls these modules yet — but the helper's input is provider-shaped `Record<string, number>`, not column-shaped, and nothing range-guards it. Cheap close: treat a source value matching **no** bucket as unreported (family absent → pending; for PA that also covers negatives), and extend the one-hot property to assert *delivered ⇒ exactly one hot per platform set* over non-integer samples so the wrong fix (leaving the gap) can't pass.
- **R59 · should-fix · calculator.ts:64-72 — the delivered-stat guard is one-sided: a malformed rules **coefficient** poisons the total to NaN, and NUMERIC(8,2) accepts NaN, so the poisoned total is storable; refs: E61 ("never a silent wrong total"), §7.3.3 snapshot rule, D57(3)'s defensive clause.** Probed live: `{ receptions: "abc" }` (rules values come from `scoring_rules_snapshot` JSONB, which can carry strings) → `contribution = NaN` → `total: NaN` (`roundHalfUp` propagates it), and `INSERT 'NaN'` into a `NUMERIC(8,2)` column **succeeds** (live-tested — Postgres numeric has a NaN value), so nothing downstream is guaranteed to throw. A string-numeric coefficient (`"0.5"`) silently coerces and scores (×4 → 2) — works by accident, masking a corrupt snapshot. The module already defends the *stats* side against exactly this class (non-finite → pending, D57's "never poisoning a total"); the rules side, same trust boundary (a JSONB blob), has no guard. Reachability requires a corrupt snapshot — v1 rules are code-authored templates frozen via the L.A1.11 RPC — but the v1.1 custom editor (F21's scope) makes rules user-shaped, and this module is the last line. Semantics call for the Builder to make **and record**: marking a bad-coefficient key `pending` would misbadge corrupt config as "waiting on data," so the honest options are throw (corrupt snapshot = programming/config error, loud) or a distinct breakdown flag; either way, pin it with a test.
- **R60 · should-fix · PROGRESS §6 — two hand-offs this task created live only in prose; per the §6 header rule (R51: "creating a hand-off without an F-row is itself a review finding") both need rows; refs: R51 precedent, E38, F20/D57(1), D44.** **(a) Rounding vs the real writer (L.D1):** D57(2)'s NUMERIC-matching claim carried no DB evidence at build time (this review supplied it — live temp-table proof, see header), and the actual consistency obligation — the L.D1 writer stores the **JS-rounded** total into `matchups`/`team_week_results` `NUMERIC(8,2)`, with a pin proving no path lets the DB do the rounding on a diverging value (benign only while both round half-away-from-zero; E38's determinism must be *pinned* at the writer, not inherited silently) — belongs to a task that doesn't exist yet in any ledger row. Add F22 → discharged by L.D1 (M4). **(b) The derive→score composition:** F20's guarantee is module-local — `scorePlayerWeek` happily accepts raw stats that never passed `deriveTierIndicators` (tier rules keys then read pending forever), and a worker that skips derive also loses the inbound-indicator stripping (D44's "never stored" laundering guard). The composition appears only in L.A1.10's task-text usage sketch (`scorePlayerWeek(template.rules, derive(stats))`); the production call site is M4's `score-league-week` (§22.2/L.D1), and no F-row keys it. Add F23 → *`score-league-week` composes `deriveTierIndicators` before `scorePlayerWeek`; pinned at the worker* — discharged by L.D1 (M4), with L.A1.10 as the interim proof-of-pattern.

### Nit

- **R61 · nit · calculator.test.ts — no stored-literal golden pin discriminates round(full sum) from Σ(rounded perKey); only the 250-run property carries E38's precision rule; refs: §4.3(a) (golden pins as stored literals), E38, D57(3).** Every literal pin's contributions are exact at ≤2 decimals (QB 11.48+8−2+2+1.2; E38 tie 9.2+6+0.04) — a Σ-of-rounded implementation passes all of them; the single-key `0.335×3 → 1.01` pin rounds identically under both (one entry). The property test does catch the wrong implementation (near-certainly, per the verified-sound note), but §4.3(a)'s point is a falsifiable *literal*: one two-key pin, e.g. rules `{a: 0.111, b: 0.111}` × stats `{a: 3, b: 3}` → full sum 0.666 → `total: 0.67` (a Σ-of-rounded impl yields 0.33+0.33 = **0.66**), pins the rule as a stored literal instead of a statistical consequence.

In the second shape `DELETE FROM public.profiles WHERE id = <removed user>` silently destroyed both of their placeholder franchises (team_count 8, seats_counted 4 → 2) and, because `league_members_team_id_fkey` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, left two `league_members` rows with `team_id NULL` — precisely the "invisible to every capacity check" shape ruling S2 / erratum v2.8.8 / D74(3) removed policies to eliminate. 063's own banner (063:151-152, 807-808) names this exact hazard as the reason it moves `owner_id` at all, then dodges it for one franchise. ## Review findings — 2026-07-27 (M1 batch 20)

**Findings-remediation Builder session on `feat/M1-L.A2.6-join-page` (PR #66 — fix-then-merge, no new PR). One should-fix (R114) from the PR #66 review: the join-by-code dialog dead-ended on a pasted `/join/…` link — the exact affordance its own copy advertises. Purely input-normalization on the join-by-code entry; the F2 surface, the six-state claim logic and the v2.8.10 erratum are untouched.**

### Should-fix

- **R114 · should-fix · `src/components/leagues/leagues-index.tsx`:65** — the join-by-code dialog breaks on a pasted `/join/…` link, the exact affordance its own copy advertises. *Evidence:* the submit handler does `router.push(\`/join/${encodeURIComponent(trimmed)}\`)`, passing the whole pasted string verbatim as the `[token]` param with no code/token extraction. But the dialog's DialogDescription tells the user to "paste a fieldscout.gg/join/… link" and the label reads "Invite code or link". The real share artifacts ARE full absolute URLs: `buildJoinLink` (invite-panel-ops.ts:264) returns `${origin}/join/${codeOrToken}`; the wizard copy button (league-create-wizard.tsx:996) copies `${window.location.origin}/join/${result.invite_code}`. `encodeURIComponent('https://fieldscout.gg/join/a1b2c3d4e5')` yields the single unresolvable segment `/join/https%3A%2F%2F…`; `get_join_preview` matches only exact token / lower(invite_code) / lower(invite_slug), so a full URL → `{found:false}` → "This link isn't valid" on a VALID invite. Typing a bare code works; pasting a link (an explicitly-offered input) dead-ends. F2 intact, no security issue. *Fix direction:* before pushing, if the input contains `/join/`, take the last non-empty path segment (strip query/hash) and encodeURIComponent only that; otherwise use the trimmed value as-is.

### Resolution — 2026-07-27 (Builder, same branch `feat/M1-L.A2.6-join-page`, PR #66)

| Finding | Resolved by |
|---|---|
| R114 (should-fix) | this commit — extraction lifted into a PURE helper `extractJoinCode` in `invite-panel-ops.ts` (the §7.2 share-link section, directly beside `buildJoinLink` as its exact inverse — NOT buried in the dialog's onClick), and `JoinLeagueDialog.handleSubmit` + the Continue-button `disabled` gate now push/enable on `extractJoinCode(code)` instead of the raw trim. The helper trims, cuts everything from the first `?`/`#`, then takes the last non-empty path segment after a case-insensitive `/join/` marker; a bare code/slug (no `/join/`) passes through trimmed. It keeps the segment's original case (seat tokens are case-sensitive; the RPC lower()s codes/slugs itself) and does NOT URL-encode — the caller still `encodeURIComponent`s the route param. Pinned in `invite-panel-ops.test.ts` §8: a 16-row table (full absolute URL, bare-host, protocol-relative, path-only, trailing slash, `?query`, `#hash`, query+slash, custom-slug link, whitespace-wrapped link, bare-code + bare-slug passthrough, empty + whitespace-only) **including the two REAL share artifacts** — `buildJoinLink('https://fieldscout.gg', CODE)`'s own output and the wizard's `${origin}/join/${invite_code}` shape — plus a case-preservation pin (mixed-case token unchanged) and an empty-code pin (`/join/` with no segment → `''`, so the dialog no-ops rather than pushing a dead segment). **Break probe shown:** helper body forced to `return raw.trim()` (the pre-R114 verbatim passthrough) → **exactly 14 of the table rows fail** (every link form), while the bare-code and empty rows STAY green — proving the table discriminates the fix rather than passing vacuously; reverted, re-proven green. **D39 browser pass (pre-auth, cheap):** against a seeded local league (`invite_code='r114probe1'`, `status='setup'`, 12 seats), navigated the EXACT URLs `router.push` targets before vs. after — `/join/https%3A%2F%2Ffieldscout.gg%2Fjoin%2Fr114probe1` (the OLD verbatim-encoded target) renders "This link isn't valid" (the bug reproduced on a valid invite); `/join/r114probe1` (the extracted bare code the NEW helper produces) renders the real "R114 Probe League · 12 seats open" claimable card. `get_join_preview` confirmed the same split at the RPC (`{found:true,status:ok}` on the bare code vs. `{found:false}` on the full URL). The authed dialog-click on `/app/leagues` could not be walked in this session (a local GoTrue seed-auth limitation — the hand-seeded user's client login didn't complete its post-sign-in redirect under automation; an environment constraint, not R114), so the observable behavior was verified at the pre-auth route it feeds — the dialog's onClick is a three-line wiring of the unit-pinned helper into `router.push`, and the URL it produces (`/join/r114probe1`) is exactly the one shown resolving. All seeded rows CLEANED (0 leagues/users/profiles/identities after teardown). The v2.8.13 §8.5.5 erratum this PR folded says the stale seat's pick "is held open until deadline + disconnect_grace_seconds — a returning manager may pick manually during the hold — then autopicks"; the code re-derived the branch each tick with freshness as of now(), so a post-deadline heartbeat retroactively granted the fresh-at-expiry branch. ## Review findings — 2026-08-19 (M3 batch 12 — L.C3.1)

**Reviewer batch (adversarial review of PR #175 — L.C3.1, the auction room, `main...feat/M3-L.C3.1-auction-room` @ `2a164db`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — four should-fixes, four nits. All eight taken same-branch same-day; mechanics at D192.**

**Adjudicated FOR the Builder first, so it is not re-litigated:** every probe reproduced at the published counts; the lint retirement is genuine (zero `eslint-disable` / `@ts-ignore` / config edits in the diff); the one-channel and never-optimistic claims verified; all 12 `nomination_order` columns measured with their three words and no resting shadow; `$500` disables the Bid button with the max-bid copy; the anti-snipe re-arm watched live. D191(2)'s anti-snipe correction was verified sound against **two of the three** attacks — a commissioner clock edit cannot lie (`draft_set_clock`'s auction arm is pause-gated, writes `config` only, never `current_deadline`, and refuses `p_extend_current` at 087:1160-1166) and cancel-and-renominate cannot either (pause writes `current_deadline = NULL` at 069:357, so the client sees a null frame that clears `previousRef`). **The third landed — R428.**

- **R427 · should-fix · `draft-room.tsx` — the SHARED status strip printed a SNAKE board coordinate in the auction room — TAKEN, suppressed at the source, pinned, and MEASURED BOTH WAYS.** `myNextPick` was computed unconditionally in `DraftRoomLive` and passed as `myNextPickLabel`, so `nextPickNumberForTeam`'s pure board walk reached a room with no board — and the `draftType` coercion whose own comment said *"the value is simply unused"* was, in fact, used. §16.4 zone 2 enumerates the strip's contents (LIVE/PAUSED · Round & Pick · draft order · presence · clock) and "your next pick" is not among them; worse, the auction rotation skips filled rosters (§8.6.7(c)/E27) so the walk coincides only in lap 1 and then diverges permanently. **Fixed** by making `myNextPick` null when `isAuction` (suppression, the smaller claim — §16.4's auction callout already gives per-team standing to the team columns), correcting the coercion comment to name its two real consumers, and pinning the posture in `auction-room.test.ts`. **Measured live on the local stack, same tree, same build, both draft types off the clock:** an 8-team AUCTION with the guard temporarily disabled read `On the clock · Team 8 | Live | Round 1 · Pick 3 | **Your next: 2.07**`; with the guard restored, the same room at pick 4 read the same strip with **no hint at all**; and an 8-team SNAKE room at pick 3 still reads `**Your next: 2.08**` — the fix is auction-only.
- **R428 · should-fix · `auction-block-ops.ts` — "same nomination key + later deadline" is NOT unique to an anti-snipe extension; a RESUME produces exactly that shape — TAKEN, closed with a SIZE test, pinned in both directions.** `draft_pause` writes `current_deadline = NULL` + `deadline_remaining_ms` (069:353-357) and `draft_resume` writes `now() + remaining` (069:485-492) — strictly later, by the pause duration, with `current_pick_number` and `current_nomination.player_id` untouched, so `nominationKey` is unchanged. The only guard was that `useAntiSnipe`'s `previousRef` had observed the NULL frame, and the ref survives refetches and reconnects because DR.7 keeps the block mounted. The reviewer's probe against the real module moved a deadline **12 seconds** (`T+18s` → `T+30s`, key unchanged) and got `reArmed: true` — announced on screen as *"Anti-snipe — clock reset to 10s"*. **They are separable by SIZE:** 085's re-arm is `GREATEST(current_deadline, now() + anti)` (085:780-791), so whenever it moves the deadline at all the new remaining is exactly `anti_snipe`, never more, while a resume restores the pre-pause remainder. `antiSnipeView` now additionally requires `deadlineMs − (nowMs + offsetMs) <= seconds * 1000 + ANTI_SNIPE_REARM_SLACK_MS` (1,500ms, sized for §9.3 offset error and no larger — every millisecond of slack is a millisecond of resume-shaped movement that still slips through). Both directions pinned as stored literals: the reviewer's exact numbers → NOT re-armed, plus a generic resume; and the genuine re-arm → re-armed, including D128's after-zero full-window case, a 400ms-late client sample, and the exact 11,500 / 11,501 boundary.
- **R429 · should-fix · `draft-room.tsx:315` — the D94 lobby's `stale` prop was provably always `false`, and it marked a rule-1/rule-2 contradiction — TAKEN, RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF BOTH RULES, NOT ESCALATED.** The reviewer is right on both halves: `absentDraftIsHonest(h)` is `h === 'ok'`, the gate precedes the lobby, and past the dataless `!detail.data` arm `health` can only be `'ok' | 'degraded'` — so the gate fired on exactly `'degraded'`, the one state rule 2 says must keep rendering behind the banner, and the prop it evicted was a constant `false`. **The rules do not genuinely conflict — the REMEDY was over-broad, and the spec settles which remedy applies.** §16.5.4's required-states line is LAW: *"degraded (banner + last-good data, never wrong numbers)"*. So rule 1 keeps its content (an absence claim must be backed by a read, never by a failure) and its remedy now scales with what the surface can DISCLOSE: the D94 lobby mounts the command bar — §16.5.4 v2.12's single banner surface, DR.7(4) — so it renders `degraded` as the spec requires, last-good data behind `STALE_ROOM_COPY`; the bare recap pointer, "no draft yet" and "Draft not found" cards have no banner and §16.5.4 forbids inventing a one-off treatment, so they keep the error-with-retry surface and keep the gate. Implemented by moving the scheduled-lobby branch AHEAD of the gate (never by weakening the gate's condition — R430's inert-gate shape is explicitly forbidden by a new pin), reasoning recorded in `room-health-ops.ts` and `room-health-ops.test.ts`, and the count pin corrected: `absentDraftIsHonest(health)` still 2, `health === 'degraded'` still 3, plus a new position pin that the scheduled branch precedes the gate. **NOT filed to §3:** the stop condition is for a spec that is ambiguous or wrong, and §16.5.4 is neither; D191(3) is this same PR's own build-mechanics entry, and a fix cycle is where an over-broad remedy in it gets corrected.
- **R430 · should-fix · F56's un-staged rule 1 had no owning row, and its stated reason was over-broad — TAKEN, F79 filed, F56's disclosure corrected with a NEW MEASUREMENT that goes further than the finding.** R430's diagnosis is confirmed — `invalidateQueries` bypasses `staleTime`, and the room calls it on `leaguesKeys.detail(leagueId)` from `use-draft.ts:335` (the R271 path), `use-draft.ts:573` and `use-draft-controls.ts:55,236`, while `retryRoom` calls `detail.refetch()` directly. **And there is a fourth site the finding did not name, inside the D94 lobby itself:** `draft-lobby.tsx:136-149` invalidates `leaguesKeys.detail(leagueId)` every `AUTO_START_POLL_MS` (5s) whenever `autoStartPollMs` is non-null — which is any instant within `AUTO_START_WATCH_MS` (2 minutes) **or already past**. Measured on the local stack: a `LC31FIX D94` league (scheduled, no drafts row, instant ~90s out) with `/api/leagues/<id>` blocked at `window.fetch` logged **8 blocked requests in ~20s with no user action and no mutation**. So **D191(4)'s "a mounted lobby cannot be made to refetch from the page" is WITHDRAWN**, and F56's disclosure is corrected rather than merely narrowed. What still could NOT be staged is the *threshold*: both failure shapes (a rejected `fetch` and a resolved 503 `Response`) park at `fetchStatus: 'paused'` / `fetchFailureCount: 1` in this pane — React Query's offline pause, with `document.visibilityState: 'hidden'` throughout (the same limit the reviewer hit for R428) — and a paused fetch then swallows every later invalidate, so the count never reaches `FETCH_FAILURES_FOR_BANNER`. Dispatched `online` / `focus` / `visibilitychange` and set `networkMode: 'always'` on both the client defaults and the query's own options; it did not clear. **F79** carries the staging shape.
- **R431 · nit · F78's inventory was short by one and self-contradictory — TAKEN, corrected and grown.** Counted: `031_draft_queue_replace.sql` asserts `'A player can appear in the queue only once.'` ×1 (:210) and `'You do not manage this queue.'` ×6 (:249, :258, :277, :288, :310, :335) = **seven**, matching the seven line numbers the row already listed and the PR body's "seven times", while the prose said "six". Two members added: `082:85`'s `'A queue can hold at most 500 players.'` (asserted at `031:224`), which is user-reachable through `queueFromList`'s append mode where the composed `finalOrder` can exceed the cap the TS `.max(500)` only guards on `upsertQueue` (`draft-service.ts:698`); and `draft-service.ts:399`'s `` `queue read failed: ${…}` ``, flagged as what it is — a thrown internal message, not a friendly refusal — so one migration retires the lot.

The stacked conditionals are now an explicit ternary so the precedence lives in the code rather than emerging from the merge, with no change to a single rendered pixel, and `auction-room.test.ts` pins both the ternary and the badges' independence.
- **R433 · nit · the `You` badge was pinned by exact source whitespace — TAKEN.** `'>\n            You\n          </Badge>'` broke on any Prettier reflow. All three word pins are now `/>\s*You\s*<\/Badge>/`-shaped.

- **R420 · should-fix · `draft-service.ts:572` and `:609-613` — the F65 integrity check discriminated on values EVERY league member can read, so F65's live-proven false success was still reachable through the shipped route while four ledger sites claimed it was refused unconditionally — TAKEN, fixed, pinned RED-first with the reviewer's own probe.** `draft_bids` RLS is `FOR SELECT USING (is_league_member(league_id))` with no column restriction (083:132-133), so any member reads every row's `action_id`, `player_id`, `amount` and `nomination_seq`. The reviewer's live probe: **mgr3 — a non-nominator during BIDDING — POSTed the nominate route with mgr2's `action_id` plus the (player, amount) read straight off `draft_bids`, and got HTTP 200 carrying `bid.team_id` = mgr2's team.** The shipped pin passed only because it happened to pick opening_bid 1 against a $2 raise; it would have stayed green if the check compared amount alone or player alone, and the converse (`nomination_seq` under the same policy) is symmetric. Blast radius was bounded — nothing written, no money moved, the settle-invalidate corrects the transient false "success" — but the CLAIM SITES said more than the code did. **Fix (the reviewer's preferred option, taken over narrowing the claims): IDENTITY is the discriminator.** The returned row's `team_id` is compared to the caller's ACTING SEAT — own `league_members.team_id`, or on a mock `config.mock.human_team_id` — resolved by the same helper the queue writers already use, renamed `resolveActingSeat` and re-documented as mirroring the RPCs' own team resolution (089:1201/1476). The argument comparison is KEPT as the second arm (it catches a caller reusing their OWN id across verbs, where the seat matches by construction). `nominatePlayer`/`placeBid` take `userId`; the routes pass `user.id`, which they already held. **The reviewer's exact probe is now the pin** — the read premise measured as mgr3, the forgery built ONLY from what that read returned, both directions, `not.toContain` on the other manager's team id, nothing written and the high bid AND its holder unchanged.
- **R421 · should-fix · `draft-service.ts:506-507` — the one user-facing string this PR authors was developer jargon and its remedy was false — TAKEN, replaced, pinned.** `ACTION_ID_REUSED_MESSAGE` read *"That action id was already used for a different action — a nomination and a bid never share one. New copy: **"That didn't go through — we couldn't confirm it as yours. Check the player and the price, then place it again."** — no internal identifier, and a remedy that works (a fresh gesture mints a fresh id; the hooks' settle-invalidate has already refetched the room).

- **R401 · should-fix · the bid feed's "run-pure by construction / the reset's one event empties a held cache" claim (D184(3)) had a hole in exactly the window the join-refetch opens — TAKEN, fix shape (b) buffer-and-replay, pinned RED-first.** Mechanism: `SUBSCRIBED` → `invalidateQueries(feed)` starts a refetch (snapshot at T0); the `'draft_bids'` handler did `getQueryData → reduceBidEvent → setQueryData`; React Query REPLACES the cache with the fetch result on resolve, discarding every interim `setQueryData`. So a bid landing in the window was lost; rows VOIDED in it (cancel/undo/reset) came back as zombies from the pre-void snapshot; after a reset run-1 zombies merged with run-2 INSERTs at seq 1 until the next rejoin; the first fetch dropped events outright. The feed has no gap detector, so nothing repaired it until another confirmed join. D184(3)'s "cannot happen by construction" sentence was false — **withdrawn in place with the mechanism named.** Fix: NEW `use-draft-feed-sink.ts` (`createFeedSink` — FIFO queue, drained only while `fetchStatus === 'idle'`, a `QueryCache` subscription drains on settle; generic over the reducer), `use-draft.ts` pushes every `draft_bids` event through it and disposes it with the channel. Why (b) over (a): the drafts-event detector is blind in the very window (the interim write may still be in the cache when the `drafts` event arrives, and later `drafts` events compare only the current high bid — a lost historical bid or a cancelled nomination's zombies at a shared seq never trip it) and leans on intra-transaction delivery order. Pin: `use-draft-feed-sink.test.ts` (**18**) — mechanism control, window, hold, first-fetch, dedupe, ZOMBIES, CROSS-RUN, FIFO, error-settle, immediate path, no-cache drop, reducer-doubt via a live `QueryObserver`, dispose, spine source pins. **RED against the pre-fix handler shape: 7 of 16**, on the survival assertions; reverted ⇒ green. NOT deferred to L.C3.1 (the reviewer's instruction; the room is about to consume this feed).
- **R402 · nit · `use-draft-bids.ts` hand-rolled offset paging that `page-all.ts` already warns against (short-page stop without a count; order not ending in a UNIQUE column) — TAKEN.** Now `pageAll(...)` with `{ count: 'exact' }` and `.order('id')` as the final key; `DRAFT_BIDS_PAGE` removed; source-pinned (the exact order sequence). Theoretical today (hosted `max_rows` = 1000; live rows unique on (seq, amount) in practice) but the CLAUDE.md "exactly 1000 rows looked like the whole table" class.
- **R403 · nit · tasks-M3 §2:35 still read "non-strict Zod parses" while the PR said the claim was CORRECTED (the correction lived only in `use-draft-ops.ts` + D184(4)) — TAKEN.** The §2 line is amended in place with a dated note naming the real mechanism (plain interfaces + `isDraftsRecord`/`isPickRecord` structural guards; named-field copy is why additive keys never leak).
- **R404 · nit · two precision slips at three sites (088:58, 088:295, spec §12.14 row) — TAKEN, all sites plus the same phrases in this file.** "NO DDL" is false (CREATE FUNCTION/TRIGGER are DDL; `CREATE TRIGGER` takes ShareRowExclusiveLock on `draft_bids`) → "no table/column/index/policy change"; "cancel/end = 1" → "cancel = 1, end = up to 1" (`draft_end` in the nominating phase: 087's helper finds no live nomination, returns 0, emits nothing). 088's per-writer paragraph corrected too; spec → **v2.12.7** (the v2.12.6 cache sentence corrected in the same entry).
- **R405 · nit · pre-existing, NOT this PR — 026's integer fixture ADPs vs restored players (the R387/R395/F60 class).** Already routed: owned by the pending 025/026 fixture-hardening chip. Not fixed here; recorded as already-routed.

## Review findings — 2026-08-18 (M3 batch 6 — L.C1.5, FINAL fix round)

**Nine findings on PR #159: R375-R377 from the stack-owning reviewer's verification pass, R378-R383 from four independent static lenses that read the diff only. VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — one BLOCKER-class, four should-fix, four nits.** Merge target `main` @ 4930bd8; `git merge-tree` clean. **The framing that matters: every pin involved passed. The lenses found what a live verification structurally could not, and three of the six are further doors into the same D160(8) insolvent/stuck-clock state R367 was filed for — R378 being R367's exact species recurring INSIDE R367's own fix. That is four consecutive rounds in which a correction re-introduced its own defect class.**

- **R378 · BLOCKER-class · the E28 arm-3 gate reproduced ONE of the award's TWO refusals, and at a settings-legal `auction_min_bid = 0` the arithmetic that masked the missing one disappears — TAKEN, fixed in the helper.** §3b's header promised "THE COMPARISON IS THE AWARD'S, RE-ASKED AFTER THE WRITE" and implemented it as the single test `v_high_bid <= v_max_bid`. `draft_tick`'s award arm asks **two** things: `open_slots < 1` (E27, `087:3479`) and `price > max_bid` (`087:3484`), and every other consumer pairs them (`draft_force_pick 087:2168-2173`, `draft_nominate 085:478`) because 084:349's `CASE WHEN v_open <= 0 THEN 0` makes a complete roster's `max_bid` a **semantic** zero — at which point `high_bid <= max_bid` is no longer the affordability question. At `min_bid >= 1` the gap is masked (`high_bid >= min_bid >= 1 > 0`, so the money arm raises anyway, with a message about dollars); at **`auction_min_bid = 0`, which is legal** (`league-settings.ts:220` = `min(0)`; 084:210 names the $0 league), both nomination writers open AT min_bid, so an unraised nomination stands at $0 and the gate computed `0 <= 0` and RETURNED. `draft_auction_solvent`'s floor there is `remaining >= 0`. **Driven:** budget $200 / min_bid $0 / total_rounds 2, t2 the standing high bidder at $0 with one pick; `draft_move_player(..., t2, null, 50)` filled its last slot, committed, and every tick then raised E27 into `auction_failures` forever. **Fix:** the gate re-derives `open_slots` alongside `max_bid`, its pass condition is `v_open >= 1 AND v_high_bid <= v_max_bid`, and the capacity case gets **its own sentence** (folding it into the max-bid message prints "$0 max bid" and sends the commissioner after money instead of a roster slot). **The coverage gap was the fixture, not the pin:** new **§I(c)** on a min_bid-$0 world (LM), one unit of `open_slots` either side, plus a min_bid-$1 pin proving the arm is the award's first question rather than a $0 special case. **Probe 7 → 5 of 199 RED**, reverted.
- **R379 · should-fix · `draft_reset` left the previous run's `draft_bids` live at sequence numbers the restart re-issues, so `draft_undo`'s auction on-clock recovery could seat the WRONG franchise — TAKEN, both halves.** `nomination_seq` IS `current_pick_number`; `draft_reset` rewinds it to 1 (`087:2573`) and `draft_start_internal` re-issues from there (`084:692`/`084:697`), while the recovery lookup (`087:1423`) had **no run discriminator at all** — no `voided_at` filter (deliberately: it must read rows the undo just voided) and no time bound. Two runs' nominations therefore collide on one sequence number, and since the seq→nominator map is not positional (§8.6.7(c) skips complete rosters) the earliest row names a DIFFERENT franchise. **Fix (a):** `draft_reset` stamps its run's rows `voided_at` — rows KEPT, §12.5 stays append-only, the same posture as the `draft_picks` soft-undo beside it — and reset is added as situation **(c)** in the D162 enumeration at `087:230-250` (whose lead-in said "exactly two situations" and now says three), in the spec (**v2.12.4**) and in `voided_at`'s writer inventory, which had said "written ONLY by two sites". **Fix (b):** the lookup scopes to `b.created_at >= v_draft.started_at`, the one discriminator available to a reader that must see voided rows, with a LOUD refusal when `started_at` is NULL on a live/paused draft rather than a silently widened window. Pinned both ways in §K, including the unscoped measurement that shows the ambiguity is real. **Probes 8 and 9 → 1 of 199 RED each**, reverted.
- **R380 · should-fix · `draft_reassign_pick`'s exclusivity check was blind to the one player who must not be assigned: the one under nomination — TAKEN.** On an auction the nominated player has **no** `draft_picks` row until the award writes it (`087:3497`), so a sweep of `draft_picks` passes for exactly him; nothing else on the path reads `current_nomination` (the E28 arms are about money; the §3b gate returns silently when the receiving team is not the high bidder). The award's INSERT then hits `uniq_draft_player_live` (065:178), ARM 2.6's `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS` (`087:3581`) swallows it into `auction_failures`, and the nomination never clears — the same stuck clock, reached through the board instead of through the money. `draft_move_player` cannot reach it (it requires a live pick), which is why the guard lives on reassign and only there. Refusal points at `draft_cancel_nomination` — the verb this task shipped. **Probe 10 → 3 of 199 RED**, reverted.
- **R381 · should-fix · the no-drift pin whose entire job is preventing R367 from recurring was satisfied by a COMMENT — TAKEN, and the weakness was measured rather than argued.** `pg_proc.prosrc` is raw body text INCLUDING comments; `draft_adjust_budget` names the arm-3 helper twice (the R367 comment at `087:776` and the `PERFORM` at `087:781`), so deleting the call and keeping the comment left the pin GREEN. **Proof, not assertion: probe 1 was re-run with exactly that mutation and the pre-R381 predicate still evaluated `TRUE`.** All three sibling pins (`036:230/238/244`) now match the CALL FORM as each helper is actually called (`PERFORM public.X(` for the two gates, `:= public.X(` for the void helper, which returns a count) and assert **cardinality** (`count(*) = N`), because `bool_and` over a shrunken set also returns TRUE. Probe 1's red set consequently GREW by exactly pin 13 — **3 of 181 → 4 of 199** — which is the finding, measured.

Those pins exercise the **post-087 bodies**. The true reason for the sweep is CO-LOCATION: three of the seven were DROP+CREATEd here, so 036 pins the eleven in the post-087 world BESIDE 025's rather than instead of them. **Third instance in this PR of a justification outrunning the facts** — v2.12.3 says exactly why that is dangerous.
- **R382 · nit · pin 127's description inverted the causality — TAKEN (description only; the pin and its arithmetic were right).** It said a cross-team move is refused "because the SLOT it consumes is what shrinks the max bid". From 084:349-350 consuming a slot **raises** max_bid by one min_bid: t2 goes 151/2/150 → 149/1/149, where the $2 price costs $2 and the slot rebates $1, net −$1. The section's own setup comment stated it correctly. Reworded to the measured cause — t2 sits at exact equality after the $49 correction, so any net reduction refuses.

- **R362 · should-fix · THE HEADLINE — ARM 2.5 still snake-autopicked a live auction mock, so the banner's "claimed by NO tick arm" was FALSE — TAKEN, fixed with the same two lines ARM 2 got, plus a pin and all three prose sites** — the migration closed ARM 2's auction door and then asserted, in three places (`086` banner ARM-2.6 block, the in-body ARM 2.6 comment, D160(9)), that a hand-built live auction mock is "claimed by NO tick arm". **ARM 2.5 had no `draft_type` predicate** in its claim or its under-lock re-verify, and its pick path is `draft_autopick_resolve` → `draft_apply_pick_internal` — the SNAKE writer, reached by a second door. **Reproduced on this branch before the fix** (privileged fixture, rolled back): a live `is_mock=true, draft_type='auction'` draft with a CPU seat on the clock, `cpu_speed: fast` so the think-time was ~58s due while the deadline was still 30s out, `started_at` fresh so ARM 1.6 could not pause it first. - **R363 · should-fix · the award's attribution lookup justified `LIMIT 1` with a uniqueness invariant D143 refutes, and tiebroke on a random UUID — TAKEN (`player_id` added to the WHERE, the claim replaced with the real discriminator, the open question routed to L.C1.5)** — the comment read *"The lookup is unique by construction — a team cannot hold two bids at one amount on one nomination (a raise must exceed the high bid and a self-raise is refused, 085)."* **D143 / tasks-M3 §6 L.C1.5** rules that `draft_cancel_nomination` voids a nomination and **does NOT consume the sequence number**, so one `nomination_seq` can carry the rows of two successive nominations, on different players, at one amount, from one team — the triple is not unique. ### Should-fix

- **R706 · should-fix · `ingest-week.ts` — the stats write preceded the enqueue, so a crash between the two PostgREST calls lost the delta permanently (at-most-once), and the named net did not repair it — TAKEN: order swapped (queue → stats), D303(2) rewritten, the wrong claim withdrawn, F218 filed.** The reviewer was right on both halves: the loss was real (Vercel `maxDuration=120`, ~1,500 rows in 3 batches — the window is not theoretical), and §23.2's reconciliation "alerts, never silent fix" — it would have NAMED a player's unscored final line, not re-enqueued it. Enqueue-first makes the pair at-least-once for free: the stored row stays stale, the next poll re-detects, the PK dedupes. Pinned over the stack with a db whose `player_stats` upsert throws (queue holds 6 at 18:20 / rows still 18:00 / drained / re-poll 6 updated · 6 enqueued / rows land at 18:20); probe (order swapped back) → `expected [] to deeply equal ['syn-g1-def', …]`, reverted. **One thing the finding did not have:** enqueue-first opens the mirror-image window — a drain that reads `player_stats` between the two calls scores the OLD row, and nothing re-enqueues afterwards. Because both stamps are the one injected instant, `updated_at >= enqueued_at` is a readiness predicate the worker can test (pinned equal on a clean poll, older-than after the crash), so L.D2.2 leaves a not-ready row queued — that obligation, and the single-transaction door, are **F218**.
- **R707 · should-fix · `ingest-week.ts` — a schedule game in a week absent from `nfl_weeks` threw the WHOLE poll after the tracker recorded success, so the live week went stale with no `stats_degraded` banner (the E45 failure mode) — TAKEN: the integrity throw is kept ONLY for the week being ingested (and fires before the first write); every other calendar-less week is skipped, counted (`weeks.outsideCalendar`) and named in `reasons`.** Latent today (sleeper carries no kickoffs) and real at L.D3.1 (nflverse `schedules` carry weeks 19–22 with kickoffs; 039 seeds 1–18). Pinned with the D146 pair: week 18 (039's last row) maintained, week 19 (one past it) skipped / 1 counted / the reason literal, the live week's 6 rows landed and enqueued, both games stored; `io.week = 19` refuses with nothing written. Probe (poll-wide throw restored) → the pin dies on `nfl_weeks has no row for 2026 week 2`, reverted. `IngestWeeksReport` gained `outsideCalendar` (touched = updated + unchanged + outsideCalendar); the six existing `weeks` literals carry `outsideCalendar: 0`.

**The three substantive fixes were stress-tested, not accepted:**

- **R768's normalisation has no side effects and the guards keep their teeth.** Nothing echoes the client's string back (both routes return the RPC payload, which Postgres wrote lowercase — asserted at `transactions-api-db.test.ts:627`); the idempotency key is minted by `crypto.randomUUID()` (lowercase by spec) so a retrying client can never send a form that now differs; `activity-service.ts`'s `team_id`/`before_id` are deliberately NOT normalised because Postgres compares them as `uuid`, which is the rule `inseason-ids.ts`'s docblock states. Both negative controls are real: an uppercase id reused for a genuinely different drop is 409 **with P2 still rostered**, and at a different seed is 409 **with `schedule_seed` unmoved**.
- **R769's refcounted room survives the race walk.** StrictMode double-mount cannot orphan a channel — `open()` always suspends at `await supabase.auth.getSession()` before reaching `supabase.channel(...)`, and cleanup sets `disposed` + deletes the map entry first; there is no `await` between the last `if (room.disposed) return` (:161-163) and `room.channel = ch` (:168), so a release can never miss a channel the room then opens. Two leagues → two rooms (pinned :296). Doctrine holds: exactly one code-level `.channel(` (:165, `private: true`), zero `postgres_changes`, event names read out of `070_*.sql:280-292` / `:305-312` and matching `LEAGUE_CHANNEL_EVENTS` with the `{operation,table,schema,record}` envelope. `single-room-tab.test.ts`'s budget pin is **byte-untouched** by the fix round (`git diff 67add74..55601a4 -- …` empty) and still asserts an exact two-element set over a recursive non-test sweep.
- **The late-joiner `onJoin` (`use-league-channel.ts:239`) was RULED: keep it as built.** At mount the room is `'connecting'` when siblings attach, so N consumers of a fresh page cost N `onJoin` calls, one each at SUBSCRIBED — no storm. The extra invalidate fires only for a consumer attaching to an already-live room, whose cache genuinely may predate it, and the feed's consumers share one React Query key so it collapses to a single refetch. A silent attach would be CLAUDE.md's forbidden shape (inferring freshness from an absence) and would break §9.3's "never depend on having received a broadcast". No loop is possible — the join effect depends only on `leagueId`.
- **R770's composite cursor: no injection, `has_more` still measured, ties deterministic across BOTH sources.** Hostile values were run through both cursor schemas and every one was rejected (embedded `",id.gt."`, `,or(id.gt.0)`, a trailing `)`, a quote, a space). Encoding holds — supabase-js appends `or` through `URLSearchParams` so `+` is percent-encoded — and the quoted composite filter was confirmed against the live local PostgREST with a **non-UTC** offset (`…lt."2026-09-01T10:00:00.5+05:30"…` → 200). `has_more` is still the per-source `limit + 1` over-fetch measured AFTER the filter. Cross-source ties are safe: Postgres renders uuids lowercase at fixed dash offsets, so `sortKey`'s JS lexicographic compare agrees with `uuid` byte order, and the single `(T, ID)` pair is applied to both queries so a tied system post and transaction are cut on the same side. The wire fixture uses `TIE_INSTANT = '2098-06-01T12:00:00.5+00:00'` — fraction **and** offset — with an instant-only negative control.
